short_description.id: Huodou adalah makhluk legenda dari kelompok minoritas Tiongkok selatan.
short_description.en: Huodou is a legendary creature originating among southern Chinese minority groups.

long_description.id: Huodou adalah makhluk legenda dari kelompok minoritas Tiongkok selatan. Penggambarannya berupa anjing hitam besar yang mengeluarkan api dari mulut.
long_description.en: Huodou is a legendary creature originating among southern Chinese minority groups. Its portrayal is a large black dog emitting fire from its mouth.

long_description.id: Kemunculannya dianggap pertanda kebakaran dan kesialan. Kutipan Shanhaijing mengaitkan makhluk di selatan dengan kemampuan memakan api. Chiya zaman Ming menggambarkan Huodou makan dan memuntahkan api.
long_description.en: Its appearance is treated as an omen of fire and misfortune. A quoted Shanhaijing passage associates southern beings with eating fire. The Ming-period Chiya describes Huodou eating and spitting fire.

long_description.id: Bencao Gangmu mengutip Yuanhua Ji bahwa Huodou berbentuk seperti anjing dan memakan api, kotorannya kembali menjadi api, dan ia dapat membakar rumah orang. Li Shizhen menempatkannya di Nanhuang, wilayah selatan dekat Heikunlun, dan menyebut hal-hal pemakan api semacam itu wajar menurut hukum lima unsur.
long_description.en: The Bencao Gangmu quotes the Yuanhua Ji that the Huodou is shaped like a dog and eats fire, its dung turns back into fire, and it can burn people's houses. Li Shizhen places it in the southern wilderness near Black Kunlun and calls such fire-eating things ordinary under the principles of the five phases.

long_description.id: Chiya edisi yang dikutip menulis bahwa Huodou mirip anjing, memakan kotoran anjing, menyemburkan api, dan sangat tidak membawa keberuntungan, sehingga sumber-sumber berbeda tentang apa yang dimakannya.
long_description.en: The edition of the Chiya quoted here says the Huodou resembles a dog, eats dog dung, spits fire and is greatly ill-omened, so sources differ on what it eats.

description.id: Menurut kutipan Bencao Gangmu ia memakan api dan kotorannya menjadi api yang dapat membakar rumah; menurut Chiya ia menyemburkan api dan mendatangkan malapetaka.
description.en: According to the Bencao Gangmu quotation it eats fire and its dung becomes fire that can burn houses; according to the Chiya it spits fire and brings disaster.

description.id: Bencao Gangmu menyebut bangsa dan binatang pemakan api di Nanhuang; negeri bangsa itu dekat Heikunlun.
description.en: The Bencao Gangmu mentions fire-eating people and beasts in the southern wilderness; the people's country is near Black Kunlun.

statement.id: Huodou adalah makhluk legenda dari kelompok minoritas Tiongkok selatan.
statement.en: Huodou is a legendary creature originating among southern Chinese minority groups.

claims.quote: It is described as having the appearance of a large black dog that can emit flames from its mouth. Fire would break out wherever the Huodou went, so the ancients saw it as a sign of fire and often an ominous symbol. It is probably a demonized tribal symbol of southern China.

claims.quote: The "Shanhaijing" states: "There are people and beasts in the south who eat fire. Their country is near Hei Kunlun (Black Kunlun). People there can eat coals, and fire-eating beasts are also known as Calamities." The Shanhaijing also mentioned that the body of the Huodou is black.

claims.quote: It is also noted in the Chiya (赤雅) of the Ming Dynasty: "the Huodou looks like a dog, it eats fire and spits fire, it is ominous".

statement.en: The Ming-period Chiya describes Huodou eating and spitting fire.

text.en: The kapre as a folklore being is clearly recorded in 1906; its source word was used from colonial times.

cultural_context.id: Penggambaran kapre modern berakar pada prasangka rasial masa kolonial terhadap suku Negrito, sehingga sejarah namanya perlu disampaikan dengan hati-hati dan tidak disamakan dengan masyarakat adat.
cultural_context.en: Modern kapre portrayals are rooted in colonial-era racial prejudice against Negrito groups, so the history of the name must be presented carefully and not equated with Indigenous peoples.

short_description.id: Kapre adalah raksasa pohon dalam cerita rakyat Filipina, tinggi, gelap, berbulu, dan berotot, yang tinggal di dahan pohon dan mengisap cerutu besar, usil tetapi umumnya tidak jahat.
short_description.en: The kapre is a tree giant of Philippine folklore, tall, dark, hairy and muscular, living in tree branches and smoking large cigars, mischievous but generally benign.

long_description.id: Kapre adalah makhluk mitos berwujud mirip manusia yang sering digambarkan sebagai raksasa pohon: tinggi, gelap, berbulu, dan berotot. Dalam cerita rakyat Filipina, kapre tinggal di dahan pohon yang tidak berbuah dan mengisap cerutu besar, bersikap usil tetapi tidak jahat terhadap para pejalan.
long_description.en: The kapre is a mythical humanlike creature often described as a tree giant: tall, dark, hairy and muscular. In Philippine folklore, kapres dwell atop the branches of fruitless trees and smoke large cigars, behaving mischievously but benignly toward travellers.

long_description.id: Kapre dipercaya aktif pada malam hari dan tidak selalu jahat, tetapi dapat menjadi pendendam bila pohon tempat tinggalnya ditebang. Mereka suka mempermainkan orang, membuat pejalan tersesat di gunung atau hutan, bahkan membuat orang bingung di pekarangannya sendiri. Kapre yang tertarik pada seorang perempuan dapat terus mengikutinya seumur hidup. Kehadirannya dikenali dari dahan yang bergoyang tanpa angin kencang, tawa dari sosok tak terlihat, asap di puncak pohon, dan mata merah menyala, atau dari bau tembakau, nyala cerutu, abu yang jatuh, dan perasaan diawasi; kunang-kunang yang melimpah dipercaya sebagai bara cerutunya.
long_description.en: Kapres are believed to be nocturnal and not necessarily evil, but they may turn vengeful when the tree they inhabit is cut down. They play pranks, making travellers lose their way in mountains or woods, even confusing people in their own gardens. A kapre attracted to a woman may follow her throughout her life. Its presence is recognised by branches rustling without strong wind, laughter from an unseen being, smoke at a treetop and glowing red eyes, or by the smell of tobacco, the glow of a cigar, falling ash and the sense of being watched; abundant fireflies are believed to be the embers of its cigar.

long_description.id: Kapre dikatakan tinggal di pohon besar seperti akasia, mangga, bambu, dan beringin (balete), dan sering terlihat duduk di bawahnya. Ia memakai cawat bahag; menurut sebagian orang, sabuknya membuatnya tak terlihat oleh manusia, dan dalam sebagian versi ia memegang batu putih ajaib yang dapat mengabulkan permintaan. Pelukis Carlos "Botong" Francisco pada 1955 menggambarkannya sebagai raksasa berwajah buruk dan berlengan berbulu. Sebuah tesis melaporkan kapre bernama Mr. Brown yang tinggal di pohon balete tua di pintu masuk Istana Malacañang.
long_description.en: Kapres are said to dwell in big trees such as acacias, mangoes, bamboo and banyan (balete), and are often seen sitting beneath them. The kapre wears a bahag loincloth; according to some, its belt makes it unseen by humans, and in some versions it holds a magical white stone that can grant wishes. The painter Carlos "Botong" Francisco described it in 1955 as a giant with an ugly face and hairy arms. A thesis reports a kapre called Mr. Brown living in the old balete tree at the main entrance of Malacañang Palace.

long_description.id: Nama kapre berasal dari kata Arab kafir (Spanyol cafre), yang berarti orang tak beriman. Orang Spanyol memakai kata itu untuk menyebut kelompok Negrito berkulit gelap, dan penggambaran kapre modern berkembang dari penggambaran berprasangka rasial terhadap suku Negrito oleh kelompok dataran rendah yang telah dikristenkan pada masa Spanyol. Peneliti Jordan Clark menekankan bahwa masyarakat adat yang masih hidup tidak boleh disamakan dengan makhluk folklor hanya karena nama yang sama.
long_description.en: The name kapre comes from the Arabic kafir (Spanish cafre), meaning unbeliever. The Spanish used the word for dark-skinned Negrito groups, and modern portrayals of the kapre evolved from racially prejudiced depictions of Negrito tribes by Christianized lowland groups during the Spanish period. Researcher Jordan Clark stresses that living Indigenous peoples must not be confused with folklore beings just because of a shared name.

long_description.id: Catatan tertulis menunjukkan kapre yang jelas bersifat folklor pada 1906, ketika Fletcher Gardner menyebutnya monster jinak yang berukuran raksasa dan sepenuhnya hitam. Isabelo de los Reyes pada kajiannya menggambarkan Pugot Ilokano sebagai makhluk besar berkulit gelap penghuni rumah kosong, dan Jean-Paul G. Potet berpendapat nama kapre dipakai bagi sosok itu. Jordan Clark mengusulkan bahwa kapre mungkin komposit nasional yang menyerap ciri dari tradisi daerah, yang mungkin mencakup motif cerutu dari kisah Pugot; ia menyebut ini sintesis sejarahnya sendiri, bukan konsensus akademik yang mapan.
long_description.en: The record shows a clearly folkloric kapre in 1906, when Fletcher Gardner called it a benign, gigantic and perfectly black monster. Isabelo de los Reyes in his study described the Ilokano Pugot as a large dark being inhabiting abandoned houses, and Jean-Paul G. Potet argues the name Kapre was applied to that figure. Jordan Clark proposes that the kapre may be a national composite absorbing traits from regional traditions, possibly including the cigar motif from Pugot narratives; he calls this his own historical synthesis, not a settled academic consensus.

long_description.id: Sebuah abstrak jurnal menyebut kapre biasanya aktif malam hari dan omnivora, sering usil dengan menyesatkan orang dan menakuti anak-anak, tidak selalu dianggap jahat pada dasarnya, tetapi sebagian dirinya tetap menyeramkan. Dalam budaya populer, kapre muncul dalam komik Darna pada 1950-an dan dalam film Pangarap ng Puso tahun 2000.
long_description.en: A journal abstract says the kapre is typically nocturnal and omnivorous, often mischievous in leading people astray and scaring off children, not always considered inherently evil, yet partly ominous. In popular culture the kapre appears in the Darna comics of the 1950s and in the 2000 film Pangarap ng Puso.

claims.quote: A kapre is a mythical creature with a human-like appearance that is often described as a tree giant, being a tall, dark-coloured, hairy, and muscular creature. In Philippine folklore, kapres are giants that often dwell atop fruitless tree branches and smoke large cigars, behaving mischievously but benignly around nearby travelers.

statement.id: Kapre adalah makhluk mitos mirip manusia yang digambarkan sebagai raksasa pohon yang tinggi, gelap, berbulu, dan berotot; dalam cerita rakyat Filipina kapre tinggal di dahan pohon tak berbuah, mengisap cerutu besar, dan usil tetapi tidak jahat terhadap pejalan.
statement.en: The kapre is a humanlike mythical creature described as a tall, dark, hairy, muscular tree giant; in Philippine folklore kapres dwell atop fruitless tree branches, smoke large cigars and are mischievous but benign toward travellers.

statement.en: The term kapre comes from Arabic kafir (Spanish cafre), meaning a non-believer, and was later brought to the Philippines by the Spanish.

claims.quote: Kapres are believed to be nocturnal and omnivorous. They are not necessarily considered to be evil. However, they may turn vengeful when the tree that they are inhabiting is cut down.

statement.id: Kapre dipercaya aktif pada malam hari dan omnivora, tidak selalu dianggap jahat, tetapi dapat menjadi pendendam bila pohon tempat tinggalnya ditebang.
statement.en: Kapres are believed to be nocturnal and omnivorous, not necessarily considered evil, but they may turn vengeful when the tree they inhabit is cut down.

claims.quote: Kapres, also called agtà, are said to play pranks on people, frequently making travelers become disoriented and lose their way in the mountains or in the woods. They are also believed to possess the ability to confuse people, even when they are in their own familiar surroundings.

statement.id: Kapre, juga disebut agtà, suka mempermainkan orang, membuat pejalan tersesat di gunung atau hutan, dan dapat membingungkan orang bahkan di lingkungan yang sudah dikenalnya.
statement.en: Kapres, also called agtà, play pranks, making travellers lose their way in mountains or woods, and can confuse people even in familiar surroundings.

claims.quote: The leading etymological path begins with Arabic kāfir, a religious term for an unbeliever or one who rejects faith. Portuguese and Spanish adopted related forms such as cafre.

statement.id: Menurut Jordan Clark, asal kata kapre bermula dari kata Arab kāfir, istilah keagamaan untuk orang tak beriman, yang diadopsi bahasa Portugis dan Spanyol sebagai cafre.
statement.en: According to Jordan Clark, the name's leading etymology begins with Arabic kāfir, a religious term for an unbeliever, adopted by Portuguese and Spanish as cafre.

claims.quote: At the same time, living Indigenous peoples must not be confused with beings in folklore simply because a colonial or lowland account used the same name. The history of a label is not a definition of a people.
claims.locator: A Colonial Word in Philippine Folklore

statement.id: Jordan Clark menekankan bahwa masyarakat adat yang masih hidup tidak boleh disamakan dengan makhluk folklor hanya karena catatan kolonial memakai nama yang sama.
statement.en: Jordan Clark stresses that living Indigenous peoples must not be confused with folklore beings just because colonial accounts used the same name.

claims.quote: it shows a colonial human label in nineteenth-century dictionaries, a clearly folkloric Kapre in 1906, and evidence that traits associated with regional beings such as the Pugot were being compared or transferred soon afterward.

statement.id: Catatan yang ada menunjukkan label manusia masa kolonial dalam kamus abad kesembilan belas, kapre yang jelas bersifat folklor pada 1906, dan bukti bahwa ciri makhluk daerah seperti pugot kemudian dibandingkan atau dialihkan kepadanya.
statement.en: The record shows a colonial human label in 19th-century dictionaries, a clearly folkloric kapre in 1906, and traits of regional beings like the pugot being compared or transferred soon after.

claims.quote: Reports of experiencing Kapre enchantment include that of witnessing rustling tree branches, even if the wind is not strong. Some more examples would be hearing loud laughter coming from an unseen being, witnessing thick smoke from the top of a tree, seeing big red glaring eyes during night time from a tree

statement.id: Laporan tentang tanda kehadiran kapre antara lain dahan pohon yang bergoyang meski angin tidak kencang, tawa keras dari sosok yang tak terlihat, asap tebal dari puncak pohon, dan mata merah besar yang menyala di pohon pada malam hari.
statement.en: Reported signs of a kapre include rustling tree branches even when the wind is not strong, loud laughter from an unseen being, thick smoke from the top of a tree, and big red glaring eyes in a tree at night.

claims.quote: who had previous contact with the Moors, they used it to describe the indigenous Negrito ethnic groups with dark skin and features similar to Black Africans. This is also apparent in the fact that a synonym for kapre is agtà, another name for the Aeta people.

statement.id: Orang Spanyol, yang sebelumnya berhubungan dengan bangsa Moor, memakai istilah itu untuk menyebut kelompok Negrito pribumi berkulit gelap; sinonim kapre adalah agtà, nama lain bagi orang Aeta.
statement.en: The Spanish, who had earlier contact with the Moors, used the term for the dark-skinned indigenous Negrito groups; a synonym for kapre is agtà, another name for the Aeta people.

claims.quote: The modern mythical characterizations of the kapre evolved from formerly racially prejudiced portrayals of Negrito tribes by the lowland Christianized ethnic groups of the Philippines during the Spanish period.

statement.id: Penggambaran mitos kapre modern berkembang dari penggambaran yang dahulu berprasangka rasial terhadap suku Negrito oleh kelompok etnis dataran rendah yang telah dikristenkan pada masa Spanyol.
statement.en: Modern mythical characterizations of the kapre evolved from formerly racially prejudiced portrayals of Negrito tribes by the lowland Christianized ethnic groups during the Spanish period.

claims.quote: A Kapre may approach people to form a friendship or when it becomes attracted to a woman. If a Kapre befriends a human, especially because of love, the Kapre will drive them away because of his negative aura and still try to consistently follow its "love interest" throughout life.

statement.id: Kapre dapat mendekati orang untuk berteman atau ketika tertarik pada seorang perempuan; bila berteman dengan manusia, terutama karena cinta, ia mengusir orang itu dengan aura negatifnya tetapi tetap berusaha mengikuti orang yang dicintainya seumur hidup.
statement.en: A kapre may approach people to make friends or when it is attracted to a woman; if it befriends a human, especially out of love, it drives the person away with its negative aura yet keeps trying to follow its "love interest" throughout life.

claims.quote: Kapres are said to dwell in big trees like acacias, mangoes, bamboo, and banyan (known in the Philippines as balete). It is also commonly observed sitting beneath those trees.

statement.id: Kapre dikatakan tinggal di pohon besar seperti akasia, mangga, bambu, dan beringin (balete di Filipina), dan sering terlihat duduk di bawah pohon-pohon itu.
statement.en: Kapres are said to dwell in big trees such as acacias, mangoes, bamboo and banyan (balete in the Philippines), and are commonly seen sitting beneath those trees.

claims.quote: The Kapre is said to wear the indigenous Northern Philippine loincloth known as bahag, and according to some, often wears a belt which gives the kapre the ability to be unseen to humans.

statement.id: Kapre dikatakan memakai cawat bahag dari Filipina utara, dan menurut sebagian orang sering memakai sabuk yang membuatnya tak terlihat oleh manusia.
statement.en: The kapre is said to wear the northern Philippine loincloth known as bahag and, according to some, often wears a belt that lets it go unseen by humans.

claims.quote: In some versions, the kapre is supposed to hold a magical white stone, a little smaller in size than a quail egg. Should any person happen to obtain this stone, the kapre can grant wishes.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian versi kapre memegang batu putih ajaib yang sedikit lebih kecil daripada telur puyuh; siapa pun yang memperoleh batu itu dapat memperoleh pengabulan permintaan dari kapre.
statement.en: In some versions the kapre holds a magical white stone slightly smaller than a quail egg; whoever obtains the stone can have wishes granted by the kapre.

claims.quote: It is also believed that abundant fireflies in woody areas are the embers from the Kapre's lit cigars or tobacco pipe.

statement.id: Dipercaya pula bahwa kunang-kunang yang melimpah di daerah berhutan adalah bara cerutu atau pipa tembakau kapre yang menyala.
statement.en: It is also believed that abundant fireflies in wooded areas are the embers of the kapre's lit cigars or tobacco pipe.

claims.quote: In a 1955 article about the creatures of Philippine mythology, painter Carlos "Botong" Francisco described the kapre as "a giant with an ugly face and hairy arms, who dwells in lightning-scarred acacia or fruitless mango."

statement.id: Dalam artikel tahun 1955 tentang makhluk mitologi Filipina, pelukis Carlos "Botong" Francisco menggambarkan kapre sebagai raksasa berwajah buruk dan berlengan berbulu yang tinggal di pohon akasia bekas tersambar petir atau mangga yang tak berbuah.
statement.en: In a 1955 article about the creatures of Philippine mythology, the painter Carlos "Botong" Francisco described the kapre as a giant with an ugly face and hairy arms who dwells in a lightning-scarred acacia or a fruitless mango.

claims.quote: In the 1950s, among the earliest issues of the Darna superhero comics by Mars Ravelo and Nestor Redondo featured a kapre being fought by the titular superhero.

statement.id: Pada 1950-an, di antara terbitan paling awal komik pahlawan super Darna karya Mars Ravelo dan Nestor Redondo, tampil seekor kapre yang dilawan sang pahlawan.
statement.en: In the 1950s, among the earliest issues of the Darna superhero comics by Mars Ravelo and Nestor Redondo, a kapre was featured being fought by the title hero.

claims.quote: In the 2000 romantic drama film Pangarap ng Puso directed by Mario O'Hara, a kapre appears sporadically in the film amidst scenes of political turmoil.

statement.id: Dalam film drama romantis tahun 2000 Pangarap ng Puso karya sutradara Mario O'Hara, seekor kapre sesekali muncul di tengah adegan gejolak politik.
statement.en: In the 2000 romantic drama film Pangarap ng Puso directed by Mario O'Hara, a kapre appears sporadically amid scenes of political turmoil.

claims.quote: It is generally depicted as a tall, hairy giant sitting in trees and smoking a large cigar or tabako. It is typically nocturnal and omnivorous.

statement.id: Abstrak jurnal menyebut kapre umumnya digambarkan sebagai raksasa tinggi berbulu yang duduk di pohon dan mengisap cerutu besar atau tabako, serta biasanya aktif malam hari dan omnivora.
statement.en: The journal abstract says the kapre is generally depicted as a tall, hairy giant sitting in trees and smoking a large cigar or tabako, and is typically nocturnal and omnivorous.

claims.quote: While often mischievous (leading people astray and scaring off children), it is not always considered inherently evil; however, a part of it is ominous and sinister.

statement.id: Abstrak yang sama menyatakan kapre sering usil (menyesatkan orang dan menakuti anak-anak), tidak selalu dianggap jahat pada dasarnya, tetapi sebagian dirinya tetap mengancam dan menyeramkan.
statement.en: The same abstract says the kapre is often mischievous (leading people astray and scaring off children) and not always considered inherently evil, yet part of it is ominous and sinister.

claims.quote: The most well-known Kapre in the Philippines is Mr. Brown, who is reported to reside in the 100-year-old balete tree at the main entrance of Malacañang Palace
claims.locator: Kapre's home near Malacañang "Old Balete Tree"

statement.id: Menurut tesis ini, kapre paling terkenal di Filipina adalah Mr. Brown, yang dilaporkan tinggal di pohon balete berumur 100 tahun di pintu masuk utama Istana Malacañang.
statement.en: According to this thesis, the best-known kapre in the Philippines is Mr. Brown, reported to live in the 100-year-old balete tree at the main entrance of Malacañang Palace.

claims.quote: The personnel sometimes refer to Mr. Brown as Mr. Jones and view him as a kind but harmless prankster.
claims.locator: Kapre's home near Malacañang "Old Balete Tree"

statement.id: Pegawai kadang menyebut Mr. Brown sebagai Mr. Jones dan memandangnya sebagai pengusil yang baik tetapi tidak berbahaya.
statement.en: Staff sometimes call Mr. Brown "Mr. Jones" and regard him as a kind but harmless prankster.

claims.quote: Fletcher Gardner, 1906 Fletcher Gardner was an American teacher and collector who published Tagalog material from Mindoro in the Journal of American Folklore. ... Another monster, but a benign one, is the kapre. It is gigantic in size … and is perfectly black.

statement.id: Fletcher Gardner, guru dan kolektor Amerika yang menerbitkan bahan Tagalog dari Mindoro dalam Journal of American Folklore, pada 1906 menyebut kapre sebagai monster yang jinak, berukuran raksasa, dan sepenuhnya hitam.
statement.en: Fletcher Gardner, an American teacher and collector who published Tagalog material from Mindoro in the Journal of American Folklore, described the kapre in 1906 as a benign monster, gigantic in size and perfectly black.

claims.quote: Isabelo de los Reyes and the Pugot, 1909 Isabelo de los Reyes was an Ilokano writer, folklorist, and political figure whose study described a large dark Pugot believed to inhabit abandoned houses

statement.id: Isabelo de los Reyes, penulis dan ahli cerita rakyat Ilokano, pada 1909 dalam kajiannya menggambarkan Pugot sebagai makhluk besar berkulit gelap yang dipercaya menghuni rumah-rumah kosong.
statement.en: Isabelo de los Reyes, an Ilokano writer and folklorist, described in his 1909 study a large dark Pugot believed to inhabit abandoned houses.

claims.quote: Jean-Paul G. Potet, a linguist and historian of Tagalog language and culture, argues in Ancient Beliefs and Customs of the Tagalogs that nineteenth-century Tagalog usage applied Kapre to this Ilokano figure. Whether the transfer occurred exactly as Potet proposes remains open to testing

statement.id: Jean-Paul G. Potet berpendapat bahwa pemakaian bahasa Tagalog abad kesembilan belas menerapkan nama kapre pada sosok Ilokano ini; apakah peralihan itu terjadi persis seperti usulnya masih terbuka untuk diuji.
statement.en: Jean-Paul G. Potet argues that nineteenth-century Tagalog usage applied the name Kapre to this Ilokano figure; whether the transfer occurred exactly as he proposes remains open to testing.

claims.quote: The Kapre may not be one ancient figure that spread unchanged across the country. It may be a later national composite formed when a widely understood name absorbed characteristics from regional traditions. This is my historical synthesis, not a settled academic consensus.

statement.id: Penulis laman ini mengusulkan bahwa kapre mungkin bukan satu sosok kuno yang menyebar tanpa berubah, melainkan komposit nasional yang kemudian terbentuk ketika nama yang dikenal luas menyerap ciri dari tradisi daerah; ia menyebutnya sintesis sejarahnya sendiri, bukan konsensus akademik yang mapan.
statement.en: The page's author proposes that the Kapre may not be one ancient figure that spread unchanged, but a later national composite formed when a widely understood name absorbed traits from regional traditions; he calls this his own historical synthesis, not a settled academic consensus.

claims.quote: Northern accounts of the Ilokano Pugot include a large, dark, tree-associated being with cigar imagery. The motif may have circulated from older Pugot narratives into the nationally standardized Kapre.
claims.locator: Why Does the Kapre Smoke a Cigar?

statement.id: Catatan utara tentang Pugot Ilokano memuat makhluk besar, gelap, terkait pohon, dengan citra cerutu; motif itu mungkin beredar dari kisah Pugot yang lebih tua ke kapre yang dibakukan secara nasional.
statement.en: Northern accounts of the Ilokano Pugot include a large, dark, tree-associated being with cigar imagery; the motif may have passed from older Pugot narratives into the nationally standardized Kapre.

claims.quote: In popular accounts, the Kapre is a giant humanlike being that inhabits a large tree, often a balete, acacia, or mango. It may be detected through the smell of tobacco, the glow of a cigar, laughter, falling ash, or the sense of being watched.

statement.id: Dalam kisah populer kapre adalah makhluk raksasa mirip manusia yang tinggal di pohon besar, sering balete, akasia, atau mangga; kehadirannya dapat dikenali dari bau tembakau, nyala cerutu, tawa, abu yang jatuh, atau perasaan sedang diawasi.
statement.en: In popular accounts the kapre is a giant humanlike being living in a large tree, often a balete, acacia or mango; it may be detected by the smell of tobacco, the glow of a cigar, laughter, falling ash or the sense of being watched.

claims.quote: Eastern Visayan narratives also describe an Agta associated with trees, forests, great size, and dark appearance.

statement.id: Kisah-kisah Visayas Timur juga menggambarkan Agta yang terkait dengan pohon, hutan, ukuran besar, dan penampilan gelap.
statement.en: Eastern Visayan narratives also describe an Agta associated with trees, forests, great size and dark appearance.

claims.quote: The Eastern Visayan figure is not automatically a subtype of Kapre.

statement.id: Penulis laman ini menyatakan sosok Visayas Timur itu tidak otomatis merupakan subtipe kapre.
statement.en: The page's author states that the Eastern Visayan figure is not automatically a subtype of Kapre.

short_description.id: Kasogonagá adalah dewi cuaca suku Toba yang digambarkan sebagai hewan berwarna-warni dengan mulut pemancar petir, terkait hujan dan guntur.
short_description.en: Kasogonagá is a Toba weather goddess described as a colorful animal with a mouth that shoots lightning, associated with rain and thunder.

long_description.id: Kasogonagá, juga dieja Gasogonaga atau Qasoxonaxa, adalah dewi cuaca suku Toba. Ia menampakkan diri kepada dukun (pio’oxonak) dalam penglihatan yang dipicu tumbuhan psikoaktif, dan digambarkan sebagai hewan berwarna-warni dengan mulut yang memancarkan petir.
long_description.en: Kasogonagá, also spelled Gasogonaga or Qasoxonaxa, is a Toba weather goddess. Shamans, called pio’oxonak, see her in visions brought on by psychoactive plants, and she is pictured as a brightly colored animal whose mouth shoots lightning.

long_description.id: Wujud hewannya berbeda-beda. Sebagian orang Toba menggambarkannya sebagai gajah berwarna-warni yang melontarkan petir, yang dikaitkan dengan hujan dan pelangi; ada pula yang menyebutnya beruang semut yang hidup di langit, atau kadang seekor babi. Dalam penuturan yang dicatat Terán ia hewan kecil berkaki empat sekaligus pemilik petir. Artikel Sarra menyebut bahwa beragam deskripsi itu mungkin berasal dari logika metamorfik dalam pandangan qom tentang pribadi dan tubuh.
long_description.en: Her animal form varies. Some Toba people describe her as a multicolored elephant that throws lightning, linked to rain and rainbows; others call her an anteater living in the sky, or sometimes a pig. In an account recorded by Terán she is a small four-legged animal and the owner of the lightning. Sarra's article says the differing descriptions may stem from the metamorphic logic of the qom conception of person and body.

long_description.id: Dalam satu kisah, Kasogonagá jatuh dari awannya dan meminta bantuan seorang pria untuk kembali ke langit dengan menunggangi asap api unggun. Sebagai tanda terima kasih ia menurunkan hujan dan berkata bahwa pria itu boleh meminta apa pun yang ia perlukan. Dalam versi lain yang diceritakan orang Toba, ia berwujud babi kecil yang jatuh dari awan. Secara ringkas, dalam kisah-kisah itu makhluk ini tinggal di langit, sewaktu-waktu dapat jatuh ke bumi, lalu memerlukan bantuan manusia untuk kembali.
long_description.en: In one story Kasogonagá has fallen from her cloud and asks a man to help her back to the sky by riding the smoke of a bonfire. In gratitude she makes it rain and says the man can ask for anything he needs. In another version told by the Toba she is a small pig that has fallen from a cloud. In brief, in these accounts the being lives in the sky, can occasionally fall to the earth, and then needs human help to return.

long_description.id: Makhluk ini dikaitkan dengan hujan, guntur, dan kilat; sebagai pemilik gejala cuaca itu, qasoxonaxa dapat menolong manusia ketika kemarau dan banjir, dan sebagai balasan atas bantuan manusia ia menawarkan pertolongan. Di lingkungan qom di Derqui ia dibayangkan sebagai gajah langit yang tinggal di atas awan; seorang anak di sana mengatakan bahwa neneknya, sang gajah di langit, menyembuhkan kutil.
long_description.en: The being is associated with rain, thunder and lightning; as owner of these phenomena qasoxonaxa can help people in droughts and floods, and in return for human help it offers assistance. In the qom neighbourhood of Derqui it is imagined as a sky elephant living above the clouds; a girl there said her grandmother, the elephant in the sky, cures warts.

statement.en: Kasogonagá is also described as an anteater that lives in the sky, and sometimes she is said to be a pig.

claims.quote: She asked the man to build a bonfire so that she could ride the smoke and return to the sky. The man did as she asked, and placed her on top of the bonfire. In her gratitude, she made it rain, and told the man that if he needed anything, he could just ask her.

statement.id: Dalam satu mitos, Kasogonagá meminta seorang pria membuat api unggun agar ia dapat menunggangi asapnya kembali ke langit; sebagai tanda terima kasih ia menurunkan hujan dan berkata kepada pria itu bahwa ia boleh meminta apa pun.
statement.en: In one myth Kasogonagá asks a man to build a bonfire so that she can ride its smoke back to the sky; in gratitude she makes it rain and tells the man he can ask her for anything he needs.

claims.quote: Kasogonaga es el rayo, pero también es un animalito. Toma la forma de un animalito de cuatro patas. Es el dueño del rayo.
claims.locator: Relato registrado por Terán entre los qom occidentales

statement.id: Dalam penuturan yang dicatat Terán, Kasogonaga adalah petir sekaligus hewan kecil; ia berwujud hewan kecil berkaki empat dan pemilik petir.
statement.en: In an account recorded by Terán, Kasogonaga is the lightning but also a small animal; it takes the form of a four-legged little animal and is the owner of the lightning.

claims.quote: Los Toba dicen que un día un hombre estaba afuera en el monte y escuchó alguien que lo llamaba. Miró quién era y allí estaba Kasogonaga bajo la forma de un pequeño cerdo que se había caído de una nube.
claims.locator: Relato de Terán, en Wilbert y Simoneau (1975)

statement.id: Orang Toba menuturkan bahwa seorang pria di hutan mendengar panggilan dan mendapati Kasogonaga berwujud babi kecil yang jatuh dari awan.
statement.en: The Toba say that a man in the bush heard someone calling him and found Kasogonaga in the form of a small pig that had fallen from a cloud.

claims.quote: En ellos, se observa también una asociación entre dicho ser celestial y la lluvia, los truenos y relámpagos; como dueño de tales fenómenos atmosféricos, qasoxonaxa puede ayudar a los seres humanos ante situaciones de sequía e inundaciones.

statement.id: Dalam kisah-kisah itu, makhluk langit tersebut dikaitkan dengan hujan, guntur, dan kilat; sebagai pemilik gejala cuaca itu, qasoxonaxa dapat menolong manusia ketika kemarau dan banjir.
statement.en: In those accounts this celestial being is associated with rain, thunder and lightning; as owner of these atmospheric phenomena, qasoxonaxa can help people in droughts and floods.

claims.quote: En los relatos, situaciones fragmentarias y dibujos que registré en el barrio qom de Derqui, dicho ser es conceptualizado como un elefante del cielo, como un pequeño animalito o como un oso hormiguero, dueño o dueña de la lluvia y los truenos, que habita en el cielo sobre las nubes

statement.id: Dalam catatan Sarra di lingkungan qom di Derqui, makhluk ini dibayangkan sebagai gajah langit, hewan kecil, atau beruang semut, pemilik atau penguasa hujan dan guntur yang tinggal di langit di atas awan.
statement.en: In Sarra's records from the qom neighbourhood of Derqui, the being is conceived as a sky elephant, a small animal or an anteater, owner of rain and thunder, that lives in the sky above the clouds.

claims.quote: Las diversas descripciones pueden deberse a la lógica metamórfica de la concepción qom de la persona y el cuerpo, que permite diferentes estados de un mismo ser

statement.id: Beragam deskripsi itu mungkin disebabkan oleh logika metamorfik dalam pandangan qom tentang pribadi dan tubuh, yang mengizinkan beberapa keadaan bagi satu makhluk yang sama.
statement.en: The differing descriptions may be due to the metamorphic logic of the qom conception of person and body, which allows different states of one and the same being.

claims.quote: Sintéticamente, en dichos relatos se describe que dicho ser tiene su morada en los cielos pero eventualmente puede caer al plano terrestre, y entonces necesita de la ayuda de los seres humanos para regresar.

statement.id: Secara ringkas, dalam kisah-kisah itu makhluk ini bertempat tinggal di langit tetapi sewaktu-waktu dapat jatuh ke bumi, lalu memerlukan bantuan manusia untuk kembali.
statement.en: In brief, in those accounts the being has its dwelling in the heavens but can occasionally fall to the earth, and then needs human help to return.

claims.quote: éstos lo ayudaron a subir al cielo mediante la construcción de un gran fuego; a cambio, qasoxonaxa les ofrecerá ayuda ante sequías o inundaciones

statement.id: Dalam dua kisah pertama, manusia menolongnya naik ke langit dengan membuat api besar; sebagai balasan, qasoxonaxa akan menolong mereka ketika kemarau atau banjir.
statement.en: In the first two accounts people helped it up to the sky by building a large fire; in return qasoxonaxa will help them in droughts or floods.

claims.quote: mi abuela que es un elefante que está en el cielo cura verrugas ... cuando llueve hay que sacar la mano para que el contacto con el agua de la lluvia, junto con los rezos correspondientes, haga su efecto.

statement.id: Seorang anak di Derqui berkata kepada Sarra bahwa neneknya, seekor gajah di langit, menyembuhkan kutil, dan bahwa saat hujan tangan harus dijulurkan agar air hujan bersama doa-doa yang sesuai bekerja.
statement.en: A girl in Derqui told Sarra that her grandmother, an elephant in the sky, cures warts, and that when it rains one must put out a hand so that the rain water, together with the appropriate prayers, takes effect.

claims.quote: La montaña qasoxonaxa se sitúa al oeste

statement.id: Gunung qasoxonaxa terletak di barat.
statement.en: The mountain qasoxonaxa is situated in the west.

short_description.id: Manaia adalah makhluk mitologi berwujud hibrida burung, manusia, dan ikan yang menjadi simbol pelindung dalam kebudayaan Māori.
short_description.en: The Manaia is a mythological creature in Māori culture combining bird, human, and fish traits as a guardian against evil.

long_description.id: Manaia adalah entitas mitologis dalam kebudayaan Māori yang sangat umum ditemukan sebagai motif ukiran kayu dan perhiasan tradisional. Wujudnya biasa dilukiskan memiliki kepala burung, tubuh manusia, dan ekor ikan, meskipun kadang hadir menyerupai burung, ular, atau sosok tampak samping.
long_description.en: The Manaia is a mythological being in Māori culture frequently appearing as a central motif in wood carvings and jewellery. It is usually depicted with the head of a bird, human body, and fish tail, though alternatively rendered as a serpent or profile figure.

long_description.id: Secara tradisional, Manaia dipercaya sebagai utusan antara alam fana manusia dan alam roh, serta berfungsi sebagai penjaga terhadap marabahaya jahat. Sosoknya lazim digambarkan berbentuk angka delapan dengan tiga jari tangan yang melambangkan siklus kelahiran, kehidupan, dan kematian, serta ditemukan pada kebudayaan Polynesian lainnya seperti di Hawaii.
long_description.en: Traditionally held as a messenger between mortals and the spirit realm, the Manaia serves as a guardian against evil. Often represented in a figure-of-eight form with three fingers symbolizing birth, life, and death, related motifs also exist in other Polynesian cultures such as Hawaii.

long_description.id: Catatan lama tentang seni Māori menggambarkan manaia dengan cara yang berbeda-beda. Hamilton menyebutnya bentuk kadal atau ular dengan beberapa varian, termasuk ular berkepala elang, dan menduga manaia mungkin dianggap gambaran kadal; ia juga mencatat bahwa di Samoa manaia adalah nama seekor kadal. Pada sebuah papan lumbung berukir, figur manusia berselang-seling dengan manaia berkepala burung, dan sebuah ukiran tulang atau batu hijau yang mungkin menggambarkan ikan kuda laut disebut manaia.
long_description.en: Older writing on Māori art describes the manaia in differing ways. Hamilton calls it a lizard or snake form with several varieties, including a snake with an eagle's head, and suggests manaias may have been considered representations of lizards; he also notes that in Samoa manaia is the name of a lizard. On a carved storehouse board, human figures alternate with bird-headed manaias, and a bone or greenstone carving that probably represents the seahorse fish is called a manaia.

claims.quote: In this form, it is usually represented in a figure-of-eight shape, the upper half culminating in a bird-like beak.

short_description.id: Many-finned sea serpent adalah kriptid laut yang dikabarkan memiliki banyak sirip.
short_description.en: The many-finned sea serpent is an alleged marine cryptid with numerous fins.

long_description.id: Many-finned sea serpent adalah kriptid laut yang dikabarkan memiliki banyak sirip. Aelian mencatat makhluk pesisir sebanding yang disebut scolopendra.
long_description.en: The many-finned sea serpent is an alleged marine cryptid with numerous fins. Aelian reports a comparable coastal creature called scolopendra.

long_description.id: Catatan kuno itu memberinya ekor menyerupai lobster dan hidung besar berbulu. Bernard Heuvelmans menggolongkannya sebagai ular laut bersirip banyak.
long_description.en: That ancient report gives it a lobster-like tail and a large hairy nose. Bernard Heuvelmans classifies it as a many-finned sea serpent.

long_description.id: Aelian dalam karyanya tentang hewan menulis bahwa skolopendra adalah sejenis ketos dan yang terbesar di antara monster laut. Menurut mereka yang ahli urusan laut, kepalanya menyembul di atas laut dengan rambut sangat panjang pada lubang hidungnya, ekornya pipih seperti ekor udang karang, dan ia berenang dengan banyak kaki berderet di kedua sisi.
long_description.en: Aelian, in his work on animals, writes that the skolopendra is a ketos and the biggest of the sea-monsters. According to those expert in marine matters, its head rises above the sea with hairs of immense length at its nostrils, its tail is flat like a crayfish's, and it swims with numerous feet in line on either side.

long_description.id: Sebuah epigram dalam Greek Anthology menceritakan jasad skolopendra sepanjang delapan depa yang ditemukan nelayan Hermonax di pantai berpasir. Laporan tahun 1899 tentang kapal perang Narcissus menyebut "monster laut" bersirip tak terhitung yang panjangnya diukur sekitar 45 meter.
long_description.en: A Greek Anthology epigram tells of the body of a scolopendra eight fathoms long found by the fisherman Hermonax on a sandy beach. A 1899 report about the warship Narcissus mentions a "sea monster" with countless fins measured at about 45 meters.

short_description.id: Nāmaka adalah dewi laut dalam keluarga Pele dalam mitologi Hawaii; ia kakak perempuan Pele dan musuh terpahitnya, yang melawan Pele dengan pasang laut dan banjir.
short_description.en: Nāmaka is a sea goddess of the Pele family in Hawaiian mythology; she is Pele's older sister and bitterest enemy, who fought her with tidal waves and floods.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Hawaii, Nāmaka (atau Nā-maka-o-Kahaʻi, "mata Kahaʻi") tampil sebagai dewi laut dalam keluarga Pele. Ia kakak perempuan Pele-honua-mea dan putri Ku-waha-ilo dan Haumea, yang anak-anak lainnya adalah Pele, saudari-saudari Hiʻiaka, saudara-saudara Kama, dan burung Halulu. Menurut satu sumber, Na-maka-o-ka-hai dan Pele lahir dari Haumea, dan versi lain menyebut Pele lahir dari kepala dan Nāmaka dari paha Haumea.
long_description.en: Nāmaka (also Nā-maka-o-Kahaʻi, "the eyes of Kahaʻi") is a sea goddess of the Pele family in Hawaiian mythology. She is the elder sister of Pele-honua-mea and a daughter of Ku-waha-ilo and Haumea; her siblings include Pele, the Hiʻiaka sisters, the Kama brothers and the bird Halulu. One source says Na-maka-o-ka-hai and Pele were born of Haumea, and another version has Pele born from the head and Nāmaka from the thighs of Haumea.

long_description.id: Menurut satu kisah, Na-maka-o-ka-hai karena perselisihan keluarga menjadi musuh terpahit Pele dan melawannya dengan banjir air, sehingga keluarga itu mewakili dua musuh abadi, api dan air. Ketika Pele bertengkar dengannya, Nāmaka mengirim gelombang pasang untuk menghancurkan tanah dan rumah Pele; ia mengalahkan Pele dan keluarganya, merobohkan rumah mereka dan mengusir mereka ke samudra.
long_description.en: According to one account, Na-maka-o-ka-hai became Pele's most bitter enemy as a result of family trouble and fought her with floods of water, so that the household represented the two eternal enemies, fire and water. When Pele quarrelled with her, Nāmaka sent tidal waves to destroy Pele's lands and homes; she defeated Pele and her family, broke down their houses and drove them into the ocean.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah itu, kedua saudari bertarung tangan kosong lama di lereng barat gunung Hale-a-ka-la, dan Na-maka-o-ka-hai mencabik tubuh Pele serta mematahkan tulang lavanya menjadi bongkahan besar yang hingga kini terletak di pesisir. Ia lalu menuju Nuu-mea-lani, negeri leluhur mitos yang tertinggi, gembira atas kehancuran musuhnya, tetapi tahu tidak akan pernah lagi dapat mengalahkan roh Pele, dewi api. Nāmaka juga mengusir Pele ketika Pele menyebabkan kebakaran besar karena terlalu dekat dengan dewa api Lono-makua.
long_description.en: In that account the sisters grappled for a long time on the western slope of the mountain Hale-a-ka-la, where Na-maka-o-ka-hai tore Pele's body and broke her lava bones into great pieces that still lie along the seacoast. She then went toward Nuu-mea-lani, the highest of the mythical ancestral lands, rejoicing at her enemy's ruin yet aware that she could not again defeat the spirit of Pele, goddess of fire. Nāmaka also chases Pele off after Pele sets off a blaze by lingering too near the fire god Lono-makua.

long_description.id: Seorang penyihir yang lebih besar, Au-kele-nui-a-iku, menikahi Na-maka-o-ka-hai, lalu melihat Pele dan adik bungsunya yang cantik, Hiiaka, dan diam-diam mengambil mereka sebagai istri. Dalam mitos Kane-huna-moku dari Thrum, Nāmaka disebut kepala perempuan orang Mu dan Menehune, dan nama Namaka kini juga dipakai untuk bulan kecil planet kerdil Haumea, sedangkan bulan lainnya dinamai menurut saudarinya, Hiʻiaka.
long_description.en: A greater sorcerer, Au-kele-nui-a-iku, married Na-maka-o-ka-hai, then saw Pele and her beautiful young sister Hiiaka and secretly took them to be his wives. Thrum's Kane-huna-moku myth names Nāmaka chiefess of the Mu and Menehune peoples, and the name Namaka is now also given to the smaller moon of the dwarf planet Haumea, whose other moon is called after her sister Hiʻiaka.

short_description.id: Anjing Bertelinga Sembilan berasal dari mitologi Semenanjung Leizhou.
short_description.en: The Nine-Eared Hound belongs to the mythology of the Leizhou Peninsula.

long_description.id: Anjing Bertelinga Sembilan berasal dari mitologi Semenanjung Leizhou. Versi awal yang bertahan dalam Taiping Guangji menyebut dua belas telinga.
long_description.en: The Nine-Eared Hound belongs to the mythology of the Leizhou Peninsula. The earliest surviving version in Taiping Guangji gives the hound twelve ears.

long_description.id: Yuan Mei menempatkan salah satu versi kisahnya dalam bab 12 What the Master Would Not Discuss. Anjing milik pemburu bermarga Chen ini meramalkan jumlah buruan melalui telinganya yang bergerak. Anjing tersebut membawa Chen kepada telur besar yang kemudian menetas menjadi bayi ketika terjadi badai. Dalam versi lain, bayi itu bernama Chen Wenyu, yang dikaitkan dengan Dewa Guntur di Leizhou.
long_description.en: Yuan Mei includes one version in chapter 12 of What the Master Would Not Discuss. The dog belongs to a hunter named Chen and predicts the number of prey through its quivering ears. The dog leads Chen to a large egg that later opens during a thunderstorm to reveal a baby. In another version the child is named Chen Wenyu, associated with the God of Thunder in Leizhou.

long_description.id: Teks-teks lama merekam kisah ini dengan jumlah telinga berbeda. Taiping Guangji menyebut anjing pemburu berdua belas telinga yang gerak telinganya dibaca sebagai jumlah buruan, dan pada suatu hari seluruh telinganya bergerak lalu ia menggonggong di tepi laut; telur-telur yang dibawa pulang kemudian pecah setelah badai dan cangkangnya dibagi serta dipuja penduduk. Guangdong Xinyu menyebut anjing bertelinga sembilan milik Chen Kun yang mengitari semak berduri hingga ditemukan telur besar; dari telur itu keluar seorang laki-laki dengan aksara pada tangannya.
long_description.en: Older Chinese texts record the tale with different numbers of ears. The Taiping Guangji describes a hunting dog with twelve ears whose moving ears were read as the number of prey; one day all its ears moved and it howled by the sea; the eggs brought home later broke open after a storm, and the shells were divided and revered by the people. The Guangdong Xinyu describes Chen Kun's nine-eared dog, which circled a thicket until a huge egg was found, from which came a boy with characters on his hands.

statement.id: Taiping Guangji mencatat seorang penduduk daerah Lei yang memelihara anjing pemburu berdua belas telinga; sebelum berburu, jumlah telinga yang bergerak dibaca sebagai jumlah buruan.
statement.en: The Taiping Guangji records a man of the Lei region who kept a hunting dog with twelve ears; before a hunt, the number of ears that moved was taken as the number of animals to be caught.

claims.quote: 以耳動為獲數。 ... 一日，諸耳畢動。既獵，不復逐獸。至海旁測中嗥鳴。郡人視之

statement.en: In this version the eggs brought home broke open after a storm and left their shells; the people of the commandery divided the shells and made offerings to them at set times, and holding a shell marked a prominent clan.

statement.id: Guangdong Xinyu menulis bahwa Chen Kun dari Leizhou, yang tidak punya anak dan berprofesi pemburu, memiliki anjing bertelinga sembilan yang sangat sakti; satu telinga yang bergerak berarti satu buruan.
statement.en: The Guangdong Xinyu says that Chen Kun of Leizhou, who had no son and made his living by hunting, kept a very efficacious nine-eared dog; each ear that moved meant one animal caught.

claims.quote: 一日出獵，而九耳俱動，鉷大喜，以為必多得獸矣。既之野，有叢棘一區，九耳犬圍繞不去。異之，得一巨卵徑尺，攜以歸，雷雨暴作，卵開，乃一男子，其手有文，左曰雷，右曰州

statement.id: Pada suatu hari kesembilan telinga bergerak dan anjing itu terus mengitari semak berduri; Chen Kun menemukan telur besar, membawanya pulang, dan ketika badai petir datang telur itu terbuka menjadi seorang laki-laki yang di telapak tangannya tertulis aksara untuk Lei dan Zhou.
statement.en: One day all nine ears moved and the dog kept circling a thicket; Chen Kun found a huge egg and took it home, and in a thunderstorm it opened to reveal a boy with the characters for Lei and Zhou written on his hands.

short_description.id: Nure-onna adalah yōkai Jepang yang berkepala perempuan dan bertubuh ular, dikaitkan dengan laut dan sungai.
short_description.en: Nure-onna is a Japanese yōkai with a woman's head and a snake's body, associated with seas and rivers.

long_description.id: Nure-onna (濡女, "perempuan basah") adalah yōkai Jepang yang menyerupai makhluk reptil berkepala perempuan dan bertubuh ular. Di laut, fenomena ini juga disebut nureyomejo. Dalam legenda ia sering dikatakan memakan manusia, tetapi tidak punya satu rupa atau watak yang baku.
long_description.en: Nure-onna (濡女, "wet woman") is a Japanese yōkai a reptile-like being with a woman's head atop a snake's body. At sea it is also seen as a phenomenon under the name nureyomejo. In legends it is often said to consume humans, but it has no single appearance or personality.

long_description.id: Seperti isoonna, nure-onna disebut muncul di laut atau sungai. Menurut Yokai.com, ia paling sering dijumpai di pesisir Kyūshū, dengan cerita perjumpaan hingga Prefektur Niigata dan Prefektur Fukushima. Namanya berasal dari rambutnya yang selalu basah dalam legenda. Banyak buku zaman Edo menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan bertubuh ular, walau cerita klasik tentang bentuk itu tidak ditemukan.
long_description.en: Like the isoonna, the nure-onna is said to appear at seas or rivers. According to Yokai.com it is most commonly found on the shores of Kyūshū, with stories of encounters as far as Niigata Prefecture and Fukushima Prefecture. Its name comes from how its hair is always wet in legends. Many Edo period publications depict it as a woman with a snake body, though no classical stories of that form can be found.

long_description.id: Yokai.com menyebut dua ragam: yang tanpa lengan menyerupai ular laut raksasa berkepala perempuan, dan yang berlengan seperti manusia. Wajahnya buruk rupa dengan ciri ular seperti lidah bercabang, dan rambut hitamnya yang panjang menempel pada tubuhnya yang basah menetes.
long_description.en: Yokai.com describes two variations: one lacking arms that looks like a giant sea serpent whose head is a woman's, and one that has arms like a human's. Its face is hideous with serpent-like features such as a forked tongue, and long black hair sticks to its dripping body.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Yokai.com, nure onna menyamar secara gaib sebagai perempuan malang yang menggendong bayi terbungkus dan meminta tolong kepada nelayan atau pelaut yang lewat. Ia memohon agar korban menggendong bayinya sebentar; jika korban setuju, "bayi" menjadi seberat batu besar dan korban tak bisa bergerak. Nure onna lalu menghisap darah korban dengan lidahnya yang panjang. Ia disebut sering muncul bersama dan bekerja sama dengan ushi oni.
long_description.en: In the account recorded by Yokai.com, a nure onna magically disguises itself as a distressed woman carrying a bundled baby and cries out for help from passing fishers or sailors. She pleads with the victim to hold her baby for a moment; if he agrees, the "baby" becomes as heavy as a boulder and the victim cannot move. The nure onna then drains his blood with her long tongue. It is said to frequently appear together and cooperate with ushi oni.

short_description.id: Ōseichū adalah penyakit aneh sekaligus serangga ajaib dalam kisah Tiongkok dan Jepang: sesuatu di dalam perut menjawab dan menirukan ucapan penderitanya.
short_description.en: The Ōseichū is a strange illness and the strange insect behind it in Chinese and Japanese tales: something inside the belly answers and mimics what the sufferer says.

long_description.id: Ōseichū (応声虫) atau Ōsei adalah penyakit aneh yang tercatat dalam kumpulan kisah dan esai Tiongkok dan Jepang, sekaligus serangga ajaib penyebabnya. Dalam kisah Tiongkok, setelah serangga itu masuk ke tubuh, dari dalam perut terdengar jawaban atas pertanyaan padahal penderitanya tidak berbicara. Dalam Chaoye Qianzai, seorang terpelajar dari Luozhou mengalami suara dari tenggorokan yang menjawab ucapannya dan disembuhkan dengan pil dari obat yang ditakuti suara itu.
long_description.en: The Ōseichū (応声虫), or Ōsei, is a strange illness found in Chinese and Japanese story collections and essays, and also the strange insect that causes it. In Chinese accounts, once the insect enters the body, replies to questions come from the belly although the person is not speaking. In the Chaoye Qianzai, a scholar of Luozhou has a voice in his throat that answers his speech and is cured with pills made from the drug the voice feared.

long_description.id: Di Jepang penyakit ini dianggap berasal dari serangga ajaib yang hidup dalam tubuh seperti cacing gelang. Penderita demam tinggi sekitar sepuluh hari, lalu perutnya muncul bisul yang lama-kelamaan berbentuk mulut yang menirukan ucapan si sakit, dan karena itulah ia dinamai Ōseichū. Mulut itu juga makan dan menuntut makanan, dan jika ditolak ia menyiksa penderita dengan demam tinggi atau memaki dengan keras.
long_description.en: In Japan the illness was regarded as coming from a strange insect living inside the body like a roundworm. The sufferer has a high fever for about ten days, then a boil appears on the belly and gradually takes the shape of a mouth that mimics what the sick person says, which is why it is called Ōseichū. The mouth also eats and demands food, and if refused it torments the patient with a high fever or shouts abuse.

long_description.id: Ringkasan basis data Nichibunken atas Shiojiri menceritakan putra seorang perajin di ibu kota pada tahun Genroku 16 yang demam lalu bersuara dari perutnya; setelah obat dan doa gagal, dokter 菅玄際 menyimpulkan penyakit itu ulah Ōseichū dan memberinya ramuan raigan (雷丸), suara itu lenyap, dan seekor serangga berbentuk kadal dengan tanduk kecil keluar dari anusnya. Ringkasan atas Kanden jihitsu menceritakan istri seorang petani di Oku-Tanba yang bersuara dari perutnya dan menarik minat seorang pengelola pertunjukan keliling.
long_description.en: The Nichibunken database summary of the Shiojiri tells of a craftsman’s son in the capital in the year Genroku 16 who ran a fever and then spoke with a voice from his belly; after medicines and prayers failed, the physician 菅玄際 concluded that the illness was the work of an Ōseichū and gave him a raigan (雷丸) decoction, the voice ceased, and a lizard-shaped insect with a small horn came out of his anus. The summary of the Kanden jihitsu tells of a farmer’s wife in Oku-Tanba who spoke from her belly and drew the interest of a travelling showman.

long_description.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang mencatat dua tafsiran atas kisah Jepang ini: sebagai gambaran cacing gelang yang nyata, atau sekadar adaptasi teks Tiongkok dengan tambahan unsur bisul berbentuk mulut (jinmensō). Di Tiongkok, orang yang hanya ikut-ikutan tanpa pendapat sendiri juga diejek dengan sebutan Ōseichū.
long_description.en: Japanese Wikipedia records two interpretations of these Japanese tales: that they describe the real roundworm, or that they are merely an adaptation of Chinese texts with the added mouth-like boil (jinmensō). In China a person who simply echoes others without an opinion of their own was also mockingly called an Ōseichū.

description.id: Raigan, obat yang berasal dari jamur parasit bambu, dikatakan manjur melawan penyakit ini dan membuat serangganya keluar; dalam kisah dari ibu kota, suara dalam perut menolak ramuan raigan dengan keras tetapi menjadi lemah setelah meminumnya.
description.en: Raigan, a medicine from a fungus that parasitises bamboo, is said to be effective against this illness and to make the insect leave; in the tale from the capital the voice in the belly strongly refused the raigan decoction but weakened after drinking it.

claims.quote: 応声虫（おうせいちゅう）または応声（おうせい）は、中国や日本の説話集・随筆集に見られる奇病、およびその病気を引き起こす怪虫。

statement.id: Ōseichū (応声虫) atau Ōsei (応声) adalah penyakit aneh yang tercatat dalam kumpulan kisah dan esai Tiongkok dan Jepang, sekaligus serangga ajaib penyebab penyakit itu.
statement.en: Ōseichū (応声虫), or Ōsei (応声), is a strange illness found in Chinese and Japanese story collections and essays, and also the strange insect that causes it.

claims.quote: 応声虫による症状（応声虫病）があらわれた人物の説話は、中国の『朝野僉載』や『文昌雑録』、『遯斎間覧』などに記述がみられ、本草書である『本草綱目』には応声虫に効果があったとされる雷丸（らいがん）や藍（あい）の解説文中にもその存在が言及されている。 応声虫が人体の中に入り込むと、本人は何もしゃべっていないのに腹の中から問いかけに応じた返事がかえって来るとされる。

statement.id: Kisah orang yang terkena penyakit ini tercatat dalam teks Tiongkok seperti Chaoye Qianzai (朝野僉載), Wenchang zalu (文昌雑録) dan Dunzhai xianlan (遯斎間覧), dan Bencao gangmu (本草綱目) menyebutnya dalam uraian tentang raigan (雷丸) dan ai (藍). Setelah serangga itu masuk ke tubuh, dari dalam perut terdengar jawaban atas pertanyaan padahal penderitanya tidak berbicara.
statement.en: Accounts of people afflicted with it are recorded in Chinese texts such as the Chaoye Qianzai (朝野僉載), Wenchang zalu (文昌雑録) and Dunzhai xianlan (遯斎間覧), and the Bencao gangmu (本草綱目) mentions it in its entries on raigan (雷丸) and ai (藍). Once the insect enters the body, replies to questions come from the belly although the person is not speaking.

claims.quote: 腹の中から虫が声を出すという症状を受け、中国では「自分の意見をもたず付和雷同した意見のみを言う者」を応声虫と揶揄して呼んだともいう。

statement.id: Karena gejala suara serangga dari dalam perut, di Tiongkok orang yang tidak punya pendapat sendiri dan hanya ikut-ikutan juga diejek dengan sebutan Ōseichū.
statement.en: Because of the symptom of an insect voicing from inside the belly, in China a person with no opinion of their own who merely echoes others was mockingly called an Ōseichū.

claims.quote: 日本においても、回虫などの寄生虫のように人間の体内に棲む怪虫によって引き起こされる病気であるとされ、人間がこの病気に冒されると、高熱が10日間ほど続いて苦しんだ後、腹に出来物ができ、次第にそれが口のような形になる。この口は病気になった者の喋ったことを口真似するため、応声虫の名がある。

statement.id: Di Jepang pun ia dianggap penyakit akibat serangga ajaib yang hidup dalam tubuh seperti cacing gelang. Penderita demam tinggi sekitar sepuluh hari, lalu perutnya muncul bisul yang lama-kelamaan berbentuk seperti mulut; mulut itu menirukan ucapan si sakit, sehingga ada nama Ōseichū.
statement.en: In Japan too it was regarded as a disease caused by a strange insect living inside the body like a roundworm. The sufferer has a high fever for about ten days, then a boil appears on the belly and gradually takes the shape of a mouth; the mouth mimics what the sick person says, hence the name Ōseichū.

claims.quote: 元禄16年正月、京師の工人の息子が急に発熱し、数日して立ち直ったものの、腹の中から物を言う声がする。薬や祈祷をしてもまったく効果がなかった。

statement.id: Basis data Kaii-Yōkai Densho Nichibunken (International Research Center for Japanese Studies) meringkas kisah dari Shiojiri (塩尻): pada bulan pertama tahun Genroku 16, putra seorang perajin di ibu kota demam mendadak dan, setelah pulih beberapa hari, terdengar suara berbicara dari dalam perutnya; obat dan doa sama sekali tidak berhasil.
statement.en: The Kaii-Yōkai Densho Database of Nichibunken (International Research Center for Japanese Studies) summarises a tale from the Shiojiri (塩尻): in the first month of Genroku 16 the son of a craftsman in the capital suddenly ran a fever and, after recovering within a few days, a voice speaking could be heard from inside his belly; medicine and prayers had no effect at all.

claims.quote: その後、医者の菅玄際が様々な書物からこの病は応声虫の仕業と見立てた。そこで雷丸の入った薬湯を飲ませようとしたところ、腹の声は大いに拒んでいたが、飲んだ次の日は声がやや涸れた。そしてさらに飲ませると声は絶えた。便所に行くと肛門から虫が下った。形はトカゲのようで、額に小さい角があり、親は殺した。息子は6月末に本復したという。

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan itu, dokter 菅玄際 menyimpulkan dari berbagai buku bahwa penyakit tersebut ulah Ōseichū. Ketika ia hendak memberi ramuan berisi raigan (雷丸), suara dari perut menolak keras, tetapi sehari setelah diminum suaranya agak serak, dan setelah diminum lagi suara itu lenyap. Saat anak itu ke toilet, seekor serangga keluar dari anusnya, berbentuk seperti kadal dengan tanduk kecil di dahi, dan orang tuanya membunuhnya; anak itu pulih sepenuhnya pada akhir bulan keenam.
statement.en: In the summary, the physician 菅玄際 concluded from various books that the illness was the work of an Ōseichū. When he tried to give a decoction containing raigan (雷丸), the voice in the belly strongly refused, but the day after it was drunk the voice grew hoarse, and when it was given again the voice ceased. When the boy went to the toilet an insect came down through the anus, shaped like a lizard with a small horn on its forehead, and his parent killed it; the boy fully recovered at the end of the sixth month.

claims.quote: 四条坊門油小路の東にいた見世物を業とする者が、奥丹波の何とか言う山里に、農人の妻で50歳ばかり者が腹中から声を出すというのを聞きつけ交渉に向かった。夫が言うには、先年の霜月に六条に詣で、茶屋で休んでいたところ、腹中から声がするようになったと語った。

statement.id: Basis data Nichibunken meringkas kisah dari Kanden jihitsu (閑田次筆): seorang pengelola pertunjukan keliling mendengar kabar tentang istri seorang petani berusia sekitar 50 tahun di sebuah desa pegunungan Oku-Tanba yang mengeluarkan suara dari dalam perutnya, lalu pergi menawarnya. Sang suami mengatakan bahwa suara itu mulai terdengar dari perutnya ketika mereka beristirahat di kedai teh setelah berziarah ke Rokujō pada bulan kesebelas tahun sebelumnya.
statement.en: The Nichibunken database summarises a tale from the Kanden jihitsu (閑田次筆): a showman heard of a farmer’s wife of about fifty in a mountain village of Oku-Tanba who spoke with a voice from her belly, and went to negotiate with her. Her husband said that the voice began coming from her belly when they were resting at a teahouse after visiting Rokujō in the eleventh month of the previous year.

claims.quote: 洛州有士人患應病，語即喉中應之。以問善醫張文仲，經夜思之，乃得一法。即取《本草》令讀之，皆應；至其所畏者，即不言。仲乃錄取藥，合和為丸，服之應時而愈。

statement.id: Dalam Chaoye Qianzai (朝野僉載), seorang terpelajar dari Luozhou (洛州) menderita "penyakit menjawab" (應病): ucapannya dijawab dari tenggorokannya. Tabib Zhang Wenzhong (張文仲) menyuruh Bencao dibacakan; suara itu menjawab semuanya sampai ke obat yang ditakutinya, lalu ia diam. Zhang mencatat obat itu, membuatnya menjadi pil, dan penderitanya sembuh seketika setelah meminumnya.
statement.en: In the Chaoye Qianzai (朝野僉載), a scholar of Luozhou (洛州) suffers from an "echoing illness" (應病): his speech is answered from his throat. The physician Zhang Wenzhong (張文仲) has the Bencao read out; the voice answers all of it until it reaches the drug it fears, and then falls silent. Zhang records that drug, makes pills, and the sufferer recovers at once after taking them.

claims.quote: 雷丸（竹に寄生するサルノコシカケ科の一種で漢方薬の一つ）を服用すれば効果があり、虫も体外に出るという。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, raigan (雷丸), jamur dari keluarga Polyporaceae yang hidup parasit pada bambu dan merupakan salah satu obat Kanpō, dikatakan manjur jika diminum, dan serangganya pun keluar dari tubuh.
statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, raigan (雷丸), a member of the Polyporaceae that parasitises bamboo and is one of the Kampō medicines, is said to be effective when taken, and the insect also leaves the body.

claims.quote: 喋るだけでなく食べ物も食べる。自ら食べ物を要求し、これを拒むと患者を高熱で苦しめたり、大声で悪口を叫んだりもする。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, mulut itu tidak hanya berbicara tetapi juga makan; ia meminta makanan sendiri, dan jika ditolak ia menyiksa penderita dengan demam tinggi atau berteriak memaki dengan suara keras.
statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, the mouth not only talks but also eats; it demands food itself, and if refused it torments the patient with a high fever or shouts abuse at the top of its voice.

claims.quote: これらの話は、実在の寄生虫である回虫を綴ったものであり、回虫が腹にいることによる異常な空腹感や、虫下しを飲んで肛門から排泄された回虫の死骸を描写したものであるとも考えられているが、前述のように応声虫はもともと中国に存在する説話であり、また『新著聞集』にあるものなどは中国に伝わるものに人面瘡の要素（口のようなできものが発症する点）が加わっており、中国の文献を単純に換骨奪胎し脚色しただけのものであるとする説もある。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang mencatat dua tafsiran atas kisah-kisah Jepang itu: sebagai gambaran cacing gelang (回虫) yang nyata, dengan rasa lapar yang tidak wajar dan bangkai cacing yang keluar dari anus setelah minum obat cacing; atau, karena Ōseichū aslinya kisah Tiongkok dan versi Shinchomonjū (新著聞集) menambahkan unsur jinmensō (人面瘡, bisul berbentuk mulut), sebagai sekadar adaptasi dan penggubahan teks Tiongkok.
statement.en: Japanese Wikipedia records two interpretations of the Japanese tales: that they describe the real roundworm (回虫), with its abnormal hunger and the dead worm passed through the anus after taking a vermifuge; or, since the Ōseichū was originally a Chinese tale and the Shinchomonjū (新著聞集) version adds the jinmensō (人面瘡) element of a mouth-like boil, that they are merely a rewriting and adaptation of Chinese texts.

topic.en: Nature of the Ōseichū tales in Japan

summary.id: Gambaran cacing gelang yang nyata (rasa lapar tak wajar, bangkai cacing keluar dari anus).
summary.en: A description of the real roundworm (abnormal hunger, dead worm passed through the anus).

summary.id: Sekadar adaptasi teks Tiongkok dengan tambahan unsur bisul berbentuk mulut.

short_description.id: Panhu adalah tokoh mitologi Han dan Yao serta kisah asal-usul sejumlah kelompok.
short_description.en: Panhu is a figure in Han and Yao mythology and in several groups' origin stories.

long_description.id: Panhu adalah tokoh mitologi Han dan Yao serta kisah asal-usul sejumlah kelompok. Kisah dasarnya menceritakan anjing naga yang menjadi manusia dan menikahi putri. Mitos ini merupakan mitos asal-usul yang penting bagi berbagai kelompok etnis, dan pada masa kini Panhu dipuja orang She dan Yao sebagai "Raja Pan". Namanya secara harfiah berarti "labu piring".
long_description.en: Panhu is a figure in Han and Yao mythology and in several groups' origin stories. The central tale describes a dragon-dog becoming a man and marrying a princess. The myth serves as a key origin tale for a range of ethnic groups, and today the She and Yao worship Panhu as "King Pan". His name literally means "plate gourd".

long_description.id: Sebuah versi bermula dari cacing emas yang dikeluarkan dari telinga perempuan di istana, yang kemudian menjadi anjing Panhu; raja menawarkan putrinya kepada siapa pun yang membawa kepala musuhnya, dan Panhu melakukannya. Dalam varian tertentu, perubahan menjadi manusia tidak selesai dan kepala anjing tetap ada. Panhu dan sang putri akhirnya memiliki enam putra dan enam putri yang menjadi 12 klan. Kisah Panhu memiliki versi yang lebih historis dan versi yang lebih mitologis.
long_description.en: One version begins with a golden worm removed from a palace woman's ear, which then becomes the dog Panhu; the king offers his daughter to anyone who brings the head of his enemy, and Panhu does so. In some variants, the human transformation remains incomplete and the dog head persists. Panhu and the princess eventually have six sons and six daughters who become 12 clans. Panhu accounts have more historicized and more mythological versions.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah teks klasik, Gaoxin yang kewalahan oleh serangan Quanrong menawarkan emas, kota, dan putri bungsunya bagi siapa pun yang membawa kepala Jenderal Wu. Anjing berbulu lima warna bernama Panhu membawa kepala itu, sehingga sang kaisar menyerahkan putrinya; Panhu membawanya ke Gunung Selatan dan tinggal di ruang batu. Setelah tiga tahun lahir dua belas anak, dan keturunan mereka kemudian berkembang dan disebut Manyi, yang menurut teks itu adalah suku Man di Changsha dan Wuling.
long_description.en: In a classical text, Gaoxin, troubled by raids from the Quanrong, offers gold, towns, and his youngest daughter to anyone who brings the head of General Wu. A five-colored dog named Panhu brings the head, so the emperor gives up his daughter; Panhu carries her to the Southern Mountain and stays in a stone chamber. After three years twelve children are born, and their descendants multiply and are called the Manyi, who according to the text are the Man of Changsha and Wuling.

claims.quote: Panhu (hanzi: 盤瓠; pinyin Pánhù; IPA: /pʰan³⁵-xu⁵¹/) is an important figure in Han and Yao mythologies. The Panhu mythological complex includes myths in Chinese and also other languages.

statement.id: Panhu adalah tokoh mitologi Han dan Yao serta kisah asal-usul sejumlah kelompok.
statement.en: Panhu is a figure in Han and Yao mythology and in several groups' origin stories.

claims.quote: The basic Panhu myth is about a dragon-dog who transformed into a man and married a princess. In the myth, there was an old woman in an ancient Chinese king's palace who had ear pain for many years. A royal physician plucked out a small, golden worm from her ear, and placed it inside of a gourd covered with a plate.

statement.id: Kisah dasarnya menceritakan anjing naga yang menjadi manusia dan menikahi putri.
statement.en: The central tale describes a dragon-dog becoming a man and marrying a princess.

claims.quote: The basic Panhu myth is about a dragon-dog who transformed into a man and married a princess. In the myth, there was an old woman in an ancient Chinese king's palace who had ear pain for many years. A royal physician plucked out a small, golden worm from her ear, and placed it inside of a gourd covered with a plate.

statement.id: Sebuah versi bermula dari cacing emas yang dikeluarkan dari telinga perempuan di istana.
statement.en: One version begins with a golden worm removed from a palace woman's ear.

claims.quote: There are also variant versions. In some variants, the dragon-dog became transformed into a human, except for his head. This is sometimes attributed to the princess worrying that he was starving inside the golden vessel he was placed inside of for seven days and seven nights to transform into a human, which resulted in the process being incomplete.

statement.id: Dalam varian tertentu, perubahan menjadi manusia tidak selesai dan kepala anjing tetap ada.
statement.en: In some variants, the human transformation remains incomplete and the dog head persists.

claims.quote: In the study of historical Chinese culture, many of the stories that have been told regarding characters and events which have been written or told of the distant past have a double tradition: one which presents a more historicized version and one which presents a more mythological version. This is also true in many of the accounts related to Panhu.

statement.id: Kisah Panhu memiliki versi yang lebih historis dan versi yang lebih mitologis.
statement.en: Panhu accounts have more historicized and more mythological versions.

claims.quote: The worm then turned into a dog, Panhu, who in some versions had five colored fur. The king offered to marry his daughter to anybody that would present him with the head of his enemy. This was accomplished by Panhu.

statement.id: Cacing itu kemudian menjadi anjing bernama Panhu yang dalam sebagian versi berbulu lima warna; raja menawarkan putrinya kepada siapa pun yang membawa kepala musuhnya, dan hal itu dilakukan oleh Panhu.
statement.en: The worm then became a dog, Panhu, who in some versions had five-colored fur; the king offered his daughter in marriage to anyone who would bring him the head of his enemy, and Panhu accomplished it.

claims.quote: Accounts vary, but eventually Panhu and the princess had six sons and six daughters who became the famous 12 clans of Chinese mythology.

statement.id: Catatan berbeda-beda, tetapi akhirnya Panhu dan sang putri memiliki enam putra dan enam putri yang menjadi 12 klan terkenal dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
statement.en: Accounts vary, but eventually Panhu and the princess had six sons and six daughters who became the famous 12 clans of Chinese mythology.

claims.quote: In modern times, Panhu has been worshiped by the She people and Yao people as "King Pan".

statement.id: Pada masa kini, Panhu dipuja oleh orang She dan orang Yao sebagai "Raja Pan".
statement.en: In modern times, Panhu has been worshiped by the She and Yao peoples as "King Pan".

claims.quote: 昔高辛氏有犬戎之寇，帝患其侵暴，而征伐不克。乃訪募天下，有能得犬戎之將吳將軍頭者，購黃金千鎰，邑萬家，又妻以少女。

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini, Gaoxin (高辛氏) kewalahan oleh serangan Quanrong (犬戎) dan menawarkan emas, kota, dan putri bungsunya kepada siapa pun yang membawa kepala Jenderal Wu (吳將軍) dari Quanrong.
statement.en: In this classical text, Gaoxin (高辛氏) is troubled by raids from the Quanrong (犬戎) and offers gold, towns, and his youngest daughter to anyone who brings the head of General Wu (吳將軍) of the Quanrong.

claims.quote: 時帝有畜狗，其毛五采，名曰槃瓠。下令之後，槃瓠遂銜人頭造闕下，群臣怪而診之，乃吳將軍首也。

statement.id: Pada saat itu sang kaisar memiliki seekor anjing berbulu lima warna bernama Panhu (槃瓠); setelah titah diumumkan, Panhu membawa sebuah kepala manusia ke istana, dan para menteri mendapati itu kepala Jenderal Wu.
statement.en: The emperor then had a dog with five-colored fur named Panhu (槃瓠); after the order was issued, Panhu carried a human head to the palace gate, and the ministers found it was General Wu's head.

claims.quote: 帝不得已，乃以女配槃瓠。槃瓠得女，負而走入南山，止石室中。所處險絶，人迹不至。

statement.id: Karena terpaksa, sang kaisar menikahkan putrinya dengan Panhu (槃瓠); Panhu menggendong sang putri ke Gunung Selatan (南山) dan tinggal di sebuah ruang batu di tempat yang berbahaya dan tidak dijejaki orang.
statement.en: Having no choice, the emperor gave his daughter to Panhu (槃瓠); Panhu carried her on his back into the Southern Mountain (南山) and stayed in a stone chamber in a perilous place no one reached.

claims.quote: 經三年，生子一十二人，六男六女。槃瓠死後，因自相夫妻。織績木皮，染以草實，好五色衣服。製裁皆有尾形。

statement.id: Setelah tiga tahun lahir dua belas anak, enam putra dan enam putri; sesudah Panhu (槃瓠) meninggal mereka saling menjadi suami istri, menenun kulit kayu, mewarnainya dengan biji tumbuhan, menyukai pakaian lima warna, dan menjahit pakaian berbentuk ekor.
statement.en: After three years twelve children were born, six sons and six daughters; after Panhu (槃瓠) died they married one another, wove tree bark, dyed it with plant seeds, liked five-colored clothes, and cut garments with tail shapes.

claims.quote: 其後滋蔓，號曰蠻夷。外癡內黠，安土重舊。 ... 今長沙武陵蠻是也。

statement.id: Keturunan mereka kemudian berkembang dan disebut Manyi (蠻夷); teks itu menyebut mereka tampak bodoh di luar tetapi cerdik di dalam, setia pada tanah dan kebiasaan lama, dan menyatakan bahwa merekalah suku Man di Changsha dan Wuling (長沙武陵蠻).
statement.en: Their descendants later multiplied and were called the Manyi (蠻夷); the text calls them seemingly foolish outside but shrewd within, attached to their land and old ways, and says they are the Man of Changsha and Wuling (長沙武陵蠻).

short_description.id: Pihi adalah burung mitologis bersayap satu yang dikaitkan dengan cerita Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Pihi is a one winged mythological bird associated with Chinese lore.

long_description.id: Pihi adalah burung mitologis bersayap satu yang dikaitkan dengan cerita Tiongkok. Karena hanya mempunyai satu sayap, Pihi dikatakan dapat terbang ketika berpasangan.
long_description.en: Pihi is a one winged mythological bird associated with Chinese lore. Because it has only one wing, Pihi is said to fly only as a pair.

long_description.id: Satu sumber menyebut bahwa kata pihi diciptakan oleh Guillaume Apollinaire dan pertama kali muncul dalam kumpulan Alcools untuk burung khayalan dari Tiongkok yang bersayap satu dan terbang berpasangan. Dalam puisi Zone, pihi digambarkan panjang dan lentur, sedangkan dalam Calligrammes ada baris tentang burung yang hanya punya satu sayap.
long_description.en: One source says the word pihi was created by Guillaume Apollinaire and first appears in the collection Alcools for imaginary birds from China that have one wing and fly in pairs. In the poem Zone the pihis are described as long and supple, while Calligrammes contains a line about the bird that has only one wing.

long_description.id: Ada burung serupa dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang disebut 比翼鸟 (biyi niao). Sumber yang sama menilai sangat mungkin Apollinaire hanya menuliskan kata biyi dalam bahasa Roman sehingga menjadi Pihi, setelah, menurut Claude Debon, membaca sebuah nomor Revue asiatique tahun 1896. Teks klasik yang dikutip Kamus Kangxi menyebut burung 比翼鳥 yang tidak terbang bila tidak berpasangan.
long_description.en: Chinese mythology has similar birds called 比翼鸟 (biyi niao). The same source judges it very probable that Apollinaire simply transcribed the word biyi in a Romance language, giving Pihi, after reading, according to Claude Debon, an issue of the Revue asiatique of 1896. A classical text quoted in the Kangxi Dictionary describes a 比翼鳥 that cannot fly unless paired.

note.id: Sumber kedua menilai pihi sangat mungkin merupakan transkripsi dari 比翼鸟 (biyi niao); teks klasik yang dikutip Kamus Kangxi menggambarkan burung 比翼鳥 yang tidak terbang bila tidak berpasangan.
note.en: The second source judges the pihi very probably to be a transcription of 比翼鸟 (biyi niao); a classical text quoted in the Kangxi Dictionary describes a 比翼鳥 that cannot fly unless paired.

description.id: Dalam puisi Zone, pihi digambarkan datang dari Tiongkok, panjang dan lentur, bersayap satu, dan terbang berpasangan.
description.en: In the poem Zone the pihis are described as coming from China, long and supple, with one wing, flying in pairs.

description.id: Sebuah baris menyebut "Abatis de pihis", dan baris berikutnya membicarakan puisi tentang burung yang hanya punya satu sayap.
description.en: One line reads "Abatis de pihis" and the next speaks of a poem about the bird that has only one wing.
