statement.id: Kata Pihi diciptakan oleh Guillaume Apollinaire dan pertama kali muncul dalam kumpulan Alcools, untuk menyebut burung khayalan dari Tiongkok yang hanya memiliki satu sayap sehingga terbang berpasangan.
statement.en: The word Pihi was created by Guillaume Apollinaire and first appears in the collection Alcools, naming imaginary birds from China that have only one wing and are therefore forced to fly as a pair.

claims.quote: Or il existe dans la mythologie chinoise des oiseaux similaires, nommés 比翼鸟, en pinyin biyi niao ... il est donc très probable que Apollinaire, à la suite selon Claude Debon de la lecture d'un numéro de la Revue asiatique de 1896, ait simplement transcrit le mot biyi en langue romane, ce qui aurait donné Pihi.

statement.id: Menurut sumber ini, dalam mitologi Tiongkok ada burung serupa bernama 比翼鸟 (biyi niao), dan sangat mungkin Apollinaire, setelah membaca sebuah nomor Revue asiatique tahun 1896 menurut Claude Debon, hanya menuliskan kata biyi dalam bahasa Roman (langue romane) sehingga menjadi Pihi.
statement.en: According to this source, Chinese mythology has similar birds called 比翼鸟 (biyi niao), and it is very probable that Apollinaire, after reading an issue of the Revue asiatique of 1896 according to Claude Debon, simply transcribed the word biyi in a Romance language, giving Pihi.

statement.en: In Apollinaire's Calligrammes, one line reads "Abatis de pihis" and the next says there is a poem to be made about the bird that has only one wing, which will be sent as a telephone message.

claims.quote: 《爾雅·釋鳥》南方有比翼鳥焉，不比不飛，其名謂之鶼鶼。《郭註》似鳧，靑赤色，一目一翼，相得乃飛。

statement.id: Kamus Kangxi mengutip Erya: di selatan ada burung 比翼鳥 yang tidak terbang bila tidak berpasangan, bernama 鶼鶼; catatan Guo menyebutnya menyerupai bebek, berwarna biru kemerahan, bermata satu dan bersayap satu, dan terbang hanya bila bersama.
statement.en: The Kangxi Dictionary quotes the Erya: in the south there is a 比翼鳥 that cannot fly unless paired, named 鶼鶼; Guo's note says it resembles a duck, is blue-red, has one eye and one wing, and flies only when together.

short_description.id: Qianliyan adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Shunfeng'er. Namanya berarti "mata seribu li" dan melambangkan penglihatan jauh.
short_description.en: Qianliyan is a Chinese sea and door god who guards Mazu temples with Shunfeng'er. His name means "thousand-li eyes" and expresses far-seeing.

long_description.id: Qianliyan adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Shunfeng'er. Namanya berarti mata seribu li dan melambangkan kemampuan melihat jauh. Penglihatan tajamnya dipakai untuk melindungi pelaut pada malam hari serta saat kabut dan cuaca buruk.
long_description.en: Qianliyan is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Shunfeng'er. His name means thousand-li eyes and expresses far-seeing ability. His sharp vision is used to protect sailors at night and during fog and bad weather.

long_description.id: Pada zaman Ming, ia juga dikenal sebagai Li Lou. Journey to the West menampilkannya sebagai personifikasi mata Kaisar Giok dan salah satu bawahannya. Dalam teks novel itu, Kaisar Giok memerintahkan Qianliyan dan Shunfeng'er mengamati, lalu keduanya melaporkan asal monyet batu. Journey to the South menampilkannya sebagai bawahan Kaisar Flowering Brightness.
long_description.en: During the Ming period, he was also known as Li Lou. Journey to the West portrays him as the personified eyes of the Jade Emperor and one of his lieutenants. In the novel's text, the Jade Emperor commands Qianliyan and Shunfeng'er to look, and the two then report on the stone monkey. Journey to the South portrays him as a lieutenant of the Emperor of Flowering Brightness.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Mazu, Qianliyan paling sering digambarkan sebagai iblis yang dikalahkan dan dijinakkan atau dijadikan sahabat oleh dewi laut itu. Dalam satu kisah, selendang sutra ajaib Mazu meniupkan pasir ke mata dan telinga kedua iblis itu; dalam kisah lain kekuatan mereka lenyap ketika dilumuri darah anjing hitam.
long_description.en: In the Mazu tradition, Qianliyan is usually pictured as a demon that the sea goddess overcame and then tamed or made a friend. In one account her magic silk scarf sends sand into the eyes and ears of the two demons; in another their powers fail once black dog blood is smeared over them.

long_description.id: Dalam seni, ia biasanya tampil sebagai iblis berkulit hijau yang menaungi matanya dari silau matahari. Dalam ziarah tahunan dari Dajia ke Beigang, patung Mazu diiringi figur Qianliyan dan Shunfeng'er setinggi sekitar tiga meter yang diperankan pria bertopeng di atas egrang.
long_description.en: In art he is usually a green-skinned demon who shades his eyes against the sun. During the annual pilgrimage from Dajia to Beigang, Mazu's idol is accompanied by figures of Qianliyan and Shunfeng'er about three metres tall, played by masked men on stilts.

description.id: Penglihatan tajam Qianliyan dipakai untuk melindungi pelaut pada malam hari, saat kabut, dan cuaca buruk; dalam beberapa kisah ia dapat melihat segala sesuatu di dunia.
description.en: Qianliyan's sharp vision is used to protect sailors at night, in fog and in bad weather; in some accounts he can see everything in the world.

description.id: Dalam satu kisah, selendang sutra ajaib Mazu meniupkan awan pasir ke mata dan telinga Qianliyan dan Shunfeng'er sehingga keduanya kalah.
description.en: In one account, Mazu's magical silk scarf blew clouds of sand into the eyes and ears of Qianliyan and Shunfeng'er, defeating them.

description.id: Dalam satu kisah, kekuatan keduanya lenyap ketika mereka dilumuri darah anjing hitam.

short_description.id: Qiqirn adalah roh anjing besar tak berbulu dalam mitologi Inuit dari sekitar Pulau Baffin yang membuat manusia dan anjing kejang [qiqirn-c01, qiqirn-c02].
short_description.en: Qiqirn is a large, hairless dog spirit of Inuit mythology from around Baffin Island that sends men and dogs into convulsions [qiqirn-c01, qiqirn-c02].

long_description.id: Qiqirn adalah roh anjing besar tak berbulu dalam mitologi Inuit [qiqirn-c01]. Kehadirannya membuat manusia dan anjing kejang, kadang sampai mati [qiqirn-c02], tetapi ia takut pada manusia dan lari jika dilihat angakkuq [qiqirn-c03]. Daniel Merkur menduga kejang itu kiasan inisiasi dukun [qiqirn-c04]. Rudyard Kipling menulis tentangnya dalam cerpen "Quiquern" [qiqirn-c05].
long_description.en: Qiqirn is a large, hairless dog spirit of Inuit mythology [qiqirn-c01]. Its presence throws men and dogs into sometimes fatal fits [qiqirn-c02], but it fears humans and flees if an angakkuq sees it [qiqirn-c03]. Daniel Merkur saw the fits as allusions to shamanic initiation [qiqirn-c04]. Rudyard Kipling wrote of it in the story "Quiquern" [qiqirn-c05].

long_description.id: Istilah serupa dalam mitologi Inuit adalah keelut, roh bumi jahat yang juga muncul sebagai anjing tak berbulu [qiqirn-c06]. Dalam cerita pendek sastra "Quiquern", Quiquern digambarkan sebagai hantu anjing raksasa tak bergigi dan tak berbulu yang konon hidup di Utara yang jauh dan berkeliaran tepat sebelum suatu peristiwa terjadi [qiqirn-c07]. Bahkan para dukun enggan membicarakannya, dan ia membuat anjing menjadi gila [qiqirn-c08]. Pada akhir cerita, sang gadis menyebut dua makhluk yang malu itu sebagai Quiquern yang menuntun mereka ke tanah aman, dengan delapan kaki dan kepala ganda [qiqirn-c09]; keduanya terikat menyamping pada leher masing-masing [qiqirn-c10], dan ternyata mereka sepasang anjing penarik kereta yang kalungnya terjerat [qiqirn-c11].
long_description.en: A similar term in Inuit mythology is keelut, a malevolent earth spirit that also appears as a hairless dog [qiqirn-c06]. In the literary short story "Quiquern", Quiquern is a phantom of a gigantic toothless, hairless dog said to live in the far North and to wander the country just before things are going to happen [qiqirn-c07]. Even sorcerers are reluctant to speak of it, and it makes dogs go mad [qiqirn-c08]. At the story's end the girl calls the two shamefaced creatures Quiquern, who led them to safe ground, with eight legs and a double head [qiqirn-c09]; each is fastened sidelong to the other's neck [qiqirn-c10], and they turn out to be a pair of sled dogs whose collars were entangled [qiqirn-c11].

description.id: Ia lari jika dilihat angakkuq.
description.en: It flees if an angakkuq sees it.

note.id: Istilah serupa dari mitologi Inuit: roh bumi jahat yang juga tampil sebagai anjing tak berbulu.
note.en: A similar term from Inuit mythology: a malevolent earth spirit that also appears as a hairless dog.

description.id: Cerpen sastra Rudyard Kipling tentang anjing hantu berkaki banyak yang ditakuti para dukun dan membuat anjing gila [qiqirn-c05, qiqirn-c07, qiqirn-c08]; "roh" itu ternyata sepasang anjing penarik kereta yang kalungnya terjerat [qiqirn-c11].
description.en: Rudyard Kipling's literary short story about a many-legged phantom dog feared by sorcerers that makes dogs go mad [qiqirn-c05, qiqirn-c07, qiqirn-c08]; the "spirit" turns out to be a pair of sled dogs whose collars were entangled [qiqirn-c11].

short_description.id: Qiulong adalah naga Tiongkok dengan definisi yang bertentangan mengenai keberadaan tanduk.
short_description.en: Qiulong is a Chinese dragon with conflicting definitions about the presence of horns.

long_description.id: Qiulong adalah naga Tiongkok dengan definisi yang bertentangan mengenai keberadaan tanduk. Sebagian definisi menyebutnya bertanduk, sementara yang lain tidak bertanduk.
long_description.en: Qiulong is a Chinese dragon with conflicting definitions about the presence of horns. Some definitions call it horned, while others describe it as hornless.

long_description.id: Nama naga ini dapat dibaca qiu atau jiu dengan dua varian aksara. Aksara yang sama kadang digunakan di Jepang untuk mizuchi, naga sungai.
long_description.en: The dragon name can be read qiu or jiu with two written variants. The same characters are sometimes used in Japan for mizuchi, a river dragon.

long_description.id: Komentar Wang Yi pada Lisao menyatakan bahwa yang bertanduk disebut long dan yang tak bertanduk disebut qiu, sedangkan Wikipedia mencatat Guangya dan Zhu Junsheng yang memberi definisi berbeda: qiu bertanduk. Dalam Lisao, sang penyair membayangkan mengendarai qiu giok, dan pengantar Wang Yi menyebut qiulong sebagai kiasan bagi orang berbudi.
long_description.en: Wang Yi's commentary on the Lisao states that one with horns is called long and one without is called qiu, while Wikipedia records the Guangya and Zhu Junsheng giving a different definition: that the qiu has horns. In the Lisao the poet imagines riding a jade qiu, and Wang Yi's preface calls the qiulong a figure for the gentleman.

long_description.id: Huainanzi menyebut 赤螭 dan 青虯 berkelana di Jizhou ketika langit cerah, lalu naik di atas angin puyuh dengan wibawa yang menggerakkan langit dan bumi sehingga belut, beruang, dan harimau tunduk. Di bagian lain kitab itu, 青虯 menjadi kuda luar kereta guntur bersama 應龍 sebagai kuda dalam.
long_description.en: The Huainanzi says the 赤螭 and 青虯 roam Jizhou when the sky is clear, then rise on the whirlwind with a might that moves heaven and earth so that eels, bears and tigers submit. Elsewhere in the text, the 青虯 are the outer horses of a thunder chariot with 應龍 as the inner horses.

cultural_context.id: Menurut pengantar Wang Yi, Lisao memakai qiulong dan burung luan serta hong sebagai kiasan bagi orang berbudi.
cultural_context.en: According to Wang Yi's preface, the Lisao uses qiulong and luan and phoenix birds as figures for the gentleman.

statement.id: Komentar Wang Yi (王逸) pada larik 駟玉虯以乘鷖兮 menyatakan bahwa yang bertanduk disebut long (龍) dan yang tak bertanduk disebut qiu (虯).
statement.en: Wang Yi's (王逸) commentary on the line 駟玉虯以乘鷖兮 states that one with horns is called long (龍) and one without horns is called qiu (虯).

claims.quote: 言我設往行游，將乘玉虯，駕鳳車，淹塵埃而上征，去離時俗，遠群小也。

statement.id: Dalam penjelasan Wang Yi atas Lisao, sang penyair membayangkan mengendarai qiu giok (玉虯) dan kereta burung hong, menembus debu dan naik ke atas untuk meninggalkan dunia biasa dan menjauhi orang-orang rendah.
statement.en: In Wang Yi's explanation of the Lisao, the poet imagines riding a jade qiu (玉虯) and a phoenix chariot, passing through the dust and ascending to leave the common world and keep far from petty people.

claims.quote: 靈修美人，以媲於君；宓妃佚女，以譬賢臣；虯龍鸞鳳，以讬君子；飄風雲霓，以為小人。

statement.id: Dalam pengantar Wang Yi, Lisao memakai qiulong (虯龍) dan burung luan serta burung hong sebagai kiasan bagi orang berbudi (君子), sedangkan angin ribut serta awan dan pelangi sekunder dipakai untuk orang rendahan (小人).
statement.en: In Wang Yi's preface, the Lisao uses qiulong (虯龍) and luan and phoenix birds as figures for the gentleman (君子), while whirlwinds and clouds and secondary rainbows stand for petty persons (小人).

claims.quote: 今夫赤螭、青虯之游冀州也，天清地定，毒獸不作，飛鳥不駭，入榛薄，食薦梅，噆味含甘，步不出頃畝之區

statement.id: Huainanzi menggambarkan 赤螭 dan 青虯 (qiu hijau) berkelana di Jizhou (冀州) ketika langit cerah dan bumi tenang, binatang berbisa tidak bertindak dan burung tidak ketakutan; mereka masuk semak, makan tanaman, dan langkahnya tidak keluar dari satu petak lahan.
statement.en: The Huainanzi describes the 赤螭 and the 青虯 (green qiu) roaming Jizhou (冀州) when the sky is clear and the earth settled, venomous beasts do not act and birds are not startled; they enter thickets, eat plants, and their steps do not leave a plot of land.

claims.quote: 今夫赤螭、青虯之游冀州也 ... 若乃至於玄雲之素朝，陰陽交爭，降扶風，雜凍雨，扶搖而登之，威動天地，聲震海內，蛇鱔著泥百仞之中，熊羆匍匐丘山盤岩，虎豹襲穴而不敢咆
claims.locator: Huainanzi (淮南子), bab Lanming Xun (覽冥訓)

statement.id: Dalam bagian yang sama, ketika pagi bermendung gelap dan yin-yang bertarung, mereka (赤螭 dan 青虯) naik di atas angin puyuh sehingga wibawanya menggerakkan langit dan bumi dan suaranya mengguncang negeri; belut menyusup ke lumpur, beruang bersujud, dan harimau serta macan tutul tidak berani mengaum.
statement.en: In the same passage, on a morning of dark clouds when yin and yang contend, they (the 赤螭 and 青虯) rise on the whirlwind so that their might moves heaven and earth and their sound shakes the realm; eels sink into the mud, bears crouch, and tigers and leopards dare not roar.

claims.quote: 乘雷車，服駕應龍，驂青虯，援絕瑞，席蘿圖，黃雲絡，前白螭，後奔蛇

statement.id: Huainanzi menggambarkan pengendara kereta guntur (雷車) dengan naga bersayap (應龍) sebagai kuda dalam dan 青虯 (qiu hijau) sebagai kuda luar, dengan 白螭 di depan dan ular berlari di belakang.
statement.en: The Huainanzi describes riders of a thunder chariot (雷車) with winged dragons (應龍) as inner horses and green qiu (青虯) as outer horses, with a white 螭 in front and running snakes behind.

claims.quote: The Shuowen Jiezi scholar Zhu Junsheng 朱駿聲 (1788–1834 CE) explains that male long ( 龍) "dragons" have horns and female ones do not, and among young dragons, jiao ( 蛟) has one horn, qiu ( 虯) has two, and chi ( 螭) is hornless.

short_description.id: Rep-un-kamuy adalah kamuy (dewa) laut dalam kepercayaan Ainu, yang kadang digambarkan sebagai paus pembunuh atau pemuda pembawa tombak ikan.
short_description.en: Rep-un-kamuy is the Ainu kamuy (god) of the sea, sometimes depicted as an orca or as a young man with a harpoon.

long_description.id: Rep-un-kamuy adalah kamuy (dewa) laut dalam kepercayaan Ainu. Ia kadang digambarkan sebagai paus pembunuh (orca), dan dalam penggambaran lain sebagai pemuda yang riang, agak jahil, dan membawa tombak ikan. Wikipedia bahasa Inggris menyebutnya tokoh penting karena laut memberi panen yang tidak ada di darat: ikan, paus, dan pelayaran dagang.
long_description.en: Rep-un-kamuy is the Ainu kamuy (god) of the sea. He is sometimes depicted as an orca, and in other depictions as a carefree, somewhat mischievous young man with a harpoon. English Wikipedia calls him an important figure because the sea gives harvests not found on land: fish, whales and trading voyages.

long_description.id: Dalam salah satu kisahnya ia menombak seekor paus dan anaknya lalu melemparkannya ke dekat desa manusia. Alih-alih marah, ia tertawa dan mengatakan bahwa daging itu milik manusia untuk diperlakukan sesuka mereka; setelah melihat penghormatan mereka, ia menjamin bahwa kelimpahan laut akan menjauhkan mereka dari kelaparan. Ia juga disebut menyelamatkan sebuah desa di Hokkaido dari laba-laba raksasa Yaushikep dengan menariknya ke laut dari Teluk Uchiura dan mengubahnya menjadi Akkorokamui.
long_description.en: In one story he spears a whale and her calf and hurls them onto the beach close to a human village. Rather than being angered, he laughs and says the meat is the humans’ to treat as they please; once he sees their piety he assures them that the sea’s bounty will keep famine away. He is also said to have rescued a village on Hokkaido from the giant spider Yaushikep by dragging it out of Uchiura Bay into the sea, where it became Akkorokamui.

long_description.id: John Batchelor (1901) menggambarkan pemimpin para dewa laut Ainu, yang ia sebut Repun-riri-kata inao uk kamui: yang terbesar dan paling dihormati, tempat semua dewa laut lain tunduk. Bila ia membiarkan dirinya terlihat, wujudnya paus terbesar; ia dikatakan berniat baik kepada manusia, dipuja orang Ainu pesisir, dan didoakan dengan inao untuk cuaca baik dan tangkapan ikan yang banyak. Kamus Batchelor (1905) mengartikan Rep-un-kamui sebagai "para dewa laut", dan salah satu pelayan dewa itu, Rep-un-kontukai, tampil sebagai kura-kura.
long_description.en: John Batchelor (1901) describes the chief of the Ainu sea gods, whom he calls Repun-riri-kata inao uk kamui: the greatest and most esteemed, to whom every other sea god is subject. When he lets himself be seen it is in the form of the largest whale; he is said to be well disposed towards mankind, worshipped by Ainu on the coast, and prayed to with inao for fair weather and a large catch of fish. Batchelor’s dictionary (1905) glosses Rep-un-kamui as "the sea gods", and one of the god’s servants, Rep-un-kontukai, appears as a tortoise.

cultural_context.id: Laut penting dalam mitologi Ainu karena menyediakan panen yang tidak ada di darat, yaitu ikan, paus, dan pelayaran dagang; para penulis lama mencatat doa dan inao untuk dewa ini agar cuaca baik dan tangkapan banyak.
cultural_context.en: The sea matters in Ainu mythology because it offers harvests not found on land, namely fish, whales and trading voyages; older writers record prayers and inao to this god for fair weather and a good catch.

statement.id: John Batchelor (1901) menulis bahwa dewa yang ia sebut Repun-riri-kata inao uk kamui adalah yang terbesar dan paling dihormati di antara semua dewa laut, dan setiap dewa lain tunduk kepadanya.
statement.en: John Batchelor (1901) writes that the god he calls Repun-riri-kata inao uk kamui is the very greatest and most highly esteemed of all the gods of the sea, to whom every other owes allegiance and is subject.

claims.quote: Whenever he allows himself to be seen by man, it is always in the bodily form of the largest of large whales. As he is said to be well disposed towards mankind, he is very frequently worshipped by those Ainu who dwell upon the sea-coast.

statement.id: Menurut Batchelor, bila ia membiarkan dirinya terlihat manusia, wujudnya selalu paus terbesar dari yang besar; ia dikatakan berniat baik kepada manusia, sehingga sangat sering dipuja oleh orang Ainu yang tinggal di pesisir.
statement.en: According to Batchelor, whenever he allows himself to be seen by man it is always in the bodily form of the largest of large whales; he is said to be well disposed towards mankind, so he is very frequently worshipped by Ainu living on the sea-coast.

claims.quote: While the young men are away in their boats pursuing their occupations, the old men may often be seen sitting by the seaside making inao, and praying to this god for fair weather and a large catch of fish.

statement.id: Batchelor mencatat bahwa ketika para pemuda pergi dengan perahu, para lelaki tua sering terlihat duduk di tepi laut membuat inao (persembahan serut kayu) dan berdoa kepada dewa ini untuk cuaca baik dan hasil tangkapan ikan yang banyak.
statement.en: Batchelor records that while the young men are away in their boats, the old men are often seen sitting by the seaside making inao and praying to this god for fair weather and a large catch of fish.

claims.quote: This god is said to have two special servants, who are supposed to act as messengers or angels between himself and ... The first of these is called Rep-un-kontukai, ... He always appears in the form of a tortoise, and is frequently worshipped.

statement.id: Batchelor menulis bahwa dewa ini dikatakan memiliki dua pelayan khusus yang bertindak sebagai pembawa pesan antara dirinya dan manusia; yang pertama bernama Rep-un-kontukai, yang selalu tampil dalam wujud kura-kura dan sering dipuja.
statement.en: Batchelor writes that this god is said to have two special servants who act as messengers between himself and mankind; the first is called Rep-un-kontukai, who always appears in the form of a tortoise and is frequently worshipped.

short_description.id: Shōkera adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar dalam gulungan zaman Edo; sifatnya tidak pasti, tetapi dalam kebiasaan Kōshin-Machi ia dipandang sebagai yōkai yang mendatangkan kerugian bagi manusia.
short_description.en: The shōkera is a Japanese yōkai pictured in Edo-period scrolls; its nature is uncertain, but in the Kōshin-Machi custom it is seen as a yōkai that harms people.

long_description.id: Shōkera adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar dalam gulungan zaman Edo. Beberapa ejaan dicatat untuk namanya, yang secara harfiah berarti roh jangkrik tanah. Ilustrasi lama tidak memiliki keterangan, sehingga sifatnya tidak pasti, dan Sekien menggambarnya mengintip melalui jendela atap.
long_description.en: The shōkera is a Japanese yōkai pictured in Edo-period scrolls. Several spellings are recorded for its name, which literally means mole cricket spirit. The old illustrations lack explanatory text, leaving its nature uncertain, and Sekien depicts it peering through a roof skylight.

long_description.id: Dalam agama rakyat ada kebiasaan bernama "shōkera" pada Kōshin-Machi, berdasarkan kepercayaan pada serangga bernama Tiga Mayat di dalam tubuh yang pada malam Kōshin melaporkan kejahatan seseorang kepada dewa langit. Orang berjaga semalaman agar Tiga Mayat tidak keluar, dan konon yang tidur siang hari sesudahnya akan menerima kerugian; syair tertentu dikatakan menangkalnya. Dari sini shōkera dari Kōshin-Machi dipandang sebagai yōkai yang mendatangkan kerugian.
long_description.en: In folk religion there is a custom called "shōkera" in the Kōshin-Machi, based on a belief in an insect called the Three Corpses inside the body that on Kōshin night reports a person's crimes to the heavenly god. People stayed awake all night so the Three Corpses would not leave, and those who then slept during the day were said to suffer damage; a certain verse was said to ward this off. From this the shōkera of Kōshin-Machi is seen as a yōkai that causes harm.

long_description.id: Tulisan Kōshinden dari tahun-tahun Genroku mengandung kalimat bahwa shōkera adalah serangga dan menurut satu teori Tiga Mayat, sehingga ada tafsir bahwa shōkera merujuk pada Tiga Mayat; dikatakan pula ia personifikasi tiga mayat. Literatur yōkai sejak Shōwa dan Heisei menafsirkan gambaran Sekien sebagai pengawasan terhadap kepatuhan pada aturan Kōshin dan memperkirakan pelanggar dihukum dengan tiga jari berkuku tajam.
long_description.en: The Kōshinden writing from the Genroku years has a passage that shōkera is an insect and, in one theory, the Three Corpses, so there is an interpretation that shōkera refers to the Three Corpses; it is also said to be a personification of the three corpses. Yōkai literature from the Shōwa and Heisei eras interprets Sekien's depiction as surveillance of whether people follow Kōshin rules and supposes that violators would be punished with three fingers with sharp nails.

long_description.id: Sebagai latar, sebuah ensiklopedia Shinto menjelaskan bahwa kōshin adalah hari ketika para penganut berjaga semalaman demi umur panjang. Kebiasaan itu bermula dari klaim Ge Hong dalam Baopuzi tentang tiga cacing di tubuh manusia yang melaporkan dosa kepada Dewa Langit, dan berjaga diadakan agar cacing itu tidak lolos. Kini tujuan kebiasaan itu banyak bergeser menjadi perjamuan biasa.
long_description.en: As background, a Shinto encyclopedia explains that kōshin is a day when believers keep an all-night vigil for the sake of longevity. The custom goes back to Ge Hong's claim in the Baopuzi of three worms in the human body that report sins to the Celestial God, and the vigil is held to stop the worms escaping. Today the purpose of the custom has widely shifted to an ordinary banquet.

cultural_context.id: Kebiasaan Kōshin-Machi, yaitu berjaga semalaman agar Tiga Mayat tidak keluar dari tubuh, menjadi latar tafsir shōkera sebagai yōkai yang merugikan orang yang melanggarnya.
cultural_context.en: The Kōshin-Machi custom of staying awake all night so the Three Corpses would not leave the body is the setting for reading the shōkera as a yōkai that harms those who break it.

statement.en: In folk religion there is a custom called "shōkera" in the Kōshin-Machi, based on a belief in an insect called the Three Corpses inside the body that on Kōshin night rises to the skies and reports the person's crimes to the Ten-Tei (heavenly god), who then takes that person's life.

claims.quote: Also, in the writing Kōshinden (庚申伝) from the Genroku years, there is the passage "shōkera is an insect, and said in one theory to be the Three Corpses" (ショウキラハ虫ノコト也、一説三尸ノコトト云), so there is also the interpretation that shōkera refers to the Three Corpses

statement.en: Yōkai-related literature from the Shōwa and Heisei eras interprets this as surveillance, and it is supposed that the shōkera would punish those who break the rule with three fingers with sharp nails.

claims.quote: A day on which the 7th "stem" (kō) in the Chinese zodiacal system combines with the 9th "branch" (shin 'monkey') is known as kōshin, when believers spend an abstemious, all-night vigil for the sake of their longevity.

statement.id: Menurut Encyclopedia of Shinto, hari ketika "batang" ketujuh (kō) bertemu "cabang" kesembilan (shin, 'monyet') dalam sistem zodiak Tiongkok disebut kōshin, saat para penganut menjalani berjaga semalaman yang bersahaja demi umur panjang.
statement.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, a day on which the 7th "stem" (kō) combines with the 9th "branch" (shin, 'monkey') in the Chinese zodiacal system is known as kōshin, when believers keep an abstemious all-night vigil for the sake of longevity.

claims.quote: The custom goes back to the Chinese Taoist Ge Hong (283-343), who in Baopuzi ("He Who Holds to Simplicity") claimed that there are three worms (J. sanshi) in the human body, upper, middle, and lower, which on the night of kōshin attempt to escape while their hosts are asleep and to report the sins of such mortals to the Celestial God , thereby causing their lives to be shortened.

statement.id: Kebiasaan ini bermula dari Ge Hong, seorang Tao Tiongkok, yang dalam Baopuzi menyatakan ada tiga cacing (sanshi) di tubuh manusia yang pada malam kōshin berusaha kabur saat tuan rumahnya tidur untuk melaporkan dosa manusia kepada Dewa Langit sehingga umurnya dipendekkan.
statement.en: The custom goes back to the Chinese Taoist Ge Hong, who in the Baopuzi claimed there are three worms (sanshi) in the human body which on the night of kōshin try to escape while their hosts sleep and report the sins of mortals to the Celestial God, thereby shortening their lives.

claims.quote: It is to prevent the escape of the worms that the vigil, called shukōshin, is held.

statement.id: Berjaga semalaman yang disebut shukōshin diadakan untuk mencegah cacing-cacing itu lolos.
statement.en: The vigil, called shukōshin, is held to prevent the escape of the worms.

claims.quote: Today, with the original significance of the vigil having been lost, the purpose of the custom has widely shifted to that of an ordinary banquet.

statement.id: Kini, setelah makna asli berjaga itu hilang, tujuan kebiasaan ini banyak bergeser menjadi sekadar perjamuan biasa.
statement.en: Today, with the original significance of the vigil lost, the purpose of the custom has widely shifted to that of an ordinary banquet.

summary.id: Gulungan lama tidak memberi keterangan sehingga sifatnya hanya dugaan.
summary.en: The old scrolls give no explanation, so its nature is only speculation.

short_description.id: Shuzi atau Shūji adalah hewan legendaris Tiongkok kuno menyerupai harimau besar.
short_description.en: Shuzi, also called Shūji, is an ancient Chinese legendary animal resembling a large tiger.

long_description.id: Shuzi atau Shūji adalah hewan legendaris Tiongkok kuno menyerupai harimau besar. Tubuh dan ekornya digambarkan sangat besar serta panjang.
long_description.en: Shuzi, also called Shūji, is an ancient Chinese legendary animal resembling a large tiger. It is described with a very large body and a long tail.

long_description.id: Ia umumnya tidak memburu hewan hidup, tetapi menyerang harimau dan macan tutul. Versi cerita berbeda mengenai apakah hasil buruannya dimakan. Sancai Tuhui menghubungkan kemunculannya dengan kewibawaan penguasa yang meluas ke wilayah luar. Shuzi kadang disamakan dengan Zouyu sehingga ciri kedua makhluk saling bercampur.
long_description.en: It generally avoids hunting living animals but attacks tigers and leopards. Versions differ over whether it eats the animals it kills. The Sancai Tuhui connects its appearance with a ruler's authority extending to the surrounding peoples. Shuzi is sometimes identified with Zouyu, allowing their attributes to overlap.

long_description.id: Sumber-sumber Tiongkok klasik yang dihimpun dalam Gujin Tushu Jicheng memberi gambaran yang sejalan sekaligus beragam. 《三才圖會》 dan 《汲冢周書》 menyebut 酋耳 berekor panjang dan memakan harimau serta macan tutul, sedangkan 《朝野僉載》 menceritakan binatang mirip harimau yang membunuh seekor harimau tanpa memakan dagingnya. 《冊府元龜》 mencatat penangkapan 酋耳 yang bercorak macan tutul pada tahun 開元二十四.
long_description.en: Classical Chinese sources gathered in the Gujin tushu jicheng give a consistent yet varied picture. The 《三才圖會》 and the 《汲冢周書》 describe the 酋耳 as long-tailed and eating tigers and leopards, while the 《朝野僉載》 tells of a tiger-like beast that killed a tiger without eating its flesh. The 《冊府元龜》 records the capture of a leopard-marked 酋耳 in the year 開元二十四.

title.en: Recorded capture of a 酋耳

description.id: 《冊府元龜》 mencatat penangkapan binatang pertanda baik 酋耳 pada bulan ketiga tahun 開元二十四.
description.en: The 《冊府元龜》 records the capture of an auspicious 酋耳 in the third month of the year 開元二十四.

claims.quote: 『三才図会』では、王者の威勢が四夷に及んだ際に世に出現する獣であるとされている。『逸周書』「王会」の解では各地から贈られて来ためずらしい禽獣魚介のうちのひとつとして贈られていることが記されているが、これを献上している央林（『三才図会』では「英林山」とされている）については西の方角に属する地である以外にはあまり詳しく分かっていない。

claims.quote: 英林山有酋耳，周成王時曾獻之。尾長於身，食虎豹。 王者威及四夷，則此獸至。
claims.locator: 騶虞部彙考〈酋耳附〉, 《三才圖會》 section

statement.id: Kutipan dari 《三才圖會》 dalam Gujin Tushu Jicheng menyebut 酋耳 ada di gunung 英林山, pernah dipersembahkan pada masa Raja Cheng dari Zhou, berekor lebih panjang dari tubuhnya, memakan harimau dan macan tutul, dan muncul ketika wibawa raja menjangkau empat penjuru bangsa asing.
statement.en: The 《三才圖會》 passage in the Gujin tushu jicheng says the 酋耳 lives on Mount 英林山, was once presented in the time of King Cheng of Zhou, has a tail longer than its body, eats tigers and leopards, and appears when a ruler's might reaches the four barbarian quarters.

claims.quote: 《汲冢周書》王會解：「史林以酋耳。」酋耳者，身若虎豹，尾 長三尺，其身食虎豹。
claims.locator: 騶虞部彙考〈酋耳附〉, 《汲冢周書》王會解

statement.id: Kitab 《汲冢周書》 bab 王會解, sebagaimana dikutip, menyebut 酋耳 berbadan seperti harimau atau macan tutul, berekor tiga chi, dan memakan harimau serta macan tutul.
statement.en: The 《汲冢周書》, chapter 王會解, as quoted, says the 酋耳 has a body like a tiger or leopard, a tail of three chi, and eats tigers and leopards.

claims.quote: 天后時，涪州龍虎界多虎暴。有一獸似虎 而絕大，日正午，逐一虎直入人家，噬殺之，不食其肉。 自是縣界不復有虎矣。錄奏檢瑞圖，乃酋耳。
claims.locator: 騶虞部彙考〈酋耳附〉, 《朝野僉載》

statement.id: Menurut 《朝野僉載》, pada masa Permaisuri (天后) seekor binatang sangat besar mirip harimau mengejar dan membunuh seekor harimau tanpa memakan dagingnya; setelah dicocokkan dengan 瑞圖 (gambar pertanda baik), binatang itu dinyatakan sebagai 酋耳.
statement.en: According to 《朝野僉載》, in the time of the Empress (天后) a huge tiger-like beast chased and killed a tiger without eating its flesh; when checked against the 瑞圖 (auspicious omen illustrations), it was identified as a 酋耳.

claims.quote: 《冊府元龜》：「開元二十四年三月，獲瑞獸，酋耳形類虎， 尾長於身，有豹文，能食虎。」
claims.locator: 騶虞部彙考〈酋耳附〉, 《冊府元龜》

statement.id: Kutipan dari 《冊府元龜》 mencatat bahwa pada bulan ketiga tahun 開元二十四 seekor binatang pertanda baik ditangkap; 酋耳 itu berbentuk seperti harimau, berekor lebih panjang dari tubuh, bercorak macan tutul, dan mampu memakan harimau.
statement.en: A passage from the 《冊府元龜》 records that in the third month of the 24th year of Kaiyuan (開元二十四年) an auspicious beast was captured; the 酋耳 was tiger-like, had a tail longer than its body, leopard markings, and could eat tigers.

topic.en: Whether the 酋耳 eats its prey

summary.id: 《三才圖會》 dan 《汲冢周書》 (sebagaimana dikutip) menyebut 酋耳 memakan harimau dan macan tutul.
summary.en: The 《三才圖會》 and the 《汲冢周書》 (as quoted) say the 酋耳 eats tigers and leopards.

short_description.id: Skinfaxi, "surai bersinar", adalah kuda Dagr (Siang) dalam mitologi Nordik yang menarik kereta Siang melintasi langit, dan suainya menerangi langit serta bumi.
short_description.en: Skinfaxi, 'shining mane', is the horse of Dagr (Day) in Norse mythology that draws Day's chariot across the sky, its mane lighting up sky and earth.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Skinfaxi adalah kuda Dagr, sang Siang, sedangkan Hrímfaxi kuda Nótt, sang Malam. Namanya berarti "surai bersinar". Setiap hari Skinfaxi menarik kereta Dagr melintasi langit, dan suainya menerangi langit serta bumi di bawahnya.
long_description.en: In Norse mythology Skinfaxi is the horse of Dagr, the Day, while Hrímfaxi is that of Nótt, the Night. Its name means "shining mane". Every day Skinfaxi pulls Dagr's chariot across the sky, and its mane lights up the sky and the earth below.

long_description.id: Menurut satu uraian, Skinfaxe ditambatkan pada kereta Dag dan dikendarai melintasi langit setiap hari; surai dan ekornya bersinar seperti emas dan menerangi dunia. Dalam Gylfaginning di Den yngre Edda disebutkan bahwa kuda milik Dag bernama Skinfakse, dan dari suainya cahaya memancar ke seluruh udara dan bumi. Penyair Oehlenschläger menyebutnya dalam puisi Guldhornene.
long_description.en: In one account Skinfaxe is harnessed to Dag's chariot and driven across the sky each day; its mane and tail shine like gold and light the world. The Gylfaginning of the Younger Edda says the horse Dag has is called Skinfakse, and light shines over all the air and earth from its mane. The poet Oehlenschläger mentions it in his poem Guldhornene.

long_description.id: Terjemahan teks Edda yang terbuka menyebut Skinfaxi sebagai kuda yang menarik siang yang berkilau bagi manusia, kuda terbaik di mata para pahlawan, dengan surai yang menyala terang. Dalam salah satu terjemahan, All-father memberi Malam dan Siang, putranya, dua kuda dan dua kereta untuk berkeliling dunia secara bergantian, masing-masing dua belas jam; kuda Siang adalah Skinfaxi, yang suainya memancarkan cahaya ke bumi dan langit. Kuda Malam, Hrimfaxi, meneteskan buih dari kekangnya yang menjadi embun.
long_description.en: Open translations of the Edda texts describe Skinfaxi as the steed that draws the glittering day for men, the best of horses in the eyes of heroes, with a brightly burning mane. In one translation All-father gives Night and her son Day two horses and two cars to drive round the world in turn, twelve hours each; the horse of Day is Skinfaxi, whose mane sheds light over earth and heavens. Night's horse Hrimfaxi lets foam fall from his bit, which becomes dew.

claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Skinfaxi (Old Norse: [ˈskinˌfɑkse] ) and Hrímfaxi [ˈhriːmˌfɑkse] are the horses of Dagr (day) and Nótt (night). The names Skinfaxi and Hrímfaxi mean "shining mane" and "frost mane", respectively. Skinfaxi pulls Dagr's chariot across the sky every day and his mane lights up the sky and earth below.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Skinfaxi dan Hrímfaxi adalah kuda Dagr (siang) dan Nótt (malam); namanya berarti "surai bersinar" dan "surai berembun beku", dan Skinfaxi menarik kereta Dagr melintasi langit setiap hari sementara suainya menerangi langit dan bumi.
statement.en: In Norse mythology Skinfaxi and Hrímfaxi are the horses of Dagr (day) and Nótt (night); the names mean 'shining mane' and 'frost mane', and Skinfaxi pulls Dagr's chariot across the sky every day, its mane lighting sky and earth.

claims.quote: Skinfaxe (Oldnordisk: Skinfaxi, 'skinnende manke') er hesten, der i nordisk mytologi er forspændt Dags vogn. Han bliver på denne kørt hen over himlen hver dag. Hestens manke og hale skinner som guld og oplyser verden.

statement.id: Skinfaxe (Nordik Kuno Skinfaxi, "surai bersinar") adalah kuda yang ditambatkan pada kereta Dag dalam mitologi Nordik dan dikendarai melintasi langit setiap hari; surai dan ekornya bersinar seperti emas dan menerangi dunia.
statement.en: Skinfaxe (Old Norse Skinfaxi, 'shining mane') is the horse harnessed to Dag's chariot in Norse mythology, driven across the sky each day; its mane and tail shine like gold and light up the world.

claims.quote: Skinfakse (Norrønt: Skinfaxi, skinnende man) er i norrøn mytologi den hesten Dag rir på over himmelen hver dag. Skinfakse nevnes i Gylvaginning i Den yngre Edda: Den hesten Dag har heiter Skinfakse og det lyser over all lufta og jorda frå fakset hans

statement.id: Skinfakse (Nordik Kuno Skinfaxi, "surai bersinar") adalah kuda yang ditunggangi Dag melintasi langit setiap hari; dalam Gylfaginning di Den yngre Edda disebut: "Kuda milik Dag bernama Skinfakse, dan cahaya memancar ke seluruh udara dan bumi dari suainya."
statement.en: Skinfakse (Old Norse Skinfaxi, 'shining mane') is the horse Day rides across the sky daily; the Gylfaginning of the Younger Edda says: 'The horse Dag has is called Skinfakse, and light shines over all the air and earth from his mane.'

claims.quote: Oehlenschlägers digt Guldhornene omtaler himmelhestene: "Hrymfaxe den sorte puster og dukker og i Havet sig begraver. Morgenens Porte Delling oplukker, og Skinfaxe traver

statement.id: Puisi Oehlenschläger Guldhornene menyebut kuda-kuda langit: Hrymfaxe yang hitam menyelam ke laut, Delling membuka gerbang pagi, dan Skinfaxe pun berderap.
statement.en: Oehlenschläger's poem Guldhornene mentions the sky horses: black Hrymfaxe sinks into the sea, Delling opens the gates of morning, and Skinfaxe trots forth.

claims.quote: Hesten Hrymfaxe er forspændt vognen, der bærer månen over himlen om natten.

statement.id: Kuda Hrymfaxe ditambatkan pada kereta yang membawa bulan melintasi langit di malam hari.
statement.en: The horse Hrymfaxe is harnessed to the chariot that carries the moon across the sky at night.

claims.quote: Skinfaxi is he, the steed who for men The glittering day doth draw; The best of horses to heroes he seems, And brightly his mane doth burn.

statement.id: Dalam terjemahan puisi Edda ini, Skinfaxi adalah kuda yang menarik siang yang berkilau bagi manusia; bagi para pahlawan ia tampak sebagai kuda terbaik, dan suainya menyala terang.
statement.en: In this translated Edda poem, Skinfaxi is the steed who draws the glittering day for men; he seems the best of horses to heroes, and his mane burns brightly.

claims.quote: Hrimfaxi name they the steed that anew Brings night for the noble gods; Each morning foam from his bit there falls, And thence come the dews in the dales.

statement.id: Hrimfaxi adalah kuda yang membawa malam bagi para dewa mulia; tiap pagi buih jatuh dari kekangnya dan menjadi embun di lembah.
statement.en: Hrimfaxi is the steed that brings night for the noble gods; each morning foam falls from his bit and becomes the dews in the dales.

claims.quote: Then took All-father, Night, and Day, her son, and gave them two horses and two cars, and set them up in the heavens that they might drive successively one after the other, each in twelve hours' time, round the world.

statement.id: All-father memberi Malam dan Siang, putranya, dua kuda dan dua kereta, lalu menempatkan mereka di langit agar bergantian berkeliling dunia, masing-masing dua belas jam.
statement.en: All-father gave Night and Day, her son, two horses and two cars and set them in the heavens to drive in turn round the world, each for twelve hours.

claims.quote: The horse made use of by Day is named Skinfaxi, from whose mane is shed light over the earth and the heavens.

statement.id: Kuda yang dipakai Siang bernama Skinfaxi; dari suainya cahaya memancar ke bumi dan langit.
statement.en: The horse Day uses is named Skinfaxi, from whose mane light is shed over the earth and the heavens.

claims.quote: She then espoused Delling, of the Æsir race, and their son was Day, (Dagr) a child light and beauteous like his father.

statement.en: Night then married Delling of the Æsir race, and their son was Day (Dagr), a child light and beautiful like his father.

claims.quote: Glath ("Joyous"): identified in the Skaldskaparmal with Skinfaxi, the horse of the day; cf. Vafthruthnismol, 12.

statement.en: The translator's note says Glath ("Joyous") is identified in the Skaldskaparmal with Skinfaxi, the horse of the day.

statement.en: The translator's notes gloss Skinfaxi as "Shining-Mane" and Hrimfaxi as "Frosty-Mane".

short_description.id: Snallygaster adalah makhluk campuran burung dan reptil dari cerita rakyat imigran Jerman di Frederick County, Maryland [snallygaster-c01].
short_description.en: The snallygaster is a bird-reptile chimera from the folklore of German immigrants in Frederick County, Maryland [snallygaster-c01].

long_description.id: Snallygaster adalah makhluk campuran burung dan reptil dari cerita rakyat imigran Jerman di Frederick County, Maryland [snallygaster-c01]. Kisah awal menyebutnya Schneller Geist, "hantu cepat" [snallygaster-c03]. Ia berparuh logam bergigi tajam [snallygaster-c04] dan menukik dari langit untuk membawa korbannya [snallygaster-c05]. Legendanya dihidupkan lagi oleh surat kabar pada awal abad ke-20 [snallygaster-c02].
long_description.en: The snallygaster is a bird-reptile chimera from the folklore of German immigrants in Frederick County, Maryland [snallygaster-c01]. Early accounts call it Schneller Geist, "quick ghost" [snallygaster-c03]. It has a metallic, sharp-toothed beak [snallygaster-c04] and swoops from the sky to carry off victims [snallygaster-c05]. Newspapers revived its legend in the early 20th century [snallygaster-c02].

long_description.id: Laporan tentang snallygaster sudah ada sejak 1730-an [snallygaster-c11], dan catatan abad ke-18 para pemukim Jerman menyebutnya Schneller Geist atau hantu cepat yang menerkam mangsanya dengan cepat [snallygaster-c12]. Kisah-kisah paling awal menyebut ia menghisap darah korban [snallygaster-c06] dan konon bertentakel seperti gurita [snallygaster-c07]. Bintang bersudut tujuh yang masih terlihat di lumbung setempat dipercaya menjaganya tetap jauh [snallygaster-c06].
long_description.en: Reports of the snallygaster go back to the 1730s [snallygaster-c11], and eighteenth-century accounts by German settlers call it a Schneller Geist, a quick ghost that rapidly pounced on its prey [snallygaster-c12]. The earliest stories say it sucked the blood of its victims [snallygaster-c06] and was said to have octopus-like tentacles [snallygaster-c07]. Seven-pointed stars still seen on local barns were believed to keep it away [snallygaster-c06].

long_description.id: Surat kabar sepanjang Februari dan Maret 1909 melaporkan perjumpaan dengan binatang bersayap sangat besar, berparuh panjang, bercakar seperti kait baja, dan bermata satu di dahi [snallygaster-c08]. Belakangan terungkap laporan itu bagian dari tipuan untuk menaikkan jumlah pembaca [snallygaster-c09]. Penampakan awal dikaitkan dengan South Mountain, Braddock Heights, dan Middletown Valley [snallygaster-c10]. Pada Desember 1932 sebuah surat kabar memberitakan kematiannya di alat penyulingan minuman keras ilegal [snallygaster-c13].
long_description.en: Newspapers throughout February and March 1909 reported encounters with a beast with enormous wings, a long bill, claws like steel hooks and one eye in its forehead [snallygaster-c08]. The reports were later exposed as a hoax meant to boost readership [snallygaster-c09]. Early sightings were associated with South Mountain, Braddock Heights and the Middletown Valley [snallygaster-c10]. In December 1932 a newspaper reported its death at a moonshine still [snallygaster-c13].

claims.quote: The snallygaster is a bird-reptile chimera originating in the folklore of early German immigrants who settled in the region of what is now Frederick County, Maryland.

statement.id: Snallygaster adalah makhluk campuran burung dan reptil dari cerita rakyat imigran Jerman awal di wilayah yang kini Frederick County, Maryland.
statement.en: The snallygaster is a bird-reptile chimera from the folklore of early German immigrants in what is now Frederick County, Maryland.

claims.quote: In the early 20th century, legends of the Snallygaster were revived through sensationalistic newspaper reports

statement.id: Pada awal abad ke-20, legendanya dihidupkan kembali oleh laporan surat kabar yang sensasional.
statement.en: In the early 20th century its legends were revived by sensational newspaper reports.

claims.quote: Early accounts describe the community being terrorized by a monster called a Schneller Geist, meaning "quick ghost" in German.

statement.id: Kisah awal menyebut masyarakat diteror monster bernama Schneller Geist, yang dalam bahasa Jerman berarti "hantu cepat".
statement.en: Early accounts describe a monster called Schneller Geist, "quick ghost" in German.

claims.quote: The snallygaster was described as being half-reptile and half-bird, possessing a metallic beak lined with razor-sharp teeth.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan setengah reptil setengah burung, berparuh logam dengan gigi setajam silet.
statement.en: It was described as half reptile, half bird, with a metallic beak lined with razor-sharp teeth.

claims.quote: The snallygaster was rumored to swoop silently from the sky to pick up and carry off its victims.

statement.id: Ia konon menukik diam-diam dari langit untuk menyambar dan membawa pergi korbannya.
statement.en: It reportedly swooped silently from the sky to carry off its victims.

claims.quote: The earliest stories claim that this monster sucked the blood of its victims. Seven-pointed stars, which reputedly kept the snallygaster at bay, can still be seen painted on local barns.

statement.id: Kisah-kisah paling awal menyebut monster ini menghisap darah korbannya; bintang bersudut tujuh, yang konon menjaga snallygaster tetap jauh, masih terlihat dicat di lumbung setempat.
statement.en: The earliest stories claim the monster sucked the blood of its victims; seven-pointed stars, which reputedly kept the snallygaster at bay, can still be seen painted on local barns.

claims.quote: It was also said to have octopus-like tentacles.

statement.id: Makhluk ini juga dikatakan memiliki tentakel seperti gurita.
statement.en: It was also said to have octopus-like tentacles.

claims.quote: Newspaper accounts throughout February and March 1909 describe encounters between local residents and a beast with "enormous wings, a long pointed bill, claws like steel hooks, and an eye in the center of its forehead."

statement.id: Laporan surat kabar sepanjang Februari dan Maret 1909 menggambarkan perjumpaan warga dengan binatang bersayap sangat besar, berparuh panjang runcing, bercakar seperti kait baja, dan bermata satu di tengah dahi.
statement.en: Newspaper accounts throughout February and March 1909 describe encounters between residents and a beast with enormous wings, a long pointed bill, claws like steel hooks and an eye in the center of its forehead.

claims.quote: It was later revealed that these reports were part of a hoax perpetrated by Middletown Valley Register editor George C. Rhoderick and reporter Ralph S. Wolfe in an attempt to increase readership.

statement.id: Belakangan terungkap bahwa laporan-laporan itu bagian dari tipuan editor Middletown Valley Register George C. Rhoderick dan reporter Ralph S. Wolfe untuk menaikkan jumlah pembaca.
statement.en: It was later revealed that these reports were part of a hoax by Middletown Valley Register editor George C. Rhoderick and reporter Ralph S. Wolfe to increase readership.

claims.quote: Early sightings led to a particular association with the Frederick County areas of South Mountain, Braddock Heights, and the Middletown Valley.

statement.id: Penampakan awal mengaitkan makhluk ini terutama dengan kawasan South Mountain, Braddock Heights, dan Middletown Valley di Frederick County.
statement.en: Early sightings led to a particular association with the Frederick County areas of South Mountain, Braddock Heights and the Middletown Valley.

claims.quote: Reports of the Snallygaster, a strange beast prowling the woods of Frederick County, have been made since the 1730s, making it one of Maryland’s oldest legends.

statement.id: Laporan tentang Snallygaster, binatang aneh yang berkeliaran di hutan Frederick County, sudah ada sejak 1730-an sehingga menjadi salah satu legenda tertua Maryland.
statement.en: Reports of the Snallygaster, a strange beast prowling the woods of Frederick County, have been made since the 1730s, making it one of Maryland's oldest legends.

claims.quote: 18th-century accounts by the early German settlers refer to the beast as a Schneller Geist or quick ghost that rapidly pounced upon its unsuspecting prey.

statement.id: Catatan abad ke-18 para pemukim Jerman awal menyebut binatang itu Schneller Geist atau "hantu cepat" yang menerkam mangsanya yang tak curiga dengan cepat.
statement.en: Eighteenth-century accounts by the early German settlers refer to the beast as a Schneller Geist, or quick ghost, that rapidly pounced upon its unsuspecting prey.

claims.quote: Then, in December 1932, the Hagerstown Morning Herald reported on the death of the Snallygaster. It was purportedly lured to a moonshine still in Frog Hollow in Washington County and was overcome by the noxious fumes and drowned in the alcoholic vat.

statement.id: Pada Desember 1932, Hagerstown Morning Herald memberitakan kematian Snallygaster: konon ia dipancing ke alat penyulingan minuman keras ilegal di Frog Hollow, Washington County, dan tewas karena asapnya lalu tenggelam di bak alkohol.
statement.en: In December 1932 the Hagerstown Morning Herald reported the death of the Snallygaster, purportedly lured to a moonshine still in Frog Hollow in Washington County, overcome by the noxious fumes and drowned in the alcoholic vat.

claims.quote: Some have suggested that the accounts beginning in 1909 were a veiled attempt at scaring away would be ne’er-do-wells from Middletown and the surrounding region.

statement.id: Ada yang menduga laporan sejak 1909 adalah upaya terselubung menakut-nakuti calon pembuat onar agar menjauh dari Middletown dan sekitarnya.
statement.en: Some have suggested that the accounts beginning in 1909 were a veiled attempt at scaring away would-be ne'er-do-wells from Middletown and the surrounding region.

claims.quote: Others have explained that the original letter from T.C. Harbaugh is the explanation – as Thomas Chalmers Harbaugh was a native of Middletown and an accomplished author with a passion for the area’s history and culture.

statement.id: Yang lain menjelaskan bahwa surat asli T.C. Harbaugh-lah penyebabnya, karena Thomas Chalmers Harbaugh adalah warga asli Middletown dan penulis mumpuni yang mencintai sejarah dan budaya kawasan itu.
statement.en: Others explain that the original letter from T.C. Harbaugh is the explanation, as Thomas Chalmers Harbaugh was a native of Middletown and an accomplished author with a passion for the area's history and culture.

summary.id: Tipuan editor dan reporter untuk menaikkan jumlah pembaca.
summary.en: A hoax by an editor and reporter to increase readership.

summary.en: A veiled attempt to scare away would-be ne'er-do-wells.

summary.en: It came from T.C. Harbaugh's letter; he was a Middletown native and author fond of the area's history.

short_description.id: Tangaroa adalah atua (dewa) agung laut, danau, sungai, dan makhluk yang hidup di dalamnya, terutama ikan, dalam mitologi Māori.
short_description.en: In Māori mythology Tangaroa is the principal atua (god) of the sea, of lakes and rivers, and of the creatures that inhabit them, fish above all.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Māori, Tangaroa (Takaroa dalam dialek South Island) adalah atua agung laut, danau, sungai, dan makhluk yang hidup di dalamnya, terutama ikan. Sebagai Tangaroa-whakamau-tai ia mengendalikan pasang surut, dan ia kadang digambarkan sebagai paus. Shortland mencatat Tangaroa sebagai leluhur ikan dan pounamu, dan sumber lain mencatat ia ayah banyak makhluk laut.
long_description.en: In Māori mythology Tangaroa (called Takaroa in the South Island dialect) is the principal atua of the sea, of lakes and rivers, and of the creatures that inhabit them, fish above all. As Tangaroa-whakamau-tai he controls the tides, and he is at times pictured as a whale. Shortland records Tangaroa as the ancestor of fish and of pounamu, and another source describes him as father of many sea creatures.

long_description.id: Tangaroa adalah putra Ranginui dan Papatūānuku, Langit dan Bumi. Setelah bergabung dengan saudara-saudaranya Rongo, Tū, Haumia, dan Tāne memisahkan orang tua mereka secara paksa, ia diserang saudaranya Tāwhirimātea, atua badai, dan terpaksa bersembunyi di laut. Pertentangannya dengan Tāne Mahuta menandakan bahwa orang Māori memandang lautan dan daratan sebagai ranah yang berlawanan, sehingga persembahan perlu diberikan kepada Tangaroa sebelum orang pergi ke laut.
long_description.en: Tangaroa is a son of Ranginui and Papatūānuku, Sky and Earth. He joined his brothers Rongo, Tū, Haumia and Tāne in forcing their parents apart, and was then attacked by his brother Tāwhirimātea, atua of storms, and driven to hide in the sea. His rivalry with Tāne Mahuta shows that the Māori saw the ocean and land as opposed realms, so offerings must be made to Tangaroa before people go to sea.

long_description.id: Tradisi mencatat versi lain. Versi Kāi Tahu menyebut Takaroa putra Temoretu dan menjadikan Papatūānuku istrinya, sedangkan Shortland dan Dixon mencatat kisah tentang Tangaroa yang menombak paha Rangi. Dalam kisah Ihenga yang dicatat Shortland, Tangaroa mengirim belut ketika dipanggil lewat karakia.
long_description.en: The tradition preserves other versions. The Kāi Tahu version makes Takaroa the son of Temoretu and Papatūānuku his wife, while Shortland and Dixon record tales of Tangaroa spearing Rangi in the thigh. In the story of Ihenga recorded by Shortland, Tangaroa sends eels when invoked through a karakia.

long_description.id: Di luar tradisi Māori, Tangaroa dikenal di Cook Islands; di Rarotonga ia dewa laut dan kesuburan dan yang terpenting di antara dewa-dewa departemental, sedangkan di Manihiki ia adalah dewa api tempat Māui mencuri api. Dalam tradisi Western Polynesian seperti Samoa dan Tonga, Tangaloa dianggap dewa tertinggi dan pencipta, sedangkan di Hawaiʻi dewa samudra disebut Kanaloa. Dixon juga memuat keterangan plat tentang patung kayu Tangaroa Upao Vahu, dewa laut yang digambarkan sedang menciptakan dewa-dewa lain dan manusia.
long_description.en: Beyond Māori tradition, Tangaroa is known in the Cook Islands; in Rarotonga he is the god of sea and fertility and the foremost of the departmental gods, while in Manihiki he is the fire deity Māui steals from. Western Polynesian traditions such as those of Samoa and Tonga treat Tangaloa as the supreme creator god, whereas in Hawaiʻi the ocean god is called Kanaloa. Dixon also includes a plate caption for a wooden figure of Tangaroa Upao Vahu, a sea-deity shown creating other gods and men.

cultural_context.id: Persembahan perlu diberikan kepada Tangaroa sebelum orang pergi ke laut untuk menangkap ikan atau bepergian, karena mereka memasuki ranah musuh Tāne Mahuta.
cultural_context.en: Offerings need to be made to Tangaroa before people go to sea to fish or travel, because they enter the realm of Tāne Mahuta's enemy.

note.id: Tangaroa sepadan (kognat) dengan Tagaloa dalam bahasa Samoa.
note.en: Tangaroa is cognate with Tagaloa in Samoan.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa orang Māori memandang laut dan daratan sebagai dua ranah yang berlawanan, dan apa akibatnya bagi perjalanan di laut?
learning_questions.en: Why did the Māori see sea and land as opposed realms, and what follows from that for travel at sea?

sources.title: Oceanic [Mythology] (The Mythology of All Races, vol. 9)
sources.author: Roland B. Dixon

claims.quote: Tangaroa (Māori; Takaroa in the South Island dialect; cognate with Tagaloa in Sāmoan) is the great atua of the sea, lakes, rivers, and creatures that live within them, especially fish, in Māori mythology.

statement.id: Tangaroa adalah atua laut, danau, sungai, dan ikan dalam mitologi Māori.
statement.en: Tangaroa is the great atua of the sea, lakes, rivers, and fish in Māori mythology.

claims.quote: As Tangaroa-whakamau-tai, he exercises control over the tides. He is sometimes depicted as a whale.

statement.id: Sebagai Tangaroa-whakamau-tai ia mengatur pasang surut dan terkadang digambarkan sebagai paus.
statement.en: As Tangaroa-whakamau-tai he governs tides and is sometimes depicted as a whale.

claims.quote: Tangaroa is son of Ranginui and Papatūānuku, Sky and Earth. After joining his brothers Rongo, Tū, Haumia, and Tāne in the forcible separation of their parents, he is attacked by his brother Tāwhirimātea, the atua of storms, and forced to hide in the sea.

statement.id: Tangaroa adalah putra Ranginui dan Papatūānuku yang bersembunyi di laut akibat serangan Tāwhirimātea.
statement.en: Tangaroa is son of Sky and Earth who hid in the sea when attacked by storm god Tāwhirimātea.

claims.quote: Tangaroa is the father of many sea creatures. Tangaroa's son, Punga, has two children, Ikatere, the ancestor of fish, and Tū-te-wehiwehi (or Tū-te-wanawana), the ancestor of reptiles.

statement.id: Tangaroa adalah ayah dari banyak makhluk laut. Punga, putra Tangaroa, memiliki dua anak: Ikatere, leluhur ikan, dan Tū-te-wehiwehi (atau Tū-te-wanawana), leluhur reptil.
statement.en: Tangaroa is the father of many sea creatures. His son Punga has two children: Ikatere, the ancestor of fish, and Tū-te-wehiwehi (or Tū-te-wanawana), the ancestor of reptiles.

claims.quote: The contention between Tangaroa and Tāne Mahuta, the father of birds, trees, and humans, is an indication that the Māori thought of the ocean and the land as opposed realms.

statement.id: Pertentangan antara Tangaroa dan Tāne Mahuta, ayah burung, pohon, dan manusia, menandakan bahwa orang Māori memandang lautan dan daratan sebagai ranah yang berlawanan.
statement.en: The contention between Tangaroa and Tāne Mahuta, the father of birds, trees and humans, indicates that the Māori thought of the ocean and the land as opposed realms.

claims.quote: When people go out to sea to fish or to travel, they are, in effect, representatives of Tāne Mahuta, entering the realm of Tāne Mahuta's enemy. For this reason, offerings need to be made to Tangaroa before any such expedition.

statement.id: Ketika orang pergi ke laut untuk menangkap ikan atau bepergian, mereka pada dasarnya mewakili Tāne Mahuta yang memasuki ranah musuh Tāne Mahuta. Karena itu, persembahan perlu diberikan kepada Tangaroa sebelum ekspedisi semacam itu.
statement.en: When people go out to sea to fish or travel, they are in effect representatives of Tāne Mahuta entering the realm of his enemy. For this reason, offerings need to be made to Tangaroa before any such expedition.

claims.quote: In Rarotonga, Tangaroa is god of the sea and fertility. He is the most important of all the departmental gods.

statement.id: Di Rarotonga, Tangaroa adalah dewa laut dan kesuburan, serta yang terpenting di antara semua dewa departemental.
statement.en: In Rarotonga, Tangaroa is god of the sea and fertility and the most important of all the departmental gods.

claims.quote: Tangaloa is one of the oldest Polynesian deities. In Western Polynesian traditions such as Samoa and Tonga, Tangaloa is considered the supreme and creator deity. In Eastern Polynesian cultures, however, he is usually considered of equal status to Tāne and thus not supreme.

statement.id: Tangaloa adalah salah satu dewa Polinesia tertua. Dalam tradisi Polinesia Barat seperti Samoa dan Tonga, Tangaloa dianggap dewa tertinggi dan pencipta; dalam budaya Polinesia Timur ia biasanya dianggap setara dengan Tāne dan karena itu tidak tertinggi.
statement.en: Tangaloa is one of the oldest Polynesian deities. In Western Polynesian traditions such as Samoa and Tonga he is considered the supreme and creator deity; in Eastern Polynesian cultures he is usually considered equal in status to Tāne and thus not supreme.

claims.quote: The Kāi Tahu version of the origin of Takaroa maintains that he is the son of Temoretu and that Papatūānuku is his wife. Papatūānuku commits adultery with Rakinui while Takaroa is away, and in the resulting battle on the beach, Takaroa's spear pierces Rakinui through both his thighs. Papatūānuku then marries Rakinui.

statement.id: Versi Kāi Tahu tentang asal Takaroa menyatakan bahwa ia putra Temoretu dan Papatūānuku adalah istrinya. Papatūānuku berzina dengan Rakinui saat Takaroa pergi; dalam pertempuran di pantai, tombak Takaroa menembus kedua paha Rakinui, lalu Papatūānuku menikah dengan Rakinui.
statement.en: The Kāi Tahu version of Takaroa's origin holds that he is the son of Temoretu and that Papatūānuku is his wife. Papatūānuku commits adultery with Rakinui while Takaroa is away; in the battle on the beach Takaroa's spear pierces Rakinui through both thighs, and Papatūānuku then marries Rakinui.

claims.quote: In Hawaiʻi, the god of ocean, healing, and long travels is called Kanaloa, the cognate term in the Hawaiian language

statement.id: Di Hawaiʻi, dewa samudra, penyembuhan, dan perjalanan jauh disebut Kanaloa, istilah sepadan (kognat) dalam bahasa Hawaii.
statement.en: In Hawaiʻi, the god of the ocean, healing and long travels is called Kanaloa, the cognate term in the Hawaiian language.

claims.quote: Tangaroa was ancestor of Fish and the Pounamu, which is classed with fish by the Maori.

statement.id: Menurut Shortland, Tangaroa adalah leluhur ikan dan pounamu, yang oleh orang Māori digolongkan bersama ikan.
statement.en: According to Shortland, Tangaroa was the ancestor of fish and of the pounamu, which the Maori classed with fish.

claims.quote: Tangaroa took to wife Te Anu-matao (=the chilly cold)

statement.id: Menurut Shortland, Tangaroa memperistri Te Anu-matao (= dingin yang menusuk).
statement.en: According to Shortland, Tangaroa took Te Anu-matao (= the chilly cold) as his wife.

claims.quote: Then Ihenga threw into the water some of his inanga. ... Then he called on Tangaroa, and Tangaroa sent the eels. The mode of calling was a karakia.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Ihenga yang dicatat Shortland, ketika memanggil Tangaroa, Tangaroa mengirim belut; cara memanggilnya adalah dengan karakia (mantra).
statement.en: In the story of Ihenga recorded by Shortland, when he called on Tangaroa, Tangaroa sent the eels; the mode of calling was a karakia (incantation).

claims.quote: Tangaroa warded it off, and it missed him. Then Tangaroa made a thrust at Rangi, and pierced him quite through the thigh, and he fell.

statement.id: Dalam versi yang dicatat Shortland, Tangaroa menangkis tusukan itu hingga meleset, lalu menusuk Rangi menembus pahanya hingga ia jatuh.
statement.en: In the version recorded by Shortland, Tangaroa warded off the thrust so that it missed him, then thrust at Rangi and pierced him quite through the thigh, so that he fell.

claims.quote: which Powers are regarded by the Maori as their own primitive ancestors, and are invoked in their karakia by all the Maori race; for we find the names of Rangi, Rongo, Tangaroa, &c., mentioned as Atua or Gods of the Maori of the Sandwich Islands and other Islands of the Pacific inhabited by the same race.

statement.id: Menurut Shortland, kekuatan-kekuatan alam personifikasi itu dianggap orang Māori sebagai leluhur purba mereka dan dipanggil dalam karakia oleh seluruh bangsa Māori; nama Rangi, Rongo, Tangaroa, dan lainnya disebut sebagai Atua atau dewa orang Māori di Kepulauan Sandwich dan pulau-pulau Pasifik lain yang dihuni ras yang sama.
statement.en: According to Shortland, these personified Powers of Nature are regarded by the Maori as their primitive ancestors and invoked in karakia by the whole Maori race; the names of Rangi, Rongo, Tangaroa and others are mentioned as Atua or gods of the Maori of the Sandwich Islands and other Pacific islands inhabited by the same race.

claims.quote: Lo, next Tangaroa, the god and father of fish and reptiles rises up, that he may rend apart the heavens and the earth, but he rends them not apart.
claims.locator: Myths of origins (account quoted from Grey)

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang dikutip Dixon, Tangaroa, dewa dan ayah ikan serta reptil, bangkit untuk memisahkan langit dan bumi tetapi tidak berhasil.
statement.en: In the account Dixon quotes, Tangaroa, the god and father of fish and reptiles, rises up to rend heaven and earth apart but does not succeed.

claims.quote: Now Papa-tu-a-nuku was the wife of Tangaroa, but had deserted him, coming to Rangi while Tangaroa was away. When the latter returned and learned of his wife's faithlessness, he attacked Rangi and speared him in the thigh

statement.id: Menurut Dixon, Papa-tu-a-nuku adalah istri Tangaroa tetapi meninggalkannya dan datang kepada Rangi saat Tangaroa pergi; ketika Tangaroa kembali dan mengetahui ketidaksetiaan istrinya, ia menyerang Rangi dan menombak pahanya.
statement.en: According to Dixon, Papa-tu-a-nuku was Tangaroa's wife but deserted him and came to Rangi while Tangaroa was away; when he returned and learned of her faithlessness, he attacked Rangi and speared him in the thigh.

claims.quote: In some of the Cook Islands, he has similar roles, though in Manihiki, he is the fire deity that Māui steals from, which in Māori mythology is instead Mahuika, a goddess of fire.

statement.id: Di sebagian Kepulauan Cook ia memiliki peran serupa, meskipun di Manihiki ia adalah dewa api tempat Māui mencuri api, yang dalam mitologi Māori justru adalah Mahuika, dewi api.
statement.en: In some of the Cook Islands he has similar roles, though in Manihiki he is the fire deity that Māui steals from, whereas in Māori mythology that figure is Mahuika, a goddess of fire.

claims.quote: Wooden figure of Tangaroa Upao Vahu,a sea-deity, represented in the act of creating other gods and men.

statement.id: Keterangan plat dalam buku Dixon menyebut sebuah patung kayu Tangaroa Upao Vahu, dewa laut, yang digambarkan sedang menciptakan dewa-dewa lain dan manusia.
statement.en: A plate caption in Dixon's book describes a wooden figure of Tangaroa Upao Vahu, a sea-deity, shown in the act of creating other gods and men.

summary.en: General tradition: Tangaroa is a son of Ranginui and Papatūānuku.

short_description.id: Teju Jagua adalah kadal raksasa berkepala anjing, putra pertama Tau dan Kerana dalam mitologi Guaraní. Ia dianggap penguasa gua serta pelindung buah dan harta terpendam.
short_description.en: Teju Jagua is a giant dog-headed lizard, first son of Tau and Kerana in Guaraní mythology. He is considered lord of the caves and protector of fruit and buried treasure.

long_description.id: Teju Jagua adalah putra pertama Tau dan Kerana, salah satu dari tujuh monster legendaris mitologi Guaraní. Ia digambarkan sebagai kadal raksasa berkepala anjing; menurut ensiklopedia daring kepalanya tujuh dengan mata yang menyemburkan api, sedangkan sebagian versi menyebut hanya satu kepala anjing raksasa. Semua versi sepakat bahwa kemampuannya bergerak terbatas, dan keturunan Tau konon dikutuk berwujud cacat dan mengerikan.
long_description.en: Teju Jagua is the first son of Tau and Kerana, one of the seven legendary monsters of Guaraní mythology. He is described as a giant lizard with a dog's head; according to the online encyclopedia he has seven heads and eyes that shoot fire, while some versions say only one giant dog head. All versions agree that his ability to move is limited, and Tau's descendants were said to be cursed with a deformed and monstrous appearance.

long_description.id: Ia dianggap penguasa gua dan pelindung buah. Sarangnya konon berada di salah satu jurang di bukit legendaris Yaguarón, dan penduduk setempat menganggap tugasnya menjaga pohon dan buah. Ia juga dipandang sebagai monster yang melindungi harta tersembunyi bangsa Guaraní; kulitnya berkilau karena berguling di debu emas.
long_description.en: He is considered lord of the caves and protector of fruit. His lair was said to be in one of the abysses of the legendary Yaguarón hill, and the locals saw his mission as looking after trees and fruit. He is also seen as the monster who protected the hidden treasures of the Guaraní people; his skin shone from rolling in gold dust.

long_description.id: Sumber-sumber berbeda tentang sifat dan makanannya. Ensiklopedia daring menyebut keganasannya diredam oleh pilihan Tupã sehingga ia tenang dan tidak berbahaya, meski ditakuti karena tatapan apinya, dan ia makan buah serta madu pemberian saudaranya Yasy Yateré. Sumber museum mencatat bahwa banyak orang percaya ia membawa korban ke gua untuk melahapnya, sementara penduduk Yaguarón percaya ia hanya makan buah dan madu liar.
long_description.en: Sources differ on his nature and diet. The online encyclopedia says his ferocity was tempered by Tupã's choice so that he is calm and harmless, though feared for his fiery gaze, and that he eats fruit and honey given by his brother Yasy Yateré. The museum source records that many believe he carried victims to the cavern to devour them, while the people of Yaguarón believed he ate only fruit and wild honey.

statement.en: The local natives regarded him as the master of the grottoes, whose mission was to look after and protect trees and fruit.

claims.quote: También se le consideraba el monstruo que protegía los tesoros ocultos de la raza guaraní. Por haberse revolcado sobre polvo aurífero (Itaju), su piel brillaba como oro y piedras preciosas.

statement.id: Ia juga dianggap monster yang melindungi harta tersembunyi bangsa Guaraní; karena berguling di atas debu emas (Itaju), kulitnya berkilau seperti emas dan batu mulia.
statement.en: He was also considered the monster who protected the hidden treasures of the Guaraní people; having rolled on gold dust (Itaju), his skin shone like gold and precious stones.

claims.quote: de tarde en tarde, en época de verano, su hermanito JASY JATERE le llevaba

statement.id: Dari waktu ke waktu pada musim panas, adik kecilnya Jasy Jatere membawanya.
statement.en: From time to time in summer, his little brother Jasy Jatere took him along.

claims.quote: El escritor y estudioso Paulo Carvalho Neto nos dice en su libro Folklore del Paraguay que en 1933 Ramón I. Cardozo recogió en Villa Rica un relato de TEJU JAGUA

statement.id: Menurut penulis dan peneliti Paulo Carvalho Neto dalam bukunya Folklore del Paraguay, pada 1933 Ramón I. Cardozo mencatat di Villa Rica sebuah kisah tentang Teju Jagua.
statement.en: According to the writer and scholar Paulo Carvalho Neto in his book Folklore del Paraguay, in 1933 Ramón I. Cardozo collected in Villa Rica a tale about Teju Jagua.

claims.quote: llegó al Paraguay el portugués don Luis Home y se estableció en Villa Rica del Espíritu Santo

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, orang Portugis bernama don Luis Home tiba di Paraguay dan menetap di Villa Rica del Espíritu Santo.
statement.en: In the tale, the Portuguese don Luis Home arrived in Paraguay and settled in Villa Rica del Espíritu Santo.

claims.quote: Ya no faltó quien dijera que el purutue D. Luis tenía oculto en el laberinto de su castillo a TEJU JAGUA, monstruo devorador de hombres e invencible poder destructivo. Lo tenía cebándolo con carne humana para utilizarlo, algún día, en la consecución de quién sabe qué plan.

statement.id: Muncul orang yang mengatakan bahwa D. Luis menyembunyikan Teju Jagua, monster pelahap manusia berkekuatan perusak tak terkalahkan, di labirin istananya dan memberinya makan daging manusia untuk dipakai suatu hari.
statement.en: Some said that D. Luis kept Teju Jagua, a man-devouring monster of invincible destructive power, hidden in the labyrinth of his castle, fattening him on human flesh to use him one day for some unknown plan.

claims.quote: Pronto esta leyenda tomó cuerpo y vida. Todo el mundo la creyó a pie juntillas, hasta el extremo de que nadie osaba pasar de noche por las proximidades de la casa de D. Luis

statement.id: Legenda itu segera hidup; semua orang memercayainya sampai tak seorang pun berani lewat malam hari di dekat rumah D. Luis.
statement.en: The legend soon took shape and life; everyone believed it to the point that nobody dared pass near D. Luis's house at night.

short_description.id: Tenghuang merupakan makhluk pembawa pertanda baik dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Tenghuang is an auspicious creature in Chinese mythology.

long_description.id: Tenghuang merupakan makhluk pembawa pertanda baik dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Artikel menyebut kemunculannya dalam Shan Hai Jing.
long_description.en: Tenghuang is an auspicious creature in Chinese mythology. Tenghuang is mentioned in the Shanhaijing.

long_description.id: Satu versi menggambarkannya seperti rubah, dengan sayap dan tanduk naga di punggung. Versi lain memberi Tenghuang rupa kuda; penunggangnya dikatakan memperoleh umur dua ribu tahun. Ungkapan yang mengacu pada menunggang Tenghuang dipakai untuk kenaikan kedudukan atau reputasi.
long_description.en: One version describes a foxlike beast with wings and dragonlike horns on its back. Another version gives Tenghuang a horse's appearance; its rider is said to gain a lifespan of two thousand years. Expressions referring to riding Tenghuang describe rising in status or reputation.

long_description.id: Teks-teks klasik Tiongkok memberi gambaran yang bervariasi. Shanhaijing menyebut 乘黃 berbentuk seperti rubah dengan tanduk di punggung, dan 《淮南子》 dengan komentar Gao You menyebut 飛黃 serupa; kutipan 《瑞應圖》 menyebut 騰黃 sebagai kuda ajaib berwarna kuning yang juga bernama 吉光, dan Ying Shao menyebut 乘黃 bersayap naga dan bertubuh kuda. Umur penunggangnya dicatat dua ribu tahun dalam Shanhaijing dan tiga ribu tahun dalam kutipan-kutipan lain.
long_description.en: Classical Chinese texts give varying pictures. The Shanhaijing says the 乘黃 looks like a fox with horns on its back, and the 《淮南子》 with Gao You's commentary says the 飛黃 is similar; a passage from the 《瑞應圖》 calls the 騰黃 a divine yellow horse also named 吉光, while Ying Shao says the 乘黃 has dragon wings and a horse's body. The rider's lifespan is two thousand years in the Shanhaijing and three thousand years in the other quoted passages.

claims.quote: Tenghuang (Chinese: 騰黃; also known by various names as Chenghuang, Feihuang, Guhuangm, and Cuihuang) is a mythological creature which is symbol of auspiciousness in Chinese mythology. It is mentioned in the Shanhaijing.

statement.id: Tenghuang merupakan makhluk pembawa pertanda baik dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
statement.en: Tenghuang is an auspicious creature in Chinese mythology.

claims.quote: It is mentioned in the Shanhaijing.

statement.id: Artikel menyebut kemunculannya dalam Shan Hai Jing.
statement.en: Tenghuang is mentioned in the Shanhaijing.

claims.quote: There are two versions of what Tenghuang looked like. It is said to be a beast like a fox, with wings and horns like a dragon on its back. The life span of those who ride it can grow to two thousand years. Another claim states that it has the appearance of a horse.

statement.id: Versi lain memberi Tenghuang rupa kuda; penunggangnya dikatakan memperoleh umur dua ribu tahun.
statement.en: Another version gives Tenghuang a horse's appearance; its rider is said to gain a lifespan of two thousand years.

claims.quote: There is an idiom in Chinese, "Flying the Yellow Tengda" (飛黃騰達) or "Riding on the Tenghuang". It is used to describe a person ascending and gaining a high position or reputation.

statement.id: Ungkapan yang mengacu pada menunggang Tenghuang dipakai untuk kenaikan kedudukan atau reputasi.

claims.quote: 白民之國在龍魚北，白身披髮。有乘黃，其狀如狐，其背上有角，乘之壽二千歲。

statement.id: Shanhaijing (Haiwai Xi Jing) menyebut 乘黃 (Chenghuang) di Negeri 白民: bentuknya seperti rubah, di punggungnya ada tanduk, dan yang menungganginya berumur dua ribu tahun.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing (Overseas West section) names the 乘黃 (Chenghuang) in the land of the 白民: it looks like a fox, has horns on its back, and whoever rides it lives two thousand years.

claims.quote: 《淮南子》曰：黃帝治天下，飛黃服皂。高誘曰：飛黃如狐，背有角，日行萬里，乘之壽三千歲。

statement.id: Himpunan 名馬記 mengutip 《淮南子》 dan komentar Gao You: 飛黃 (Feihuang) seperti rubah dengan tanduk di punggung, berlari sepuluh ribu li sehari, dan penunggangnya berumur tiga ribu tahun.
statement.en: The compilation 名馬記 quotes the 《淮南子》 and Gao You's commentary: the 飛黃 (Feihuang) is like a fox with horns on its back, covers ten thousand li a day, and its rider lives three thousand years.

claims.quote: 《瑞應圖》曰：騰黃者，神馬也，其色黃，王者德御四方則至。一名吉光，乘之壽三千歲，此馬無死時。
claims.locator: 神馬○騰黃○吉光○騕褭○飛兔○駃蹄

statement.id: Kutipan dari 《瑞應圖》 dalam 名馬記 menyebut 騰黃 sebagai kuda ajaib berwarna kuning yang datang ketika penguasa memerintah keempat penjuru dengan kebajikan, juga dinamai 吉光, yang penunggangnya berumur tiga ribu tahun dan kuda itu tak punya masa mati.
statement.en: A passage from the 《瑞應圖》 in the 名馬記 calls the 騰黃 a divine yellow horse that arrives when a ruler governs the four quarters through virtue, also named 吉光, whose rider lives three thousand years and which never dies.

claims.quote: 應劭曰：乘黃，龍翼馬身，黃帝乘而仙。 《瑞應圖》曰：乘黃者，王者輿服有度則出。

statement.id: Menurut Ying Shao (應劭) yang dikutip dalam 名馬記, 乘黃 bersayap naga dan bertubuh kuda, dan Kaisar Kuning (黃帝) menungganginya lalu menjadi dewa; 《瑞應圖》 menambahkan bahwa 乘黃 muncul ketika kereta dan busana penguasa sesuai aturan.
statement.en: According to Ying Shao (應劭), quoted in the 名馬記, the 乘黃 has dragon wings and a horse's body, and the Yellow Emperor (黃帝) rode it and became an immortal; the 《瑞應圖》 adds that the 乘黃 appears when a ruler's carriage and dress follow proper rules.

summary.id: Shanhaijing: seperti rubah dengan tanduk di punggung; penunggang berumur dua ribu tahun.
summary.en: Shanhaijing: fox-like with horns on its back; rider lives two thousand years.

summary.id: Kutipan 《淮南子》/Gao You dan 《瑞應圖》: penunggang berumur tiga ribu tahun.
summary.en: Quoted 《淮南子》/Gao You and 《瑞應圖》: rider lives three thousand years.

summary.id: Ying Shao: bersayap naga dan bertubuh kuda.
summary.en: Ying Shao: dragon-winged with a horse's body.
