short_description.id: Tepegöz adalah raksasa bermata satu dalam mitologi Turkik, kiklop dari Kitab Dede Korkut yang dibutakan dan dikalahkan.
short_description.en: Tepegöz is a one-eyed giant of Turkic mythology, the cyclops of the Book of Dede Korkut who is blinded and defeated.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, Tepegöz adalah raksasa bermata satu di dahi, semacam kiklop, yang muncul dalam Kitab Dede Korkut, epos bangsa Turk Oghuz. Namanya berarti "mata di bukit" atau "mata di dahi"; lubang bundar di puncak yurt juga disebut tepegoz.
long_description.en: In Turkic mythology Tepegöz is a giant with one eye on his forehead, a kind of cyclops, appearing in the Book of Dede Korkut, the epic of the Oghuz Turks. His name means "eye on the hill" or "eye on the forehead"; the round opening at the top of a yurt is also called a tepegoz.

long_description.id: Kisahnya bermula ketika seorang gembala Oghuz menemukan bayi mengerikan berupa gumpalan daging yang dilahirkan seorang peri. Inti ceritanya: Tepegöz menggiring orang ke guanya untuk dimakan, tetapi korbannya membutakan matanya yang tunggal dan lolos dengan berselubung kulit domba.
long_description.en: His story begins when an Oghuz herdsman finds a monstrous infant, a lump of flesh born to a nymph. Its core: Tepegöz drives a man into his cave to eat him, but the victim blinds his single eye and escapes wrapped in a sheepskin.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah itu, setelah dewasa anak bermata satu tersebut menggigit putus hidung dan telinga seorang anak tetangga dan diusir dari desa. Tak seorang pun mampu membunuhnya: pedang tidak melukainya, panah tidak membunuhnya, dan kulitnya sangat keras. Dede Korkut membuat kesepakatan agar dua orang dan 500 domba diserahkan setiap hari, hingga Basat membunuhnya dengan menyerang matanya dan memenggal kepalanya.
long_description.en: In the story, once grown, the one-eyed boy bites off a neighbour child's nose and ear and is driven out of the village. Nobody can kill him: the sword cannot cut him, the arrow cannot kill him, and his skin is very hard. Dede Korkut strikes a deal for two men and 500 sheep daily, until Basat kills him by striking his eye and cutting off his head.

long_description.id: Para sarjana tertarik pada kedekatan kisah Tepegöz dengan kisah Odiseus dan Kiklop dalam karya Homeros. Sebagian berpendapat kisah Homeros masuk ke versi Turkik, sebagian lain bahwa Homeros mengambilnya dari tradisi yang lebih tua di Asia Kecil.
long_description.en: Scholars are intrigued by the close relation of the story of Tepegöz to that of Odysseus and the Cyclops in Homer. Some argue that the Homeric story found its way into the Turkic version, others that Homer took it from an earlier tradition circulating in Asia Minor.

short_description.id: La Tulevieja adalah hantu bertopi tule dalam cerita rakyat Kosta Rika dan Panama yang sering digambarkan setengah burung [tulevieja-c01, tulevieja-c02].
short_description.en: La Tulevieja is a tule-hatted ghost of Costa Rican and Panamanian folklore, often described as half bird [tulevieja-c01, tulevieja-c02].

long_description.id: La Tulevieja adalah hantu bertopi tule dalam cerita rakyat Kosta Rika dan Panama [tulevieja-c01]. Ia sering digambarkan sebagai campuran perempuan dan burung [tulevieja-c02] dengan kaki elang yang meninggalkan jejak terbalik [tulevieja-c03]. Ia konon memakan arang dan abu di sekitar api unggun [tulevieja-c04], dan hanya doa "Alabado sea el Santísimo" yang dapat mengusirnya [tulevieja-c05].
long_description.en: La Tulevieja is a tule-hatted ghost of Costa Rican and Panamanian folklore [tulevieja-c01]. She is often a woman-bird hybrid [tulevieja-c02] with eagle legs that leave reversed footprints [tulevieja-c03]. She reportedly eats charcoal and ashes by campfires [tulevieja-c04], and only the prayer "Alabado sea el Santísimo" drives her away [tulevieja-c05].

long_description.id: Versi Kosta Rika yang dihimpun kementerian pendidikan negara itu menggambarkan Tulevieja sebagai nenek yang tinggal dekat Sungai Virilla dan memakai topi besar dari tule [tulevieja-c07]. Setelah menjadi legenda, ia dilukiskan berdada telanjang, berkaki gavilán, bersayap kelelawar, berwajah penyihir, dan membawa kayu bakar [tulevieja-c08]. Dikatakan ia terbang dan menimpa orang yang berdosa berat [tulevieja-c09].
long_description.en: A Costa Rican version collected by that country's education ministry describes the Tulevieja as an old woman who lived near the Virilla river and wore a big tule hat [tulevieja-c07]. Once she became a legend, she was described with bare breasts, hawk legs, bat wings, a witch's face and a load of firewood [tulevieja-c08]. It is said that she takes flight and falls on people in mortal sin [tulevieja-c09].

long_description.id: Dalam versi itu, anak-anak yang mengejek memberinya julukan Tulevieja [tulevieja-c10], dan ia tewas tenggelam ketika mengejar topinya yang terbawa arus Sungai Tiribi yang sedang banjir [tulevieja-c11]. Versi lain menceritakan seorang gadis yang menenggelamkan anaknya di sungai dan dihukum menjadi makhluk mengerikan [tulevieja-c06].
long_description.en: In that version, mocking children gave her the nickname Tulevieja [tulevieja-c10], and she drowned while chasing her hat, carried off by the swollen Tiribi river [tulevieja-c11]. Another version tells of a girl who drowned her child in a river and was punished by becoming a hideous creature [tulevieja-c06].

statement.en: La Tulevieja (also Tulivieja) is a legendary figure of Costa Rican and Panamanian folklore, a ghost wearing a distinctive hat called a tule.

short_description.id: Scultone adalah makhluk mirip naga atau ular dalam legenda Sardinia yang tatapannya dapat membunuh dan yang menuntut korban manusia di sekitar Baunei, sebelum dikalahkan oleh Rasul Petrus.
short_description.en: The Scultone is a dragon-like or serpent creature of Sardinian legend whose gaze could kill and which demanded human sacrifices around Baunei before the apostle Peter defeated it.

long_description.id: Legenda rakyat Sardinia menyebut Scultone sebagai hewan mirip reptil seperti naga yang membunuh manusia dan hewan; di dekat Baunei, kaburnya naga ini konon membuka jurang Golgo. Situs pariwisata Baunei menyebut monster itu "Sa Serpente", sejenis naga jahat yang kadang keluar dari jurang Golgo dan menuntut korban manusia. Menurut artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Korsika, ia hidup di antara semak-semak dan abadi.
long_description.en: Sardinian folk legends describe the Scultone as a reptile-like, dragon-like animal that killed people and animals; near Baunei its flight is said to have opened the Golgo chasm. The Baunei tourism site calls the monster "Sa Serpente", a sort of evil dragon that sometimes came out of the Golgo chasm demanding human sacrifices. According to the Corsican-language Wikipedia article, it lived among the shrubs and was immortal.

long_description.id: Konon Rasul Petrus yang mengalahkannya. Satu versi menyebut tatapan Scultone mematikan sehingga Petrus memandangnya lewat cermin kecil dan membuatnya tenggelam ke perut bumi; versi lain menyebut Petrus melemparkan monster itu ke tanah sehingga Su Sterru membuka dan menelannya. Portal pariwisata Sardinia menyebut jurang itu sebagai sarang ular dan ancamannya dijauhkan dengan pembangunan gereja Santo Petrus di dekatnya.
long_description.en: The apostle Peter is said to have defeated it. One version says the Scultone's gaze could kill, so Peter looked at it through a small mirror and sank it into the earth; another says Peter threw the monster to the ground so that Su Sterru opened and swallowed it. The Sardinian tourism portal calls the chasm a serpent's lair whose threat was averted by building the nearby church of Saint Peter.

long_description.id: Scultone muncul dalam wujud basilisk sebagai lawan utama dalam komik Martin Mystère dan menjadi salah satu tokoh buku La Dottoressa Heja e il Drago dei Nuraghi. Sebuah artikel mencatat bahwa seperti basilisk, ia dapat membunuh dengan tatapan dan dilawan dengan cermin.
long_description.en: It appears as a basilisk, the main antagonist of a Martin Mystère comic, and is one of the protagonists of the book La Dottoressa Heja e il Drago dei Nuraghi. An article notes that, like the basilisk, it can kill with its gaze and is fought with a mirror.

statement.en: According to the Corsican-language Wikipedia article, U Scultone is a reptile-like, dragon-like animal that killed people and animals, lived among the shrubs and was immortal.

claims.quote: Legend has it that once upon a time the entire plateau was at the mercy of a vicious monster, “Sa Serpente”, a sort of evil dragon who would sometimes come out of the chasm of Golgo (“Su Sterru”) demanding human sacrifices.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, dahulu seluruh dataran tinggi berada di bawah ancaman monster ganas, "Sa Serpente", sejenis naga jahat yang kadang keluar dari jurang Golgo ("Su Sterru") dan menuntut korban manusia.
statement.en: Legend has it that the whole plateau was once at the mercy of a vicious monster, "Sa Serpente", a sort of evil dragon that sometimes came out of the Golgo chasm ("Su Sterru") demanding human sacrifices.

claims.quote: St. Peter prevailed in the clash with the evil reptile and has been the most beloved saint of the Baunesis, eternally grateful for being freed from the Golgo monster, ever since.

statement.id: Santo Petrus menang dalam pertarungan melawan reptil jahat itu, dan sejak itu menjadi santo yang paling dicintai orang Baunei yang berterima kasih karena dibebaskan dari monster Golgo.
statement.en: Saint Peter prevailed in the clash with the evil reptile and has since been the most beloved saint of the Baunesis, who are grateful to have been freed from the Golgo monster.

claims.quote: According to another version of the legend, however, “Su Sterru” opened up the ground of Golgo, swallowing “Sa Serpente”, when St. Peter threw the evil monster to the ground.

statement.id: Menurut versi lain legenda itu, "Su Sterru" membuka tanah Golgo dan menelan "Sa Serpente" ketika Santo Petrus melemparkan monster jahat itu ke tanah.
statement.en: According to another version of the legend, "Su Sterru" opened up the ground of Golgo and swallowed "Sa Serpente" when Saint Peter threw the evil monster to the ground.

claims.quote: si diceva fosse tana di un serpente (su scultone), la cui minaccia fu allontanata con la costruzione (XVII secolo) della vicina chiesa di san Pietro.
claims.locator: Su Sterru – Il Golgo di Baunei

statement.id: Su Sterru, jurang di dataran tinggi Golgo, konon adalah sarang seekor ular (su scultone), yang ancamannya dijauhkan dengan pembangunan gereja Santo Petrus di dekatnya pada abad ke-17.
statement.en: Su Sterru, the chasm on the Golgo plateau, was said to be the lair of a serpent (su scultone), whose threat was averted by building the nearby church of Saint Peter in the 17th century.

claims.quote: lo scultone, come il basilisco, può uccidere con lo sguardo e viene combattuto con uno specchio

statement.id: Menurut catatan "lihat pula" pada artikel itu, scultone, seperti basilisk, dapat membunuh dengan tatapan dan dilawan dengan cermin.
statement.en: According to the "see also" note in the article, the scultone, like the basilisk, can kill with its gaze and is fought with a mirror.

claims.quote: Lo Scultone è uno dei protagonisti de La Dottoressa Heja e il Drago dei Nuraghi (Edizioni A.Car, 2024), insieme a varie altre creature del folklore sardo che si uniranno per affrontarlo.

statement.id: Scultone adalah salah satu tokoh utama La Dottoressa Heja e il Drago dei Nuraghi (Edizioni A.Car, 2024), bersama beberapa makhluk folklor Sardinia lain yang bersatu untuk menghadapinya.
statement.en: The Scultone is one of the protagonists of La Dottoressa Heja e il Drago dei Nuraghi (Edizioni A.Car, 2024), together with various other creatures of Sardinian folklore who unite to face it.

topic.id: Cara Santo Petrus mengalahkan monster itu
topic.en: How Saint Peter overcame the monster

summary.id: Satu versi: Petrus memandangnya lewat cermin kecil sehingga tatapan mematikannya tak berdaya, lalu menenggelamkannya ke perut bumi.
summary.en: One version: Peter looked at it through a small mirror, neutralising its deadly gaze, and sank it into the bowels of the earth.

summary.id: Versi lain: Petrus melemparkannya ke tanah dan Su Sterru membuka lalu menelannya.
summary.en: Another version: Peter threw it to the ground and Su Sterru opened and swallowed it.

summary.id: Sumber ketiga: ancamannya dijauhkan dengan pembangunan gereja Santo Petrus di dekatnya (abad ke-17).
summary.en: A third source: its threat was averted by building the nearby church of Saint Peter (17th century).

short_description.id: Fuxi (負屓) adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga yang gemar membaca dan menulis; sosoknya dilukiskan melilit puncak atau sisi prasasti batu.
short_description.en: Fuxi (負屓) is one of the dragon's nine sons, fond of reading and writing; its likeness is shown coiling around the top or sides of stone steles.

long_description.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, 負屓 adalah salah satu putra naga dalam uraian Li Dongyang di 懐麓堂集. Ia gemar membaca dan menulis, sehingga digambarkan melilit puncak prasasti batu. Tafsir harfiah aksara namanya mengacu pada memikul beban berat: 『贔』 menggambarkan banyaknya harta, sedangkan 『屓』 adalah 『贔』 yang ditambah 『尸』 dan bermakna menanggung harta.
long_description.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, 負屓 is one of the dragon's sons in Li Dongyang's account in the 懐麓堂集. It is fond of reading and writing, which is why it is depicted coiling around the top of stone steles. A literal reading of the characters of its name refers to bearing a heavy load: 『贔』 conveys abundance of goods, while 『屓』 is 『贔』 with 『尸』 added and means holding on to treasure.

long_description.id: Dalam Shuo Lüe karya Gu Qiyuan (Ming), putra naga yang gemar sastra dan berada di sisi prasasti ditulis 屓屭. Penulisnya menjelaskan bahwa aksara 屓 dan 屭 punya ragam tulisan lain, termasuk 贔, dan mengutip kamus Yunhui bahwa artinya perawakan besar atau kura-kura laut raksasa, sedangkan Guangyun menyebutnya "orang kuat yang mengerahkan tenaga". Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyebut 负屃 sebagai putra kedelapan naga yang gemar sastra, dengan naga-naga bersastra di kedua sisi prasasti sebagai sosoknya.
long_description.en: In Gu Qiyuan's Shuo Lüe (Ming), the dragon's son that likes literature and is at the sides of steles is written 屓屭. Its author explains that the characters 屓 and 屭 have variant forms, including 贔, and quotes the dictionary Yunhui that the word means a huge appearance or a giant sea turtle, while the Guangyun calls it "a strong man exerting strength". Chinese Wikipedia calls 负屃 the eighth son of the dragon, fond of literature, with the literary dragons at both sides of steles as its likeness.

long_description.id: Sumber-sumber tidak sepakat tentang kegemaran putra naga di prasasti. Yŏrha ilgi mengutip Zonggui bahwa 贔屭 gemar sastra sehingga berada di kedua sisi tulisan prasasti, tetapi Bowuzhi yipian menyebut 贔屭 gemar beban dan memikul prasasti, sedangkan 螭虎 yang gemar hiasan sastra berdiri di atas tulisan. Penulisnya mempertanyakan bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan Gu Qiyuan sendiri tidak menemukan satu pun nama dalam daftar yang dibahasnya tercatat sebagai putra naga.
long_description.en: Sources disagree about what the dragon's son at the stele likes. The Yŏrha ilgi quotes the Zonggui that 贔屭 likes literature and so is at both sides of the inscription, but the Bowuzhi yipian says 贔屭 likes heavy loads and carries the stele, while 螭虎, which likes literary ornament, stands on the inscription. Its author asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and Gu Qiyuan himself found none of the names in the list he discusses recorded as a dragon's son.

literal_meaning.id: Ditafsirkan secara harfiah, 負屓 berarti "memikul beban berat".
literal_meaning.en: Interpreted literally, 負屓 means "carrying a heavy load".

who.id: Salah satu dari sembilan putra naga yang gemar sastra.
who.en: One of the dragon's nine sons, fond of literature.

origin.id: Dicatat dalam daftar putra naga pada teks Ming, dan menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang dalam uraian Li Dongyang.
origin.en: Recorded in lists of the dragon's sons in Ming texts, and according to Japanese Wikipedia in Li Dongyang's account.

role.id: Gemar sastra; sosoknya melilit puncak atau berada di sisi prasasti batu.
role.en: Fond of literature; its likeness coils around the top of, or stands at the sides of, stone steles.

claims.quote: 負屓（ふき、拼音：Fùxì）は、李東陽が著した『懐麓堂集』の説による竜生九子の一つ。文章の読み書きを好み、故に石碑の頂に絡み付いているという。

claims.quote: 『贔』の字は財貨が多い様を表し、『屓』の字は『贔』に『尸』を付けたし、財宝を抱え込んでしまう意がある。つまり、『負屓』を字義通りに解釈すると『重たい荷物を背負う』という意味になる。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, tafsir harfiah aksara namanya mengacu pada memikul beban berat.
statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, a literal interpretation of the characters of its name refers to bearing a heavy load.

claims.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。

statement.id: Dalam Shuo Lüe (說略, karya Gu Qiyuan, Ming), daftar sembilan putra naga yang "tidak menjadi naga, masing-masing punya kegemaran" memuat 屓屭 yang gemar sastra (好文) dan berada di sisi prasasti (在碑兩傍). Teksnya menambahkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi (弘治) kaisar (泰陵) menyuruh seorang kasim menanyakan nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang (李東陽); Li tidak dapat menyebut semuanya, bertanya kepada Liu Ji (劉績), dan memperoleh keterangannya dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya pun tidak diketahui.
statement.en: In the Shuo Lüe (說略, by Gu Qiyuan, Ming), the list of the dragon's nine sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness" includes 屓屭, which likes literature (好文) and is at the sides of steles (在碑兩傍). The text adds that in the Hongzhi (弘治) period the emperor (泰陵) had a eunuch ask Li Dongyang (李東陽) for the names of the nine sons; Li could not give them all, asked Liu Ji (劉績), and obtained the account from an old register whose origin was also unknown.

claims.quote: 屓屭，屓一作𤣂，一作贔。屭，一作㞒。《韻會》狀大貌。又鼇也。一曰雌鼇為屓。《廣韻》壯士作力貌。〈西京賦〉巨靈贔屓。〈吳都賦〉巨鼇贔屓。 ... 已上都不見有龍子之說，囚牛、嘲風、霸下，俟考。

statement.id: Penulis Shuo Lüe menjelaskan 屓屭: aksara 屓 dan 屭 punya ragam tulisan lain (termasuk 贔); menurut kamus Yunhui (韻會) artinya perawakan besar, juga 鼇 (kura-kura laut raksasa), dan menurut Guangyun (廣韻) "orang kuat yang mengerahkan tenaga"; ia mengutip Xijing fu (西京賦) dan Wu du fu (吳都賦) tentang 贔屓. Ia tidak menemukan satu pun nama yang dibahasnya dalam catatan sebagai putra naga; 囚牛, 嘲風, dan 霸下 ia tinggalkan untuk diteliti.
statement.en: The author of the Shuo Lüe glosses 屓屭: the characters 屓 and 屭 have variant forms (including 贔); according to the dictionary Yunhui (韻會) it means a huge appearance, also the 鼇 (giant sea turtle), and according to the Guangyun (廣韻) "a strong man exerting strength"; he cites the Xijing fu (西京賦) and the Wu du fu (吳都賦) on 贔屓. He found none of the names he discusses described in records as a dragon's son, and left 囚牛, 嘲風 and 霸下 for further examination.

claims.quote: 又博物逸篇云。贔屭。性好重。故載碑。螭虎。形似龍。性好文釆。故立于碑文上。又總龜云。龍之九子。一名覇夏。好負重。故爲碑座。贔屭。好文故在碑文兩旁。諸說亦各不同。龍子名號及性情。何以知之。古說傅會多此類。

statement.id: Dalam Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記): Bowuzhi yipian (博物志逸篇) menyebut 贔屭 gemar beban sehingga memikul prasasti, sedangkan 螭虎 yang gemar hiasan sastra berdiri di atas tulisan prasasti; Zonggui (總龜) menyebut 覇夏 gemar memikul beban sehingga menjadi alas prasasti dan 贔屭 gemar sastra sehingga berada di kedua sisi tulisan prasasti. Penulisnya menyatakan pendapat-pendapat itu berbeda-beda, mempertanyakan bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan menyebut teori kuno semacam itu banyak yang dibuat-buat.
statement.en: In the Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記): the Bowuzhi yipian (博物志逸篇) says 贔屭 likes heavy things and so carries steles, while 螭虎, which likes literary ornament, stands on the inscription; the Zonggui (總龜) says 覇夏 likes bearing loads and so serves as a stele base, and 贔屭 likes literature and so is found at both sides of the inscription. The author says the accounts differ, asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and says old theories of this kind are mostly embellishment.

claims.quote: 负屃是中国神话中龙的第八个儿子。似龙形，排行老八，平生好文，石碑两旁的文龙是其遗像。

statement.id: Catatan dalam Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyebut 负屃 (Fùxì) sebagai putra kedelapan naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, berbentuk seperti naga, gemar sastra (平生好文), dan naga-naga bersastra di kedua sisi prasasti adalah sosoknya.
statement.en: A note in Chinese Wikipedia calls 负屃 (Fùxì) the eighth son of the dragon in Chinese mythology, dragon-shaped, fond of literature (平生好文), with the literary dragons at both sides of steles as its likeness.

topic.id: Apa yang digemari putra naga pada prasasti: sastra atau memikul beban
topic.en: What the dragon's son at the stele likes: literature or bearing loads

summary.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang dan Tionghoa, Shuo Lüe, serta Zonggui (dikutip Yŏrha ilgi): gemar sastra dan berada di sisi atau puncak prasasti.
summary.en: Japanese and Chinese Wikipedia, the Shuo Lüe and the Zonggui (quoted in the Yŏrha ilgi): fond of literature and at the sides or top of steles.

summary.id: Bowuzhi yipian (dikutip Yŏrha ilgi): 贔屭 gemar beban dan memikul prasasti, sedangkan 螭虎 gemar hiasan sastra; tafsir harfiah 負屓 pun mengacu pada memikul beban.
summary.en: Bowuzhi yipian (quoted in the Yŏrha ilgi): 贔屭 likes heavy loads and carries the stele, while 螭虎 likes literary ornament; the literal reading of 負屓 likewise refers to bearing a load.

short_description.id: Jiguang adalah hewan ajaib pembawa keberuntungan dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Jiguang is an auspicious fabulous animal in Chinese mythology.

long_description.id: Jiguang adalah hewan ajaib pembawa keberuntungan dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Salah satu uraian memberinya bentuk kuda putih berpola dengan surai merah yang lahir di rawa besar.
long_description.en: Jiguang is an auspicious fabulous animal in Chinese mythology. One description gives it the form of a patterned white horse with a red mane, born in a great marsh.

long_description.id: Jiguang kerap dicampur dengan Tenghuang, sementara bentuk rubah dan kuda berbeda menurut versinya. Ungkapan Jiguang pianyu memakai sehelai bulunya sebagai kiasan untuk peninggalan atau dokumen langka.
long_description.en: Jiguang is often confused with Tenghuang, while fox and horse forms differ between versions. The expression Jiguang pianyu uses a strand of its fur as a metaphor for rare relics or documents.

long_description.id: Sumber-sumber klasik memberi gambaran yang beragam. 名馬記 mengutip 《山海經》 tentang kuda berpola bertubuh putih dan bersurai merah bernama 吉良, sedangkan kutipan 《瑞應圖》 menyebut 騰黃 yang kuning juga bernama 吉光. Baopuzi menyebut 騰黃之馬 dan 吉光之獸 sama-sama berumur tiga ribu tahun, dan 《海內十洲記》 menyebut mantel bulu 吉光 berwarna kuning, golongan kuda ajaib, yang tidak tenggelam di air dan tidak hangus di api.
long_description.en: Classical sources give varied pictures. The 名馬記 quotes the 《山海經》 on a patterned horse with a white body and red mane named 吉良, while a quoted 《瑞應圖》 passage says the yellow 騰黃 is also named 吉光. The Baopuzi says both the 騰黃 horse and the 吉光 beast live three thousand years, and the 《海內十洲記》 says the 吉光 fur coat is yellow, of the divine-horse kind, and neither sinks in water nor scorches in fire.

sources.title: 吉光 - 维基百科，自由的百科全书

claims.quote: 吉光，又稱吉良、澤馬，是中國神話傳說中的神獸，是吉祥的象徵。常與騰黃混淆在一起。

claims.quote: 因為吉光是極難得一見的神獸，因此民間有成語「吉光片羽」，以吉光的一絲獸毛，來形容某種極難得一見的文獻或是文物。

statement.id: Ungkapan Jiguang pianyu memakai sehelai bulunya sebagai kiasan untuk peninggalan atau dokumen langka.
statement.en: The expression Jiguang pianyu uses a strand of its fur as a metaphor for rare relics or documents.

claims.quote: 澤馬，一曰吉良。《山海經》曰：大封國有文馬，縞身朱鬛，名曰吉良，乘之壽千歲。

statement.id: Himpunan 名馬記 menyebut 澤馬 juga bernama 吉良 dan mengutip 《山海經》: di negeri 大封國 ada kuda berpola bertubuh putih dan bersurai merah bernama 吉良, yang penunggangnya berumur seribu tahun.
statement.en: The compilation 名馬記 says the 澤馬 is also called 吉良 and quotes the 《山海經》: in the country 大封國 there is a patterned horse with a white body and red mane named 吉良, whose rider lives a thousand years.

claims.quote: 《瑞應圖》曰：騰黃者，神馬也，其色黃，王者德御四方則至。一名吉光，乘之壽三千歲，此馬無死時。

statement.id: Kutipan dari 《瑞應圖》 menyebut 騰黃 sebagai kuda ajaib berwarna kuning yang juga bernama 吉光, dan penunggangnya berumur tiga ribu tahun.
statement.en: A passage from the 《瑞應圖》 calls the 騰黃 a divine yellow horse that is also named 吉光, and whose rider lives three thousand years.

claims.quote: 蟾蜍壽三千歲，騏驎壽二千歲。騰黃之馬，吉光之獸，皆壽三千歲。

statement.id: Baopuzi menulis bahwa 騰黃之馬 dan 吉光之獸 sama-sama berumur tiga ribu tahun, disebut bersama katak (蟾蜍) dan 騏驎 yang berumur lebih pendek.
statement.en: The Baopuzi says that both the 騰黃 horse and the 吉光 beast live three thousand years, listed alongside the toad (蟾蜍) and the 騏驎, which live shorter lives.

claims.quote: 献此膠四兩，吉光毛裘，武帝受以付外庫 ... 吉光毛裘黃色，盖神馬之類也。裘入水数日不沉，入火不焦。

statement.id: Dalam 《海內十洲記》, 吉光毛裘 dipersembahkan kepada Kaisar Wu (武帝) dan disimpan di gudang luar; mantel bulu itu berwarna kuning dan dikatakan termasuk golongan kuda ajaib; mantel itu tidak tenggelam selama berhari-hari di air dan tidak hangus di api.
statement.en: In the 《海內十洲記》 a 吉光 fur coat is presented to Emperor Wu (武帝) and stored in the outer treasury; the coat is yellow and said to belong to the divine-horse kind; it does not sink after days in water and does not scorch in fire.

summary.en: The quoted 《瑞應圖》: 吉光 is another name of the yellow 騰黃; the 《海內十洲記》 calls its fur yellow.

short_description.id: Xiaotian Quan adalah anjing mitologis China yang menyertai dewa Erlang Shen.
short_description.en: Xiaotian Quan is a Chinese mythological dog accompanying the god Erlang Shen.

long_description.id: Xiaotian Quan adalah anjing mitologis China yang menyertai dewa Erlang Shen. Ia membantu Erlang Shen melawan iblis melalui gigitan dan lolongannya, dan digambarkan sebagai anjing hitam. Banyak kuil Erlang Shen juga memuliakannya.
long_description.en: Xiaotian Quan is a Chinese mythological dog accompanying the god Erlang Shen. It helps Erlang Shen fight demons through its bite and howl and is depicted as a black dog. Many temples to Erlang Shen also enshrine it.

long_description.id: Sebagian orang mengidentifikasinya dengan Tiangou. Ia juga diidentifikasi dengan anjing pemburu Hou Yi. Dalam novel Journey to the West ia membantu melawan Sun Wukong; teks bab 6 novel itu menyebut anjing Erlang dengan sebutan 細犬 dan menceritakan ia menggigit betis orang yang melarikan diri.
long_description.en: Some identify it with Tiangou. It is also identified with Hou Yi's hunting hound. In the novel Journey to the West it helps fight Sun Wukong; the text of chapter 6 of the novel calls Erlang's dog 細犬 and tells how it bites the calf of a fleeing figure.

long_description.id: Dalam satu versi legenda, anjing setia Hou Yi mengejar Chang'e ke bulan dan menelannya; Ibu Suri Barat mengampuninya dan menganugerahi gelar Tiangou sebagai penjaga Gerbang Surga Selatan, hingga ia mengabdi kepada Erlang Shen. Legenda lain mengatakan ia dahulu perempuan jahat yang diubah menjadi anjing dan berusaha menelan matahari dan bulan. Ia pertama muncul dalam In Search of the Supernatural, dan dalam dongeng Lotus Lantern ia mencegah Liu Chenxiang membelah Gunung Hua.
long_description.en: In one version of the legend, Hou Yi's loyal dog chased Chang'e to the moon and swallowed it; the Queen Mother of the West spared it and granted the title Tiangou as guardian of the Southern Heavenly Gate, until it entered Erlang Shen's service. Another legend says it was once a wicked woman transformed into a dog who tried to swallow the sun and the moon. It first appeared in In Search of the Supernatural, and in the folktale of Lotus Lantern it prevents Liu Chenxiang from splitting Mount Hua.

statement.en: In one version of the legend, after Hou Yi's wife Chang'e stole his elixir of immortality and fled to the moon, the loyal dog chased her and swallowed the moon in an attempt to bring her back.

claims.quote: The Queen Mother of the West, moved by the dog's devotion to its master, spared it from punishment and granted it the title of "Tiangou", appointing it as guardian of the Southern Heavenly Gate. The dog later released the moon and eventually entered the service of the deity Erlang Shen, where it became known as Xiaotian Quan.

statement.id: Ibu Suri Barat, tersentuh oleh kesetiaan anjing itu kepada tuannya, mengampuninya dari hukuman dan menganugerahinya gelar "Tiangou" sebagai penjaga Gerbang Surga Selatan; anjing itu kemudian melepaskan bulan dan akhirnya mengabdi kepada dewa Erlang Shen, tempat ia dikenal sebagai Xiaotian Quan.
statement.en: The Queen Mother of the West, moved by the dog's devotion to its master, spared it from punishment and granted it the title "Tiangou" as guardian of the Southern Heavenly Gate; the dog later released the moon and eventually entered the service of Erlang Shen, where it became known as Xiaotian Quan.

claims.quote: According to one legend, Xiaotian Quan was once a woman whose extreme wickedness led the Jade Emperor to transform her into a dog and imprison her in the depths of hell. ... After her release, she sought revenge against heaven and attempted to swallow the sun and the moon, plunging the world into darkness.

statement.id: Menurut satu legenda, Xiaotian Quan dahulu seorang perempuan yang kejahatannya begitu besar sehingga Kaisar Giok mengubahnya menjadi anjing dan memenjarakannya di dasar neraka; setelah dibebaskan ia membalas dendam kepada langit dan berusaha menelan matahari dan bulan sehingga dunia gelap.
statement.en: According to one legend, Xiaotian Quan was once a woman whose extreme wickedness led the Jade Emperor to transform her into a dog and imprison her in the depths of hell; after her release she sought revenge against heaven and tried to swallow the sun and the moon, plunging the world into darkness.

claims.quote: Many temples dedicated to Erlang Shen to also enshrine Xiaotian Quan and in modern times it is suggested that people with sick pets pray to it.

statement.id: Banyak kuil Erlang Shen juga memuliakan Xiaotian Quan, dan pada zaman modern disarankan agar orang yang hewan peliharaannya sakit berdoa kepadanya.
statement.en: Many temples dedicated to Erlang Shen also enshrine Xiaotian Quan, and in modern times it is suggested that people with sick pets pray to it.

claims.quote: 爬將起來就跑。被二郎爺爺的細犬趕上，照腿肚子上一口，又扯了一跌。他睡倒在地，罵道：「這個亡人！你不去妨家長，卻來咬老孫！」

statement.id: Dalam teks 西遊記 bab ini, ketika seseorang berlari kabur, anjing kurus milik Erlang (二郎爺爺的細犬) mengejarnya, menggigit betisnya, dan menariknya jatuh; yang digigit mengumpat. Teks bab ini menyebutnya 細犬 dan tidak menyebut nama Xiaotian Quan.
statement.en: In this chapter of Journey to the West, as someone runs away, Erlang's thin dog (二郎爺爺的細犬) catches up, bites the calf and drags him down; the bitten one curses. The chapter calls it 細犬 and does not use the name Xiaotian Quan.

summary.id: Anjing setia Hou Yi yang menelan bulan dan diberi gelar Tiangou.
summary.en: The loyal dog of Hou Yi that swallowed the moon and was given the title Tiangou.

summary.id: Dahulu seorang perempuan jahat yang diubah menjadi anjing oleh Kaisar Giok.
summary.en: Once a wicked woman transformed into a dog by the Jade Emperor.

short_description.id: Xolotl adalah dewa Aztec yang digambarkan berkepala anjing, pengantar jiwa orang mati, dan saudara kembar Quetzalcōātl.
short_description.en: Xolotl is an Aztec god depicted with a dog's head, a guide of the dead, and the twin brother of Quetzalcōātl.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa api dan petir yang lazim digambarkan sebagai pria berkepala anjing dan menjadi psikopomp. Ia juga disebut dewa kembar, monster, kematian, kemalangan, penyakit, dan kecacatan. Dalam kodeks dan arca Aztec ia tampil sebagai anjing atau dewa berkepala anjing, dan ia dikenal sebagai dewa anjing bangsa Mexica.
long_description.en: In Aztec mythology Xolotl is a god of fire and lightning, commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and a psychopomp. He is also named god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities. In Aztec codices and statuary he appears as a dog or a god with a dog's head, and he is known as the dog god of the Mexica people.

long_description.id: Xolotl adalah saudara kembar berwujud anjing dari Quetzalcōātl, dan ia disebut personifikasi gelap planet Venus sebagai Bintang Senja. Satu sumber menyebut tugasnya melindungi matahari dari bahaya dunia bawah, sedangkan sumber lain menyebut ia menemani Quetzalcoatl mengambil tulang-tulang dari dunia bawah untuk menciptakan manusia. Sebagai psikopomp ia menuntun orang mati ke Mictlān, dan anjing yang mungkin menjelmakan perannya dipercaya menuntun tuannya ke Dunia Bawah dan membantu menyeberangi perairan.
long_description.en: Xolotl is the canine twin brother of Quetzalcōātl and is described as the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star. One source says his task was shielding the sun from underworld perils, while another says he went with Quetzalcoatl to fetch bones from the underworld so that people could be made. As a psychopomp he guides the dead to Mictlān, and dogs that may embody his role are said to have guided their masters into the Underworld and helped them cross water.

long_description.id: Dalam mitos pengorbanan para dewa demi matahari yang baru diciptakan, para dewa memutuskan mengorbankan diri. Xolotl berusaha melarikan diri: ia menjadi tanaman jagung ganda, lalu tanaman maguey ganda, lalu salamander yang hingga kini dinamai axolotl, tetapi akhirnya tertangkap dan dikorbankan bersama dewa-dewa lain. Versi lain menyebut ia menangis begitu lama hingga matanya jatuh dari rongganya.
long_description.en: In the myth of the gods sacrificing themselves for the newly created sun, the gods decided to give their lives. Xolotl tried to escape: he turned into a double maize plant, then a doubled maguey plant, then a salamander still named axolotl, but he was ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the other gods. In the Teotihuacan legend he wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.

cultural_context.id: Meskipun kembar umumnya dianggap pertanda buruk dan dipandang dengan waswas dalam peradaban Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa pelindung kembar dan orang dengan kelainan fisik, yang menjadi bahan ketertarikan dalam budaya Mesoamerika.
cultural_context.en: Twins were mostly viewed as ill omens by the Aztecs, yet Xolotl stood as patron of twins and of people with physical abnormalities, who fascinated Mesoamerican cultures.

who.id: Dewa Aztec berkepala anjing, pengantar jiwa, dan saudara kembar Quetzalcōātl.
who.en: An Aztec god with a dog's head, a guide of souls, and the twin of Quetzalcōātl.

origin.id: Mitologi Aztec, dikenal sebagai dewa anjing bangsa Mexica.
origin.en: Aztec mythology, known as the dog god of the Mexica people.

role.id: Menuntun orang mati ke Mictlān, menemani Quetzalcoatl ke dunia bawah, dan menjadi pelindung kembar.
role.en: Guides the dead to Mictlān, accompanied Quetzalcoatl to the underworld, and is patron of twins.

famous_for.id: Berusaha lolos dari pengorbanan para dewa dengan berganti wujud, dan salamander axolotl memakai namanya.
famous_for.en: Trying to escape the gods' sacrifice by changing shape, and the axolotl salamander bearing his name.

did_you_know.id: Kata axolotl adalah gabungan istilah Nahuatl xolotl dan atl ("air"), sehingga kira-kira berarti "kembar air".
did_you_know.en: The word axolotl combines the Nahuatl terms xolotl and atl ("water") and can roughly be translated as "water twin".

description.id: Xolotl berubah menjadi tanaman jagung muda berbatang dua, tanaman maguey ganda, dan hewan amfibi axolotl.
description.en: Xolotl transformed into a young two-stalked maize plant, a doubled maguey plant, and the amphibious axolotl.

description.id: Menurut sebagian sarjana, Xolotl dapat membantu kelahiran kembali Matahari karena ia berkuasa masuk dan keluar dari dunia bawah.
description.en: Some scholars say Xolotl can help the Sun's rebirth because he has the power to enter and exit the underworld.

title.id: Pengorbanan para dewa untuk matahari baru
title.en: The gods' sacrifice for the new sun

role.id: Xolotl mundur dari pengorbanan, berganti wujud, lalu tertangkap.
role.en: Xolotl withdraws from the sacrifice, changes shape, and is caught.

summary.id: Para dewa memutuskan mengorbankan diri demi matahari yang baru diciptakan. Xolotl berusaha melarikan diri dengan menjadi jagung ganda, maguey ganda, dan axolotl, tetapi akhirnya tertangkap dan dikorbankan bersama dewa-dewa lain; dalam penuturan lain ia menangis hingga matanya jatuh dari rongganya.
summary.en: The gods resolved to offer themselves for the freshly created sun. Xolotl tried to flee as a double maize plant, a doubled maguey plant, and an axolotl, but was ultimately caught and sacrificed with the other gods; in another telling he wept until his eyes fell out of their sockets.

role.id: Xolotl menemani Quetzalcoatl.
role.en: Xolotl accompanies Quetzalcoatl.

summary.id: Xolotl menemani Quetzalcoatl dalam misi mengambil tulang-tulang dari dunia bawah untuk menciptakan umat manusia.
summary.en: Xolotl went along with Quetzalcoatl when he set out to fetch bones from the underworld so that people could be made.

description.id: Alam baka dalam mitos, tempat Xolotl menuntun orang mati.
description.en: The afterlife in myths, to which Xolotl guides the dead.

description.id: Tempat dalam legenda ketika para dewa memutuskan mengorbankan diri demi matahari yang baru diciptakan.
description.en: The place in the legend where the gods decided to sacrifice themselves for the newly created sun.

note.id: Saudara kembar berwujud anjing; keduanya putra Chīmalmā. Xolotl juga menemani Quetzalcoatl ke dunia bawah.
note.en: His twin brother; both are sons of Chīmalmā. Xolotl also accompanied Quetzalcoatl to the underworld.

description.id: Film Disney itu memuat penghormatan kepada Xolotl berupa seekor anjing bernama Dante.
description.en: The Disney film includes an homage to Xolotl in the form of a dog named Dante.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa dewa yang dihubungkan dengan anjing dan kembar bisa memiliki peran sebagai pengantar jiwa?
learning_questions.en: Why might a god linked to dogs and twins have a role as a guide of souls?

learning_questions.id: Apa arti perubahan wujud Xolotl menjadi beberapa makhluk dalam kisah pengorbanan para dewa?
learning_questions.en: What does Xolotl's change into several forms mean in the story of the gods' sacrifice?

sources.author: Jordy Samuels
sources.title: Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claims.quote: In Aztec mythology, Xolotl ... was a god of fire and lightning. He was commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and was a psychopomp. He was also god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa api dan petir yang lazim digambarkan sebagai pria berkepala anjing dan menjadi psikopomp (pengantar jiwa). Ia juga dewa kembar, monster, kematian, kemalangan, penyakit, dan kecacatan.
statement.en: In Aztec mythology, Xolotl was a god of fire and lightning, commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and a psychopomp, and also god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities.

claims.quote: Xolotl is the canine brother and twin of Quetzalcōātl, the pair being sons of the virgin Chīmalmā. He is the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star, and was associated with heavenly fire.

statement.id: Xolotl adalah saudara kembar berwujud anjing dari Quetzalcōātl; keduanya putra Chīmalmā yang masih perawan. Ia adalah personifikasi gelap planet Venus sebagai Bintang Senja (Evening Star) dan dikaitkan dengan api surgawi.
statement.en: Xolotl is the canine brother and twin of Quetzalcōātl, the pair being sons of the virgin Chīmalmā; he is the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star and was associated with heavenly fire.

claims.quote: Xolotl was the sinister god of monstrosities who wears the conch-like ehēcailacacōcatl "twisted wind jewel" of Quetzalcōātl. His job was to protect the sun from the dangers of the underworld.

statement.id: Xolotl disebut dewa kengerian (monstrosities) yang sinis dan mengenakan permata angin berbentuk kerang milik Quetzalcōātl. Tugasnya melindungi matahari dari bahaya dunia bawah.
statement.en: Xolotl was the sinister god of monstrosities who wears the conch-like "twisted wind jewel" of Quetzalcōātl, and his job was to protect the sun from the dangers of the underworld.

claims.quote: His empty eye sockets are explained in the legend of Teotihuacan, in which the gods decided to sacrifice themselves for the newly created sun. Xolotl withdrew from this sacrifice and wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.

statement.id: Rongga matanya yang kosong dijelaskan dalam legenda Teotihuacan: ketika para dewa memutuskan mengorbankan diri demi matahari yang baru diciptakan, Xolotl mundur dari pengorbanan itu dan menangis begitu lama hingga matanya jatuh dari rongganya.
statement.en: Xolotl's empty eye sockets are explained by the Teotihuacan legend in which the gods decided to sacrifice themselves for the newly created sun; Xolotl withdrew from the sacrifice and wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.

claims.quote: Xolotl transformed himself into a young maize plant with two stalks (xolotl), a doubled maguey plant (mexolotl), and an amphibious animal (axolotl). Xolotl is thus a master transformer. In the end, Ehecatl succeeded in finding and killing Xolotl.

statement.id: Xolotl mengubah dirinya menjadi tanaman jagung muda berbatang dua (xolotl), tanaman maguey ganda (mexolotl), dan hewan amfibi (axolotl), sehingga disebut ahli transformasi. Pada akhirnya Ehecatl berhasil menemukan dan membunuhnya.
statement.en: Xolotl transformed himself into a young two-stalked maize plant, a doubled maguey plant, and an amphibious animal (axolotl), and is thus a master transformer; in the end Ehecatl succeeded in finding and killing him.

claims.quote: As a psychopomp, Xolotl would guide the dead on their journey to Mictlān, the afterlife in myths. His two spirit animal forms are the xoloitzcuintle breed of dog and the aquatic salamander species known as the axolotl.

statement.id: Sebagai psikopomp, Xolotl menuntun orang mati dalam perjalanan ke Mictlān, alam baka dalam mitos. Dua wujud hewan rohnya adalah anjing ras xoloitzcuintle dan salamander air yang disebut axolotl.
statement.en: As a psychopomp, Xolotl would guide the dead on their journey to Mictlān, the afterlife in myths; his two spirit animal forms are the xoloitzcuintle dog breed and the aquatic salamander known as the axolotl.

claims.quote: Xolotl was the dog god of the Mexica people, commonly known as the Aztecs. He is represented in codices, statuary, and other extant examples of Aztec art as a dog or a god with the head of a dog.

statement.id: Xolotl adalah dewa anjing bangsa Mexica, yang lazim dikenal sebagai Aztec. Dalam kodeks, arca, dan karya seni Aztec lain yang masih ada, ia digambarkan sebagai anjing atau dewa berkepala anjing.
statement.en: Xolotl was the dog god of the Mexica people, commonly known as the Aztecs, and is represented in codices, statuary, and other surviving Aztec art as a dog or a god with a dog's head.

claims.quote: While twins were generally seen as a bad omen and viewed with trepidation in the Aztec civilization, Xolotl was the patron god of twins and individuals with physical abnormalities, which were a subject of fascination in Mesoamerican cultures.

statement.id: Meskipun kembar umumnya dianggap pertanda buruk dan dipandang dengan waswas dalam peradaban Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa pelindung kembar dan orang dengan kelainan fisik, yang menjadi bahan ketertarikan dalam budaya Mesoamerika.
statement.en: Although twins were generally seen as a bad omen in Aztec civilization, Xolotl was the patron god of twins and individuals with physical abnormalities, a subject of fascination in Mesoamerican cultures.

claims.quote: Xolotl accompanied Quetzalcoatl on his mission to retrieve bones from the underworld in order to create humanity

statement.id: Xolotl menemani Quetzalcoatl dalam misinya mengambil tulang-tulang dari dunia bawah untuk menciptakan umat manusia.
statement.en: Xolotl accompanied Quetzalcoatl on his mission to retrieve bones from the underworld in order to create humanity.

claims.quote: While most of the gods willingly offer themselves for sacrifice, setting a mythic precedent for the Aztec culture of human sacrifice, Xolotl attempts to escape.

statement.id: Ketika sebagian besar dewa rela mengorbankan diri, Xolotl berusaha melarikan diri.
statement.en: While most of the gods willingly offer themselves for sacrifice, Xolotl attempts to escape.

claims.quote: Xolotl makes his first attempt to escape by turning into a double maize plant. When he is discovered in that guise, he turns into a doubled maguey plant, and when that transformation fails to conceal him, he turns into a salamander still known today by its Nahuatl name, axolotl.

statement.id: Xolotl pertama kali mencoba kabur dengan menjadi tanaman jagung ganda. Ketika ketahuan, ia menjadi tanaman maguey ganda, dan ketika itu pun gagal menyembunyikannya, ia menjadi salamander yang hingga kini dikenal dengan nama Nahuatl axolotl.
statement.en: Xolotl first tries to escape by turning into a double maize plant; when discovered he becomes a doubled maguey plant, and when that fails to conceal him he becomes a salamander still known by its Nahuatl name, axolotl.

claims.quote: Even in the form of an axolotl, Xolotl is ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the rest of the gods

statement.id: Bahkan dalam wujud axolotl, Xolotl akhirnya tertangkap dan dikorbankan bersama dewa-dewa lainnya.
statement.en: Even in the form of an axolotl, Xolotl is ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the rest of the gods.

claims.quote: dogs, perhaps embodying the role of Xolotl, guided their masters into the Underworld after death and were of particular use in crossing bodies of water

statement.id: Anjing, yang mungkin menjelmakan peran Xolotl, menuntun tuannya ke Dunia Bawah setelah mati dan sangat berguna untuk menyeberangi perairan.
statement.en: Dogs, perhaps embodying the role of Xolotl, guided their masters into the Underworld after death and were of particular use in crossing bodies of water.

claims.quote: The word axolotl is a combination of the Nahuatl terms xolotl (explained above) and atl, meaning "water," and so could be roughly translated as "water twin."

statement.id: Kata axolotl adalah gabungan istilah Nahuatl xolotl dan atl yang berarti "air", sehingga kira-kira dapat diterjemahkan sebagai "kembar air".
statement.en: The word axolotl is a combination of the Nahuatl terms xolotl and atl, meaning "water", and so could be roughly translated as "water twin".

claims.quote: An homage to Xolotl also appears in the 2017 Disney film Coco in the form of a dog poignantly named Dante.

statement.id: Penghormatan kepada Xolotl juga muncul dalam film Disney Coco (2017) berupa seekor anjing bernama Dante.
statement.en: An homage to Xolotl also appears in the 2017 Disney film Coco in the form of a dog named Dante.

claims.quote: Xolotl was the patron of the Mesoamerican ballgame. Some scholars argue the ballgame symbolizes the Sun's perilous and uncertain nighttime journey through the underworld. Xolotl is able to help in the Sun's rebirth since he possesses the power to enter and exit the underworld.

statement.id: Xolotl adalah pelindung permainan bola Mesoamerika. Sebagian sarjana berpendapat permainan itu melambangkan perjalanan malam Matahari yang berbahaya melalui dunia bawah; Xolotl dapat membantu kelahiran kembali Matahari karena ia berkuasa keluar-masuk dunia bawah.
statement.en: Xolotl was the patron of the Mesoamerican ballgame, which some scholars say symbolizes the Sun's perilous nighttime journey through the underworld; Xolotl can help the Sun's rebirth because he has the power to enter and exit the underworld.

short_description.id: Yara-ma-yha-who adalah makhluk vampir dalam legenda Aborigin Australia tenggara: lelaki merah kecil berkepala besar yang tinggal di pohon ara dan mengisap darah mangsanya.
short_description.en: The Yara-ma-yha-who is a vampiric creature of south-eastern Australian Aboriginal legend: a little red man with a big head that lives in fig trees and drains the blood of its prey.

long_description.id: Yara-ma-yha-who adalah monster vampir legendaris dalam mitologi Aborigin Australia tenggara; legendanya dituturkan oleh David Unaipon. Ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki merah kecil setinggi sekitar empat kaki dengan kepala, mulut, dan perut sebagai bagian terbesar. Mulutnya tak bergigi dan ia menelan makanan begitu saja, bahkan orang dewasa; kepalanya agak mirip ular, dan ujung jari tangan serta kakinya berbentuk cawan seperti pengisap gurita.
long_description.en: The Yara-ma-yha-who is a legendary vampiric monster of south-eastern Australian Aboriginal mythology; the legend is recounted by David Unaipon. It is described as a little red man about four feet high whose biggest parts are his head, mouth and stomach. The creature is toothless and swallows its food whole, even a grown man; the head recalls a snake's, and the tips of its fingers and toes are cup-shaped, much like octopus suckers.

long_description.id: Makhluk ini tinggal di pohon ara dan sebagian besar di pohon rimbun. Ia tidak berburu: ia menunggu pengelana beristirahat di bawah pohon, menjatuhkan diri, dan menguras darahnya lewat pengisap, tetapi menyisakan cukup agar korban tetap hidup. Setelah itu ia merangkak seperti goanna, menyedot korban ke mulutnya dengan kepala lebih dulu, menari sampai korban masuk ke perutnya, minum banyak air, lalu tidur.
long_description.en: The creature lives in fig trees and mostly in thick, leafy trees. It does not hunt: it waits for a traveller to rest under the tree, drops down and drains the blood with its suckers, but leaves enough to keep the victim alive. It then crawls like a goanna, sucks the victim into its mouth head first, dances until the victim is well inside its stomach, drinks copious water and falls asleep.

long_description.id: Saat bangun ia memuntahkan korbannya, dan orang yang berulang kali tertelan menjadi semakin pendek hingga akhirnya menyerupai Yara-ma-yha-who. Ia hanya aktif pada siang hari dan hanya menyasar mangsa yang hidup, sehingga "pura-pura mati" sampai matahari terbenam disebut sebagai siasat; ia beberapa kali memeriksa mangsa dengan menyodok dan menggelitik, dan korban dapat kabur bila ia tertidur. Bila ia lalai memeriksa, roh pohon ara liar akan membunuhnya.
long_description.en: On waking it vomits up its victim, and a person swallowed repeatedly becomes shorter until he at last resembles a Yara-ma-yha-who. It is only active during the day and targets only living prey, so "playing dead" until sunset is offered as a ploy; it checks its prey several times by poking and tickling, and the victim can run away if it falls asleep. If it fails to check, the spirit of the wild fig tree would kill it.

long_description.id: Cerita tentang makhluk ini dilaporkan dituturkan kepada anak-anak yang nakal. Asalnya diyakini adalah tarsius, dan kemungkinan ceritanya dibawa ke Australia oleh pemukim Melayu; teori lain adalah Thylacoleo carnifex, marsupial karnivora yang menjatuhkan diri ke mangsa dari puncak pohon.
long_description.en: Stories of this creature were reportedly told to misbehaving children. One view traces it to the tarsier, with the story probably carried to Australia by Malay settlers; another proposes Thylacoleo carnifex, a meat-eating marsupial that leapt down on prey from the treetops.

short_description.id: Yazi adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga dalam tradisi Tiongkok, berkepala anjing liar, garang, dan gemar bertarung serta membunuh; rupanya diukir pada senjata.
short_description.en: Yazi is one of the nine sons of the dragon in Chinese tradition, with a wild dog's head, fierce, and fond of fighting and killing; its image is carved on weapons.

long_description.id: Yazi (睚眦; Jepang: Gaisai) adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga dalam tradisi Tiongkok. Ia berkepala anjing liar, berwatak garang, dan gemar bertarung serta membunuh. Karena itu rupanya diukir pada cincin pedang, mulut sarung pedang, serta sabit dan tombak untuk eksekusi, dan banyak dipakai dalam gambar panji militer pada zaman kuno.
long_description.en: Yazi (睚眦; Japanese: Gaisai) is one of the nine sons of the dragon in Chinese tradition. It has a wild dog's head, a fierce temper, and a fondness for fighting and killing. For that reason its image is carved on sword rings, scabbard mouths, and on sickles and halberds for executions, and was much used in military banner designs in antiquity.

long_description.id: Shuolue mencatat bahwa kesembilan putra naga bukan naga dan masing-masing punya kegemaran: Yazi gemar membunuh dan dipakai menghiasi gagang pedang. Teks itu juga menceritakan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi seorang pejabat istana menanyakan nama mereka, daftar itu didapat dari catatan lama yang asalnya tak diketahui, dan penulisnya menilainya tidak berdasar.
long_description.en: The Shuolue records that the dragon's nine sons are not dragons and each has its own fondness: Yazi likes killing and is used to adorn sword hilts. It also tells that in the Hongzhi era a palace official asked for their names, the list was obtained from an old register of unknown origin, and its author judged it unfounded.

long_description.id: Nama 睚眦 sendiri terdiri atas huruf yang berarti tepi atau rongga mata dan "melotot"; artinya adalah menatap marah, dan secara luas "sedikit". Ungkapan 睚眦之怨 dalam Shiji berarti dendam sekecil dipelototi.
long_description.en: The name 睚眦 itself consists of characters meaning the edge or socket of the eye and "to glare"; it means to look in anger and, by extension, "slight". The phrase 睚眦之怨 in the Shiji means a grudge as small as being glared at.

cultural_context.id: Karena wataknya yang garang dan gemar bertarung, wujud Yazi diukir pada cincin dan gagang senjata serta dipakai pada panji perang kuno; Shuolue mencatat bahwa ia dipakai menghiasi gagang pedang.
cultural_context.en: Because of its fierce, combative character, Yazi's image is carved on rings and hilts of weapons and used on ancient military banners; the Shuolue records that it is used to adorn sword hilts.

literal_meaning.id: Gabungan huruf yang berarti sudut atau rongga mata dan "melotot"; arti kiasannya menatap marah atau "sedikit".
literal_meaning.en: A compound of characters meaning the corner or socket of the eye and "to glare"; extended meanings are looking in anger, or "slight".

statement.en: Its image appears on weapons and military banners.

claims.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。

statement.id: Menurut Shuolue, sembilan putra naga bukan naga dan masing-masing punya kegemaran: Yazi gemar membunuh dan dipakai menghiasi gagang pedang; delapan lainnya adalah Qiuniu, Chaofeng, Pulao, Suanni, Baxia, Bi'an, Xixi, dan Chiwen.
statement.en: According to the Shuolue, the nine sons of the dragon are not dragons and each has its own fondness: Yazi likes killing and is used to adorn sword hilts; the others are Qiuniu, Chaofeng, Pulao, Suanni, Baxia, Bi'an, Xixi and Chiwen.

claims.quote: 弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。余憶十一、二時，曾見其說於《對類總龜》中，近因歴考傳記，乃知其說為不經。

statement.id: Menurut Shuolue, pada masa Hongzhi seorang pejabat istana bertanya tentang nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang, yang tidak dapat menyebutkannya; Liu Ji lalu mendapatkannya dari sebuah catatan lama yang asal-usulnya tidak diketahui, dan penulis menilai uraian itu tidak berdasar (bujing).
statement.en: According to the Shuolue, in the Hongzhi era a palace official asked Li Dongyang for the names of the dragon's nine sons; he could not give them all, Liu Ji obtained them from an old register of unknown origin, and the author judged the account unfounded (bujing).

claims.quote: 睚眦，《戰國策》聶政曰：賢者以感忿睚眦之意。注：睚，舉眼也；眦，目匡也。

statement.id: Menurut Shuolue, istilah 睚眦 muncul dalam Zhanguoce dengan kalimat "Orang berbudi tergerak oleh sedikit kemarahan"; catatannya menjelaskan ya sebagai "mengangkat mata" dan zi sebagai "rongga mata".
statement.en: According to the Shuolue, the term 睚眦 appears in the Zhanguoce in a line about the worthy being moved by a slight resentment; the note explains ya as "raising the eyes" and zi as "the eye socket".

claims.quote: 『睚』の字の由来は目のきわ、『眦』は目のわずかに開きはじめた部分、で、どちらも、まなじりや目じりという意味である。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, 睚 berasal dari tepi mata dan 眦 dari bagian mata yang baru mulai terbuka; keduanya berarti sudut mata.
statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, the character 睚 derives from the edge of the eye and 眦 from the part where the eye just begins to open; both mean the corner of the eye.

claims.quote: また、どちらに字にも『にらむ』という意味があり、転じて『睚眦』には『目を怒らして見る。にらむ』という意味があり、転じて『わずか』という意味もある。史記・范雎伝にある『睚眦之怨』（がいさいのうらみ）は、ちょっとにらまれた程度の恨み、という意味である。

statement.id: Kedua huruf itu juga berarti "melotot"; 睚眦 berarti menatap marah dan, secara luas, "sedikit"; 睚眦之怨 dalam Shiji adalah dendam setingkat dipelototi sedikit.
statement.en: Both characters also mean "to glare"; 睚眦 means to look in anger and, by extension, "slight"; the 睚眦之怨 of the Shiji is a grudge as small as being glared at.

short_description.id: Yellow Dragon adalah perwujudan berbentuk hewan dari Kaisar Kuning dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: The Yellow Dragon is the animal-form manifestation of the Yellow Emperor in Chinese mythology.

long_description.id: Yellow Dragon adalah perwujudan berbentuk hewan dari Kaisar Kuning dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Dalam Wuxing, naga ini melambangkan unsur bumi.
long_description.en: The Yellow Dragon is the animal-form manifestation of the Yellow Emperor in Chinese mythology. In Wuxing, this dragon embodies the earth element.

long_description.id: Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun menyebut Naga Kuning sebagai binatang pusat, tempat tanah, kaisar Huangdi, dan roh Zhenxing. Dalam Fengshan shu dari Shiji, naga kuning dan 地螾 dikatakan muncul ketika Huangdi memperoleh kebajikan tanah, sedangkan Naga Biru muncul pada Xia dan burung merah pada Zhou.
long_description.en: The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun names the Yellow Dragon as the beast of the centre, linked with earth, the emperor Huangdi and the spirit Zhenxing. In the Fengshan shu of the Shiji, a yellow dragon and 地螾 are said to have appeared when Huangdi obtained the virtue of earth, while the azure dragon appeared with Xia and a red crow with Zhou.

long_description.id: Shiji juga mencatat bahwa Gongsun Chen menyatakan Han harus menerima kebajikan tanah yang ditandai naga kuning. Tiga tahun kemudian naga kuning muncul di Chengji, dan Kaisar Wen mengangkat Gongsun Chen sebagai cendekiawan serta memerintahkan penyusunan perubahan kalender dan warna busana.
long_description.en: The Shiji also records Gongsun Chen declaring that Han should take the virtue of earth, signalled by the yellow dragon. Three years later a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji, and Emperor Wen appointed Gongsun Chen an erudite and had changes to the calendar and the colour of dress drafted.

title.en: A yellow dragon appears at Chengji

role.id: Pertanda kebajikan tanah
role.en: The sign of the virtue of earth

summary.id: Gongsun Chen mengajukan bahwa Han mewakili kebajikan tanah yang ditandai naga kuning. Tiga tahun kemudian naga kuning muncul di Chengji dan Kaisar Wen memanggilnya serta mengangkatnya sebagai cendekiawan.
summary.en: Gongsun Chen proposed that Han stood for the virtue of earth, whose sign is the yellow dragon. Three years later a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji and Emperor Wen summoned him and appointed him an erudite.

note.id: Naga Kuning adalah perwujudan berbentuk hewan dari Kaisar Kuning; Huainanzi menyebutnya binatang pusat yang kaisarnya Huangdi.
note.en: The Yellow Dragon is the zoomorphic incarnation of the Yellow Emperor; the Huainanzi calls it the beast of the centre, whose emperor is Huangdi.

claims.quote: The Yellow Dragon (simplified Chinese: 黄龙; traditional Chinese: 黃龍; pinyin: Huánglóng; Cantonese Yale: Wong4 Lung4)  is the zoomorphic incarnation of the Yellow Emperor of the center of the universe in Chinese religion and mythology.

statement.id: Yellow Dragon adalah perwujudan berbentuk hewan dari Kaisar Kuning dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
statement.en: The Yellow Dragon is the animal-form manifestation of the Yellow Emperor in Chinese mythology.

claims.quote: The Yellow Dragon is a part of Wuxing and the Four Symbols as the embodiment of the element of earth.

statement.id: Dalam Wuxing, naga ini melambangkan unsur bumi.
statement.en: In Wuxing, this dragon embodies the earth element.

claims.quote: 中央，土也，其帝黃帝，其佐后土，執繩而制四方。其神為鎮星，其獸黃龍，其音宮，其日戊己。

statement.id: Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun (天文訓) menyebut bahwa pusat (中央) adalah tanah (土), kaisarnya Huangdi (黃帝), pembantunya Houtu (后土) yang memegang tali dan mengatur empat penjuru; rohnya adalah Zhenxing (鎮星) dan binatangnya (獸) adalah Naga Kuning (黃龍).
statement.en: The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun (天文訓) says the centre (中央) is earth (土), its emperor is Huangdi (黃帝), its assistant Houtu (后土), who holds the cord and governs the four directions; its spirit is Zhenxing (鎮星) and its beast (獸) is the Yellow Dragon (黃龍).

claims.quote: 或曰：「黃帝得土德，黃龍地螾見。夏得木德，青龍止於郊，草木暢茂。殷得金德，銀自山溢。周得火德，有赤烏之符。

statement.id: Shiji (史記), Fengshan shu, mencatat ucapan seseorang bahwa Huangdi (黃帝) memperoleh kebajikan tanah (土德) dan 黃龍 serta 地螾 muncul; Xia memperoleh kebajikan kayu dan Naga Biru (青龍) singgah di pinggiran kota; Shang memperoleh logam, dan Zhou memperoleh api dengan pertanda burung merah (赤烏).
statement.en: The Shiji (史記), Fengshan shu, records someone saying that Huangdi (黃帝) obtained the virtue of earth (土德) and a 黃龍 (yellow dragon) and 地螾 appeared; Xia obtained wood and an azure dragon (青龍) stopped at the suburb; Shang obtained metal, and Zhou obtained fire with a red crow (赤烏) as its sign.

claims.quote: 魯人公孫臣上書曰：「始秦得水德，今漢受之，推終始傳，則漢當土德，土德之應黃龍見。宜改正朔，易服色，色上黃。」

statement.id: Shiji mencatat bahwa Gongsun Chen (公孫臣) dari Lu mengajukan surat: Qin memperoleh kebajikan air dan Han sepatutnya menerima kebajikan tanah (土德); tanggapan atas kebajikan tanah adalah munculnya naga kuning (黃龍見), sehingga ia mengusulkan agar kalender dan warna busana diubah dan warna kuning dijunjung.
statement.en: The Shiji records that Gongsun Chen (公孫臣) of Lu submitted a memorial: Qin had obtained the virtue of water and Han should take the virtue of earth (土德), whose response is the appearance of a yellow dragon (黃龍見); he proposed changing the calendar and the colour of dress, and honouring yellow.

claims.quote: 後三歲，黃龍見成紀。文帝乃召公孫臣，拜為博士，與諸生草改歷服色事。

statement.id: Shiji mencatat bahwa tiga tahun kemudian naga kuning muncul di Chengji (成紀); Kaisar Wen (文帝) lalu memanggil Gongsun Chen, mengangkatnya sebagai cendekiawan (博士), dan bersama para sarjana menyusun perubahan kalender dan warna busana.
statement.en: The Shiji records that three years later a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji (成紀); Emperor Wen (文帝) then summoned Gongsun Chen, appointed him an erudite (博士), and with the scholars drafted changes to the calendar and the colour of dress.

short_description.id: Abdu-Fisch adalah ikan konsumsi yang belum teridentifikasi dan berperan dalam mitologi Mesir: bersama Ant-Fisch ia mengawal bahtera matahari.
short_description.en: The Abdu-Fisch is an unidentified food fish with a special role in Egyptian mythology: with the Ant-Fisch it escorted the solar barque.

long_description.id: Abdu-Fisch (juga disebut Abdju-Fisch atau Abydos-Fisch) adalah ikan konsumsi yang belum teridentifikasi dan memiliki peran khusus dalam mitologi Mesir. Bersama Ant-Fisch ia kadang mengawal bahtera matahari dan menjaga air. Tugasnya adalah memberi tahu kedatangan musuh berwujud ular, dan dewa matahari sendiri kadang disebut "Abdu-Fisch agung".
long_description.en: The Abdu-Fisch (also called Abdju-Fisch or Abydos-Fisch) is an unidentified food fish with a special role in Egyptian mythology. Together with the Ant-Fisch it at times escorted the solar barque and watched over the water. Its task was to announce the approach of the serpent enemy, and the sun god himself was sometimes called the "great Abdu-Fisch".

long_description.id: Dalam catatan kaki pada terjemahan Budge, ikan Abtu dan ikan Ant digambarkan berenang di depan Bahtera Ra dan memandunya. Ikan ini mungkin juga bermakna dalam kepercayaan tentang kematian Mesir: karena kemiripan nama dengan Abydos, Abdu kadang dikaitkan dengan Osiris, dan di beberapa makam Teban zaman Ramesside mumi yang seperti Osiris dibungkus sebagai Abdu-Fisch. Ikan itu juga dipakai sebagai lambang kehidupan yang misterius, seperti katak.
long_description.en: A footnote to Budge's translation describes the Abtu and Ant fishes as swimming before the Boat of Ra and guiding it. The fish may also have had special meaning in Egyptian beliefs about death: because of the similarity of its name to Abydos, the Abdu was occasionally linked with Osiris, and in some Theban tombs of the Ramesside period the Osiris-like mummy is wrapped as an Abdu-Fisch. The fish was also used as a mysterious symbol of life, like the frog.

long_description.id: Pada masa Helenistik, ikan Oxyrhynchos digambarkan di atas mumi orang mati. Menurut Hans Bonnet, Abdu-Fisch mungkin sudah digambarkan serupa pada masa lebih awal dan lama-kelamaan berbentuk Oxyrhynchos. Orang mati mungkin ingin menyatakan harapan melihat matahari, sedangkan Wilhelm Spiegelberg menyebut ikan-ikan itu hanya wujud jiwa.
long_description.en: In the Hellenistic period Oxyrhynchos fish were depicted above the mummy of the dead. According to Hans Bonnet the Abdu-Fisch may have been depicted similarly earlier and over time took the Oxyrhynchos form. The dead person probably wished to express the hope of seeing the sun, whereas Wilhelm Spiegelberg held that the fish were only a form of the soul.

short_description.id: Al Ana adalah iblis perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Turkik yang tinggal di semak tepi air dan menculik bayi yang baru lahir untuk ditukar dengan anaknya sendiri.
short_description.en: Al Ana is a female demon of Turkic folklore who lives in thickets by the water and steals newborns to swap them with her own children.

long_description.id: Al Ana adalah roh atau iblis perempuan pembawa maut dalam cerita rakyat Turkik yang konon tinggal di semak dekat sungai dan danau. Menurut sebagian cerita lisan, ia perempuan tua buruk rupa yang berbulu, berambut panjang lurus, bertopi merah berhias ranting pakis, dengan payudara begitu besar hingga dipakai mencuci pakaiannya.
long_description.en: Al Ana is a deadly female spirit or demon of Turkic folklore said to live in thickets by rivers and lakes. Some oral tales make her an ugly, hairy old woman with long straight hair and a red hat with a fern twig, whose breasts are so huge she washes her clothes with them.

long_description.id: Ia konon menculik bayi yang baru lahir dan menggantinya dengan anaknya sendiri, anak tukaran yang dapat dikenali dari tubuhnya yang tak proporsional dan wataknya yang jahat. Menurut sumber lain, banyak ritual kelahiran berkaitan dengan sosok Hal, meski menyebut namanya sering ditabukan.
long_description.en: She was said to steal newborns and replace them with her own children, changelings recognisable by their disproportionate bodies and wickedness. According to another source, many birth rituals concern the figure of Hal, though saying its name is often taboo.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel ensiklopedis, anak tukaran Al Ana digambarkan berperut sangat besar, berkepala luar biasa kecil atau besar, berpunuk, berlengan dan berkaki kurus, bertubuh berbulu, dan berkuku panjang. Untuk melindungi anak, seorang ibu harus mengikatkan pita merah di tangannya, memakaikan topi merah, dan melindungi wajahnya dari cahaya bulan. Yang dianggap paling berisiko menjadi iblis semacam ini setelah mati ialah bidan, perawan tua, ibu yang tidak menikah, perempuan hamil yang meninggal sebelum melahirkan, dan anak terlantar yang lahir di luar nikah.
long_description.en: According to the encyclopedic article, Al Ana's changeling is pictured with an enormous belly, a head that is oddly small or oversized, a hump on its back, spindly limbs, hairy skin and long claws. To guard a child, a mother had to knot a red ribbon on its hand, cover its head with a red hat and keep the moon's glow off its face. Those thought most at risk of becoming such demons after death were midwives, old maids, unmarried mothers, pregnant women who die before childbirth, and abandoned children born out of wedlock.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah artikel jurnal, nama Al, alkarısı, dan alanası dicatat untuk makhluk yang disebut Albastı, yang dikenal di hampir seluruh dunia Turki. Ia dipercaya paling memusuhi perempuan yang baru melahirkan dan bayi, mencabut hati atau paru-paru mereka lalu membuangnya ke air atau memakannya. Karena ia takut pada warna merah, kepala perempuan yang baru melahirkan ditutup kerudung merah dan kerahnya dipasangi pita merah.
long_description.en: In a journal article, the names Al, alkarısı and alanası are recorded for the being called Albastı, found in almost the whole Turkic world. It is believed to be most hostile to women in childbed and to babies, tearing out their liver or lungs and throwing them into water or eating them. Because it fears the color red, the head of a woman in childbed is covered with a red kerchief and a red ribbon is attached to her collar.

short_description.id: Animikii adalah burung guntur mitologis raksasa dalam tradisi suku Ojibwe dan beberapa suku lain. Guntur disebabkan oleh kepakan sayapnya, dan ia diperlakukan dengan hormat.
short_description.en: The Animikii is a giant mythological thunderbird in the traditions of the Ojibwe and several other tribes. Thunder is caused by the beating of its wings, and it is treated with reverence.

long_description.id: Animikii (juga Binesi, Wapoothi, Waputhi) adalah burung guntur mitologis raksasa yang dikenal di suku-suku utara dan barat, yaitu Ojibwe, Algonquin, Ottawa, dan Shawnee. Mereka menimbulkan guntur dengan memukulkan sayap raksasa mereka.
long_description.en: The Animikii (also Binesi, Wapoothi, Waputhi) is a giant mythological thunderbird known among the northern and western tribes, namely the Ojibwe, Algonquin, Ottawa and Shawnee. They cause thunder by beating their enormous wings.

long_description.id: Walaupun sangat kuat, burung guntur jarang mengganggu manusia, dan orang Ojibwe memperlakukannya dengan hormat. Animikii secara harfiah berarti "pembuat guntur", sedangkan Binesi berarti "burung besar". Salah satu kisah Ojibwe yang terkait menceritakan Nanabozho yang mencuri api dari Burung Guntur untuk dibagikan kepada manusia.
long_description.en: Although very powerful, thunderbirds rarely bother humans, and the Ojibwe treat them with reverence. Animikii literally means "thunderer" and Binesi means "the great bird". One related Ojibwe story tells of Nanabozho stealing fire from Thunderbird to share with the people.

short_description.id: Anka adalah burung raksasa dalam legenda Iran dan dongeng Turki, Kazakh, dan Altay yang tinggal di Gunung Kaf dan lahir kembali dari abunya.
short_description.en: Anka is a giant bird of Iranian legend and of Turkic, Kazakh and Altay tales that lives on Mount Kaf and is reborn from its ashes.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda Iran, Anka adalah burung raksasa yang berkelana di Gunung Qaf; Wikipedia bahasa Kazakh menyebut jenis keduanya sebagai Samuryq, dan dalam dongeng Kazakh dan Altay burung dongeng seperti qartlan, kokzhore, dan qumai disetarakan dengannya.
long_description.en: According to Iranian legends, Anka is a giant bird that roams Mount Qaf; Kazakh Wikipedia gives its second kind as Samuryq, and in Kazakh and Altay tales fairy-tale birds such as qartlan, kokzhore and qumai are equated with it.

long_description.id: Kamus Mitologi Turki karya Karakurt mendefinisikan Anka sebagai burung raksasa merah dari bahasa Persia yang tinggal di Gunung Kaf, kadang digambarkan berkepala anjing dan bercakar harimau, dan lahir kembali dari abunya. Ia menyebut dalam kepercayaan Turki lama Anka dikenal sebagai burung Toğrul dan Kongrul, yang melambangkan keabadian dan kebangkitan.
long_description.en: Karakurt's Dictionary of Turkic Mythology defines Anka as a giant red bird from Persian that lives on Mount Kaf, sometimes depicted with a dog's head and tiger claws, and is reborn from its ashes. It says that in old Turkic belief the Anka is known as the Toğrul and Kongrul birds, which symbolise immortality and resurrection.

long_description.id: Karakurt menambahkan bahwa ciri Anka dalam budaya Persia dipindahkan seluruhnya kepada burung Kongrul, dan bahwa kepercayaan akan kematian harian dan kelahiran kembali dari abu, yang meluas karena pengaruh Persia dan Timur Tengah, sebenarnya melambangkan Matahari.
long_description.en: Karakurt adds that the features of the Persian Anka were transferred entirely to the Kongrul bird, and that the belief in a daily death and rebirth from ashes, widespread through Persian and Middle Eastern influence, in fact symbolises the Sun.

cultural_context.id: Sosok Anka diyakini sepadan dengan burung Samuryq dalam cerita dongeng.
cultural_context.en: Anka is regarded as equivalent to the Samuryq bird in fairy tales.

claims.quote: Аңқа  — иран аңыздары бойынша Қап тауында жүретін алып құс. Оның екінші түрі — самұрық. Қазақ пен алтай халықтары ертегілерінде оған теңдестіріліп айтылатын ертегі құстар: қартлан, көкжөре, құмай.
Anka (Farsça, Anka): Kızıl renkli devasa kuş. Kaf dağında yaşar. Köpek başlı, kaplan pençeli olarak tasvir edildiği de olur. Kendi küllerinden yeniden doğar.

statement.id: Kamus Mitologi Turki karya Karakurt mendefinisikan Anka (dari bahasa Persia) sebagai burung raksasa berwarna merah, yang tinggal di Gunung Kaf, kadang digambarkan berkepala anjing dan bercakar harimau, dan lahir kembali dari abunya sendiri.
statement.en: Karakurt's Dictionary of Turkic Mythology defines Anka (Persian) as a giant red-coloured bird that lives on Mount Kaf, sometimes depicted with a dog's head and tiger claws, and is reborn from its own ashes.

claims.quote: Anka Kuşu (eski Türk inancında Toğrul ve Kongrul Kuşları) burada yaşar ve yuvasını bu dağın zirvesine kurmuştur.

statement.id: Dalam entri Gunung Kaf, burung Anka (dalam kepercayaan Turki lama adalah burung Toğrul dan Kongrul) disebut hidup di sana dan membuat sarangnya di puncak gunung itu.
statement.en: In the Mount Kaf entry, the Anka bird (in old Turkic belief the Toğrul and Kongrul birds) is said to live there and to have built its nest on the summit.

claims.quote: Doğaüstü nitelikleri olan kızıl renkli devasa kuş. Ölümsüzlüğü ve yeniden dirilişi simgeler. Diğer pek çok Dünyâ uluslarının mitolojilerinde de değişik adlarla mevcuttur.

statement.id: Entri Toğrul, yang diberi judul 'Anka Kuşu', menyebutnya burung raksasa merah berkemampuan gaib yang melambangkan keabadian dan kebangkitan, dan ada dalam mitologi banyak bangsa dengan nama berbeda.
statement.en: The Toğrul entry, headed 'Anka Kuşu', calls it a giant red bird with supernatural qualities that symbolises immortality and resurrection and exists under different names in the mythologies of many peoples.

claims.quote: Kongrul Kuşu diğer ulusların söylencelerindeki Anka Kuşu ile pek çok benzer özellikler taşır, hattâ zaman zaman geçişim yoluyla o mitolojilerden alıntılar yapılarak içselleştirilmiştir. Örneğin Fars kültüründeki Anka Kuşu'nun özellikleri bütünüyle bu kuşa aktarılmıştır.

statement.id: Karakurt menyatakan burung Kongrul memiliki banyak ciri yang mirip burung Anka dalam legenda bangsa lain, dan ciri Anka dalam budaya Persia dipindahkan seluruhnya kepada burung ini.
statement.en: Karakurt states that the Kongrul bird shares many features with the Anka bird of other peoples' legends, and the features of the Anka in Persian culture were transferred entirely to this bird.

claims.quote: Fars ve hatta genel olarak Ortadoğu kültürünün etkisiyle her gün yanarak öldüğü ve kendi küllerinden yeniden doğduğu inanışı yaygındır. Bu ise aslında Güneş'i sembolize eder. Kaf Dağı'nda yaşar ve bu dağı korur.

statement.id: Karakurt menulis bahwa, karena pengaruh budaya Persia dan Timur Tengah, kepercayaan bahwa burung itu mati terbakar setiap hari dan lahir kembali dari abunya tersebar luas, dan hal ini sebenarnya melambangkan Matahari; ia tinggal di Gunung Kaf dan menjaganya.
statement.en: Karakurt writes that, through Persian and Middle Eastern influence, the belief that it burns to death each day and is reborn from its ashes is widespread, and this in fact symbolises the Sun; it lives on Mount Kaf and guards it.

note.en: Karakurt gives Anka Kuşu as another name for the Toğrul and Kongrul birds in old Turkic belief.

short_description.id: Anki-Kiele adalah roh laut dalam mitologi Chukchi dan Eskimo, yang tinggal di dasar laut dan dapat memberi tangkapan baik bila didatangi jiwa seorang dukun.
short_description.en: Anki-Kiele is the sea spirit of Chukchi and Eskimo mythology, living on the sea bed and able to grant a good catch when a shaman's soul visits him.

long_description.id: Anki-Kiele, juga Anky-Kele atau Anka-Kal, adalah roh laut dalam mitologi Chukchi dan Eskimo. Ia termasuk roh kele, golongan yang mencakup kekuatan yang memusuhi manusia maupun roh penguasa. Menurut gambar seniman Chukchi Onno, ia tinggal di dasar laut dan berkepala besar berbulu dengan mulut lebar bergigi, sedangkan gambar dari koleksi V. G. Bogoraz menggambarkannya bertubuh ikan. Ia bisa memberi tangkapan ikan atau buruan laut yang baik, yang diupayakan dengan mengirim jiwa seorang dukun kepadanya.
long_description.en: Anki-Kiele, also Anky-Kele or Anka-Kal, is the sea spirit of Chukchi and Eskimo mythology. He belongs to the kele spirits, a category embracing both forces hostile to people and master spirits. According to a drawing by the Chukchi artist Onno he lives on the sea bed and has a huge shaggy head with a large toothy mouth, while a drawing from V. G. Bogoraz's collection gives him a fish body. He could grant a good catch of fish or sea game, sought by sending a shaman's soul to him.

long_description.id: Etnografer Bogoras, dalam karyanya tentang suku Chukchi, mencatat gambar seorang "roh" yang hidup di laut (a'nqa-kal): ia bertubuh ikan dengan kepala berbulu yang sangat besar. Sketsa lain menampilkan roh laut besar yang berambut sangat panjang di kepala dan pantatnya. Bentuk a'nqa-kal ini sejalan dengan nama Anka-Kal yang disebut dalam entri sebelumnya sebagai salah satu ejaan nama Anki-Kiele.
long_description.en: In his work on the Chukchi, the ethnographer Bogoras records a drawing of a "spirit" living in the sea (a'nqa-kal), with the body of a fish and a very large shaggy head. Another sketch shows a large sea-spirit with very long hair on both his head and his buttocks. The form a'nqa-kal is in line with the name Anka-Kal that the earlier entry gives as one spelling of the name Anki-Kiele.
