short_description.id: Ao Guang adalah Raja Naga Laut Timur dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Ao Guang is the East Sea Dragon King in Chinese folklore.

long_description.id: Ao Guang adalah Raja Naga Laut Timur dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok. Tokoh ini muncul dalam Fengshen Yanyi dan Journey to the West.
long_description.en: Ao Guang is the East Sea Dragon King in Chinese folklore. This figure appears in Fengshen Yanyi and Journey to the West.

long_description.id: Dalam penafsiran Buddhis, Ao Guang disebut Raja Naga Sagara, yang menurut Avataṃsaka Sūtra berkedudukan sebagai nāgaraja pengatur hujan bagi dunia. Sebuah kisah menyebut keempat raja naga dihukum Kaisar Giok karena menurunkan hujan tanpa izin pada masa kekeringan. Dalam kisah Avalokiteśvara, Ao Guang memohon bantuan ketika putra ketiganya tertangkap nelayan.
long_description.en: In Buddhist interpretation, Ao Guang is called the Dragon King Sagara, who in the Avataṃsaka Sūtra holds the rank of nāgaraja governing the rain that the world receives. One tale says the four Dragon Kings were punished by the Jade Emperor for bringing rain without permission in times of drought. In the Avalokiteśvara tale, Ao Guang seeks help when his third son is captured by a fisherman.

long_description.id: Menurut Fengshen Yanyi, Ao Guang membawa kekacauan dengan menciptakan kekeringan, badai, dan bencana lain. Setelah Nezha membunuh Li Gen dan Ao Bing, Ao Guang menemui ayah Nezha; kemudian ia terpaksa mengubah diri menjadi ular kecil dan ikut Nezha kembali ke Old Pond Pass.
long_description.en: According to Fengshen Yanyi, Ao Guang brought chaos by creating droughts, storms and other disasters. After Nezha killed Li Gen and Ao Bing, Ao Guang went to Nezha's father; he was later forced to turn himself into a small snake and go with Nezha back to the Old Pond Pass.

long_description.id: Dalam teks Journey to the West bab 3, Ao Guang menyambut Sun Wukong bersama putra naga, cucu naga, prajurit udang, dan jenderal kepiting. Dalam memorialnya kepada Kaisar Giok, ia menyatakan telah mempersembahkan tongkat besi ajaib, topi emas, baju zirah rantai, dan sepatu penjejak awan. Sun Wukong juga disebut memperoleh Ruyi Jingu Bang dari Ao Guang, dan hujan deras Ao Guang tidak dapat menghentikan api Red Boy, yang tidak dapat dipadamkan air biasa.
long_description.en: In the text of Journey to the West chapter 3, Ao Guang welcomes Sun Wukong together with his dragon sons, dragon grandsons, shrimp soldiers and crab generals. In his memorial to the Jade Emperor he states that he presented the magic iron staff, the golden cap, the chain-mail armor and the cloud-treading boots. Sun Wukong is also said to have obtained the Ruyi Jingu Bang from Ao Guang, and Ao Guang's torrential rain could not put out Red Boy's fire, which ordinary water cannot stop.

description.en: According to the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, he is the nāgaraja that presides over the world's supply of rain.

short_description.id: Ao Run adalah Raja Naga Laut Barat dan anggota Raja Naga Empat Laut.
short_description.en: Ao Run is the West Sea Dragon King and a member of the Dragon Kings of the Four Seas.

long_description.id: Ao Run, juga disebut Ao Ji, adalah Raja Naga Laut Barat dan salah satu dari Raja Naga Empat Laut dalam agama Tiongkok dan mitologi Korea. Kuil Empat Raja Naga dibangun di berbagai tempat untuk memuja mereka.
long_description.en: Ao Run, also known as Ao Ji, rules the West Sea as its Dragon King and is counted among the four Dragon Kings of the Seas in Chinese religion and Korean mythology. Temples to the Four Dragon Kings are built in various places for worship.

long_description.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan Danau Qinghai, dan saudara-saudaranya adalah Ao Guang, Ao Qin, dan Ao Shun. Dalam novel Xiyouji, seorang Raja Naga menyebut ketiga adiknya, dan Ao Run menasihati agar tidak melawan seseorang melainkan menyiapkan satu set zirah untuknya; bab lain menyebut putranya, yang membakar mutiara dan dituduh ayahnya durhaka.
long_description.en: He is linked to Qinghai Lake, and his brothers are Ao Guang, Ao Qin, and Ao Shun. In the novel Xiyouji, a Dragon King names his three younger brothers and Ao Run advises against fighting a man and instead putting together a suit of armour for him; another chapter mentions his son, who burned a pearl and was accused of impiety by his father.

long_description.id: Dalam mitos Jakjaegeon, bagian dari mitos pendirian dinasti Goryeo, Raja Naga Laut Barat muncul dalam mimpi dan meminta Jakjaegeon membunuh gwishin tua dengan busur; sebagai balas budi ia memberikan putrinya.
long_description.en: In the Jakjaegeon myth, part of the founding myth of the Goryeo Dynasty, the Dragon King of the West Sea appears in a dream and asks Jakjaegeon to kill an old gwishin with a bow; in gratitude he gives him his daughter.

short_description.id: Bai Ze adalah makhluk gaib legenda Tiongkok yang mengetahui persoalan roh dan dewa.
short_description.en: Bai Ze is a Chinese legendary being knowledgeable about spirits and deities.

long_description.id: Bai Ze (白澤, Báizé) adalah makhluk mitos dari legenda Tiongkok kuno. Pada masa Tang, makhluk ini diperkenalkan ke Jepang dengan nama yang tetap. Menurut catatan Tiongkok, ada Bái Zé Tú, "diagram Baize": Bai Ze, makhluk ilahi, mengetahui segala urusan hantu dan dewa di dunia; atas permintaan Kaisar Kuning, ia menggambar semua hantu dan roh yang diketahuinya dan menambahkan keterangan.
long_description.en: Bai Ze (白澤, Báizé) is a creature of ancient Chinese legend that was carried to Japan in the Tang era under the same name. Chinese records mention the Bái Zé Tú, the "diagram of Baize": the divine being Bai Ze knew everything about the ghosts and gods of the world and, at the Yellow Emperor's request, drew every ghost and spirit it knew in pictures and annotated them.

long_description.id: Yunji Qiqian menceritakan bahwa Kaisar Kuning mendapatkan Bai Ze di pantai timur setelah mendaki Gunung Huan; Bai Ze dapat berbicara dan menyebutkan 11.520 jenis hantu dan roh yang kemudian digambar. Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Tiongkok kekaisaran, Bai Ze melambangkan kemampuan mengusir hantu dan menangkal roh jahat. Li Shizhen dalam Bencao Gangmu mencatat bahwa Baize Tu termasuk kitab yang memuat jelmaan roh dengan cukup lengkap, dan mengutipnya tentang roh pohon Penghou.
long_description.en: The Yunji Qiqian relates that the Yellow Emperor obtained Bai Ze on the eastern coast after climbing Mount Huan; Bai Ze could speak and named 11,520 kinds of ghosts and spirits, which were then drawn. In the folk beliefs of imperial China Bai Ze stood for the power to drive out ghosts and ward off evil spirits. In the Bencao Gangmu, Li Shizhen notes that the Baize Tu is among the books that describe spirit-monsters in detail, and quotes it on the tree spirit Penghou.

long_description.id: Dalam buku Ming SanCai TuHui, Bai Ze digambarkan berkepala naga berambut hijau dengan tanduk di puncak dan dapat terbang, sedangkan History of Yuan mencatatnya berkepala harimau, berambut surai merah, bertubuh naga, dan bertanduk. Satu-satunya bukti tentang Bái Zé Tú di Tiongkok adalah naskah Dunhuang yang tidak lengkap, yang tidak memuat gambar Bai Ze. Di Jepang ia disebut Hakutaku; dalam Tiandi ruixiang zhi ia bertubuh sapi dan berkepala manusia berjenggot, dan pada wabah kolera Edo 1858 orang diinstruksikan menaruh gambarnya di bantal.
long_description.en: The SanCai TuHui, a Ming Dynasty work, describes Bai Ze with a dragon head covered in green hair, a horn on top and the power of flight, while the History of Yuan records a tiger's head, red mane, dragon body and a horn. The only surviving evidence of the Bái Zé Tú in China is an incomplete Dunhuang manuscript, which has no drawings of Bai Ze. In Japan it is called Hakutaku; the Tiandi ruixiang zhi gives it a cow's body and a bearded human head, and during the 1858 Edo cholera outbreak people were told to put its picture on their pillows.

description.en: According to the Yunji Qiqian, Bai Ze could speak and understood the nature of all things, including ghosts and spirits.

description.en: In Japan Bai Ze is called Hakutaku; in the Tiandi ruixiang zhi it has a cow's body and a bearded human head, and the painting by Fukuhara Gogaku shows three faces with three eyes each and a pair of horns.

claims.quote: Bai Ze (simplified Chinese: 白泽; traditional Chinese: 白澤; pinyin: Báizé) is a mythical creature from ancient Chinese legends. During the Tang Dynasty, it was introduced to Japan with its name unchanged.

statement.id: Bai Ze adalah makhluk gaib legenda Tiongkok yang mengetahui persoalan roh dan dewa.
statement.en: Bai Ze is a Chinese legendary being knowledgeable about spirits and deities.

claims.quote: Entrusted by the Yellow Emperor, Bai Ze drew all the ghosts and spirits he knew into pictures and added annotations, which is the origin of the Bái Zé Tú.

statement.id: Kisah menghubungkannya dengan gambar roh yang dibuat atas permintaan Kaisar Kuning.
statement.en: A tale links it to pictures of spirits commissioned by the Yellow Emperor.

claims.quote: In the Ming Dynasty book SanCai TuHui (三才圖會), Bai Ze’s appearance is described as having green hair on a loong head, with a horn growing on the top and the ability to fly. In the History of Yuan (元史), it is recorded as having the head of a tiger, red mane, loong’s body, and a horn. Bai Ze’s image in China combines features of both the loong and tiger.

statement.id: SanCai TuHui menggambarkan kepala naga dengan rambut hijau, tanduk, dan kemampuan terbang.
statement.en: The SanCai TuHui describes a dragon head with green hair, a horn, and flight.

claims.quote: In the Ming Dynasty book SanCai TuHui (三才圖會), Bai Ze’s appearance is described as having green hair on a loong head, with a horn growing on the top and the ability to fly. In the History of Yuan (元史), it is recorded as having the head of a tiger, red mane, loong’s body, and a horn. Bai Ze’s image in China combines features of both the loong and tiger.

statement.id: History of Yuan memberikan varian kepala harimau, surai merah, dan tubuh naga.
statement.en: The History of Yuan gives a variant with a tiger head, red mane, and dragon body.

claims.quote: The only existing evidence related to Bái Zé Tú in China is an incomplete Dunhuang manuscript. It is said to have been copied in the 9th or 10th century and titled “Baize-jing guai—tu” ‘Bai Ze Diagrams of Spectral Prodigies’ (白澤精惟圖), now kept at the National Library of France (P2682). This Dunhuang manuscript does not contain any drawings of Bai Ze.

statement.id: Naskah Dunhuang yang tersisa membahas diagram roh dan tidak memuat gambar Bai Ze sendiri.
statement.en: The surviving Dunhuang manuscript concerns spirit diagrams and contains no drawing of Bai Ze itself.

claims.quote: In Japan, Bai Ze is also called Hakutaku. The oldest known depiction of Hakutaku appears in the Tiandi ruixiang zhi ‘Treatise on the Auspicious Signs of Heaven and Earth’ (天地瑞祥志), a work originated in China. This work is listed in late 9th-century Japanese bibliographies, while it is unknown in Chinese ones.

statement.id: Di Jepang, makhluk ini dikenal sebagai Hakutaku.
statement.en: In Japan, this being is known as Hakutaku.

claims.quote: 帝巡狩東至海，登桓山，於海濱得白澤神獸，能言，達於萬物之情。因問天下鬼神之事，自古精氣為物，游魂為變者，凡萬一千五百二十種，白澤言之，帝令以圖寫之以示天下，帝乃作《祝邪之文》以祝之。

statement.id: Menurut Yunji Qiqian, Kaisar Kuning dalam perjalanan keliling ke timur sampai laut, mendaki Gunung Huan, dan di pantai mendapatkan binatang gaib Bai Ze yang dapat berbicara dan memahami keadaan segala hal. Ia bertanya tentang urusan hantu dan roh; Bai Ze menyebutkan 11.520 jenis, kaisar memerintahkan agar digambar untuk ditunjukkan ke seluruh dunia, dan menyusun naskah penangkal kejahatan.
statement.en: According to the Yunji Qiqian, the Yellow Emperor, touring east to the sea and climbing Mount Huan, obtained the divine beast Bai Ze on the coast; it could speak and understood the nature of all things. He asked about ghosts and spirits; Bai Ze named 11,520 kinds, the emperor had them drawn to show the world, and composed a text for warding off evil.

claims.quote: 精怪之屬甚伙，皆為人害。惟《白澤圖》、《玄中記》、《抱朴子》、《酉陽雜俎》諸書載之頗悉，起居者亦不可不知。

short_description.id: Bal-bal adalah monster mayat hidup dalam mitologi Filipina yang mencuri jenazah dari rumah duka atau kubur untuk dimakan, lalu meninggalkan batang pisang di peti mati.
short_description.en: The bal-bal is an undead monster of Philippine mythology that steals corpses from wakes or graves to eat, then leaves a banana trunk in the coffin.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, bal-bal adalah monster mayat hidup yang mencuri jenazah, baik di rumah duka maupun di kubur, lalu memakannya. Ia berpenciuman tajam terhadap mayat manusia, dan cakar serta giginya cukup tajam untuk merobek pakaian jenazah. Karena hanya memakan mayat, napasnya berbau busuk. Menurut kisah-kisah, setelah makan ia meninggalkan batang pohon pisang di peti mati untuk menciptakan ilusi jenazah yang dicuri.
long_description.en: In Philippine mythology the bal-bal is an undead monster that steals corpses, whether at a wake or in a grave, and eats them. It has a keen sense of smell for dead human bodies, and its claws and teeth are sharp enough to rip the clothing of the dead. Because it eats nothing but corpses, its breath is foul. According to the stories, after feeding it leaves the trunk of a banana tree in the coffin to create an illusion of the stolen body.

long_description.id: Dalam catatan lama tentang orang Tagbanua, balbal ditakuti selama jenazah menunggu dikubur. Dean C. Worcester menulis bahwa makhluk ini, yang menurut orang Tagbanua berasal dari negeri Moro, meluncur di udara seperti bajing terbang, berwujud mirip manusia, merobek atap rumbia dengan kuku melengkung, dan "menjilat" jenazah dengan lidah panjang. Satu buku lama menyebutnya vampir yang tinggal di Mindanao, berwujud manusia bersayap dengan cakar besar. Maximo Ramos mengembalikan kisah bal-bal kepada orang Tagbanua di Palawan tengah dan utara.
long_description.en: In older accounts of the Tagbanua people the balbal is dreaded while a corpse awaits burial. Dean C. Worcester wrote that this creature, which the Tagbanua say comes from the Moro country, glides through the air like a flying squirrel, is manlike, rips open thatch roofs with curved nails and "licks up" the bodies with a long tongue. One older book calls it a vampire living on Mindanao, in the form of a man with wings and great claws. Maximo Ramos traced the tales of the bal-bal to the Tagbanua of central and northern Palawan.

long_description.id: Sebuah catatan dari Duero menyebut balbal dapat menjelma burung, anjing, kucing hitam, babi raksasa, atau bahkan rumah. Kisah-kisah modern menyebutnya berjalan sebagai manusia biasa sampai tersiram cahaya bulan purnama, lalu berubah menjadi pengumpul tulang yang cacat, dan sebagian menyatakan bahwa orang yang menyebut namanya akan dicari dan dimakan.
long_description.en: A record from Duero says a balbal can appear as a bird, a dog, a black cat, an enormous pig or even a house. Modern tales say it walks as a regular human until drenched by the light of the full moon, then turns into a disfigured bone collector, and some hold that anyone who utters its name will be sought out and devoured.

long_description.id: Bal-bal dikaitkan dengan aswang, amalanhig, dan busaw, yang semuanya pemakan daging, dan digolongkan sebagai salah satu makhluk paling menakutkan di Filipina. Ciri fisiknya diadopsi ke banyak kisah makhluk pemakan daging lain, dan seorang penulis menyebutnya mungkin pencuri jenazah yang paling mengerikan di Filipina.
long_description.en: The bal-bal is associated with the aswang, amalanhig and busaw, all flesh-eaters, and is classed among the most fearful creatures in the Philippines. Its physical attributes were adopted into many other tales of flesh-eating creatures, and one writer calls it perhaps the most gruesome of the Philippine corpse thieves.

short_description.id: Beaman Monster adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Missouri yang dinamai menurut kota Beaman [beaman-monster-c01]. Wujudnya beragam, dari keturunan gorila sirkus hingga makhluk berbentuk serigala atau koyote [beaman-monster-c02].
short_description.en: The Beaman Monster is a Missouri folklore creature named after the town of Beaman [beaman-monster-c01]. Its form varies, from the offspring of a circus gorilla to a wolf- or coyote-shaped beast [beaman-monster-c02].

long_description.id: Beaman Monster adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Missouri yang dinamai menurut kota Beaman [beaman-monster-c01]. Kisahnya beragam: keturunan gorila sirkus setinggi 12 kaki, atau makhluk berbentuk serigala atau koyote [beaman-monster-c02]. Ceritanya diwariskan turun-temurun di daerah Sedalia [beaman-monster-c03].
long_description.en: The Beaman Monster is a Missouri folklore creature named after the town of Beaman [beaman-monster-c01]. Accounts vary: offspring of a 12-foot circus gorilla, or a wolf- or coyote-shaped beast [beaman-monster-c02]. Its tales have passed down for generations around Sedalia [beaman-monster-c03].

long_description.id: Menurut sebuah laporan berita, kisahnya sudah dituturkan lebih dari seabad, meski bukti keberadaannya tidak ada [beaman-monster-c04]. Dalam satu penuturan, sebuah kereta mengalami kecelakaan pada 1904 dan semua hewan tertangkap lagi kecuali seekor gorila setinggi 12 kaki, yang konon menurunkan sang monster [beaman-monster-c05]. Kebanyakan orang menganggapnya sejenis Sasquatch, sedangkan seorang pria Sedalia mengingatnya berbentuk serigala atau koyote [beaman-monster-c06].
long_description.en: A news report says its tales go back more than a century, though there is no evidence the creature exists [beaman-monster-c04]. In one telling, a train crashed in 1904 and every animal was recaptured but one 12-foot-tall gorilla, said to be the monster's parent [beaman-monster-c05]. Most people think of it as a type of Sasquatch, while one Sedalia man remembers it as wolf- or coyote-shaped [beaman-monster-c06].

long_description.id: Seorang warga mengatakan, menurut ayahnya, anak-anak lelaki yang kelewatan akan "dipanggilkan" Beaman Monster [beaman-monster-c07]. Pada akhir 1950-an, orang-orang bersenapan berburu menyisir sebuah ladang jagung untuk memburunya [beaman-monster-c08], dan sebagian orang melaporkan jejak kaki besar sebagai bukti [beaman-monster-c09]. Ada pula yang mengingatnya sebagai lelucon 1950-an dengan rambu konstruksi berlampu berkedip [beaman-monster-c10], dan sebagian menduga asalnya lebih berkaitan dengan moonshine [beaman-monster-c11].
long_description.en: One resident said that, according to his father, boys who got out of hand would have the Beaman Monster called out on them [beaman-monster-c07]. In the late 1950s, people with shotguns walked through a cornfield hunting it [beaman-monster-c08], and some people report large footprints as evidence [beaman-monster-c09]. Others recall it as a 1950s prank involving a construction sign with flashing lights [beaman-monster-c10], and some speculate its origins have more to do with moonshine [beaman-monster-c11].

short_description.id: Bulgasari adalah makhluk legenda Korea pemakan logam.
short_description.en: Bulgasari is a metal-eating legendary creature of Korean folklore.

long_description.id: Bulgasari adalah makhluk legenda Korea pemakan logam. Tubuhnya memadukan ciri beruang, gajah, badak, harimau, dan banteng.
long_description.en: Bulgasari is a metal-eating legendary creature of Korean folklore. Its body combines features of a bear, elephant, rhinoceros, tiger, and bull.

long_description.id: Salah satu pembacaan namanya berarti sesuatu yang mustahil dibunuh. Sebagian kisah menampilkan kehancuran yang dilakukannya sebagai hukuman atas kejahatan. Sebuah versi menyebut figur dari beras yang tumbuh setelah diberi jarum.
long_description.en: One reading of its name denotes something impossible to kill. Some tales portray its destruction as punishment of evil. One version describes a rice figure growing after being fed needles.

long_description.id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Budaya Korea, kisah ini menceritakan seorang biksu yang membuat binatang aneh dari butir nasi; binatang itu memakan logam apa saja dan tubuhnya terus membesar. Busur dan pedang tidak mempan, dan ketika negara mencoba membakarnya, ia tidak mati dan berkeliling sebagai bola api sehingga banyak tempat terbakar. Karena itu ia disebut 불가살이, yang tidak dapat dibunuh.
long_description.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, the tale tells of a monk who makes a strange beast out of grains of rice; the beast eats any metal and its body keeps growing. Bows and swords were useless, and when the state tried to burn it, it did not die and roamed about as a ball of fire so that many places burned. Hence it was called 불가살이, the one that cannot be killed.

long_description.id: Versi-versi kisah berbeda tentang cara ia lenyap, antara lain dengan jimat, tongkat biksu yang membuatnya memuntahkan logam, atau pembakaran ekornya. Sebagian mitos menyebutnya masih hidup, dan sebagian lain menyebutnya dikalahkan para biksu. Ensiklopedia itu juga mencatat hubungan nama 화가살 dengan pemikiran Lima Unsur, yang menyatakan api mengalahkan logam.
long_description.en: Versions of the tale differ on how it vanishes, including a talisman, a monk's staff that makes it spew out the metal, or burning its tail. Some myths say it still lives, and others say it was defeated by monks. The encyclopedia also links the name 화가살 to Five Phases thought, in which fire overcomes metal.

long_description.id: Dalam adat rakyat, bulgasari dianggap pencegah bencana dan kebakaran, dan digambar pada paravan atau cerobong. Menurut legenda, ia dipahat sebagai penjaga pada dinding, cerobong, pagar, dan tiang karena dapat mengalahkan mimpi buruk dan roh jahat serta mencegah wabah dan bencana alam. Ensiklopedia Budaya Korea memahami bulgasari dan 맥 (貘) di Tiongkok, yang sama-sama memakan logam, sebagai berkembang secara terpisah.
long_description.en: In folk custom the bulgasari is regarded as preventing disaster and fire and is drawn on folding screens or chimneys. According to legend, carvings of it stand guard on walls, chimneys, railings and pillars because it can defeat nightmares and evil spirits and prevent plagues and natural disasters. The Encyclopedia of Korean Culture understands the bulgasari and the Chinese 맥 (貘), which both eat metal, as having developed separately.

description.id: Menurut legenda, ia adalah binatang haus darah yang bertambah besar saat memakan logam; dalam kisah ensiklopedia, ia memakan semua logam yang ditemukannya.
description.en: According to legend it is a bloodthirsty beast that grows in size as it eats metal; in the encyclopedia's tale it eats all the metal it finds.

description.en: It cannot be killed by any means yet can be killed by fire, hence also called 화가살; in another account it is finally burned away.

The creature is a composite creature with the body of a bear, the trunk of an elephant, the eyes of a rhinoceros, the claws of a tiger, and the tail of a bull.

claims.quote: In Korean, the name "Bulgasari" translates to "something impossible to kill"; however, swapping the first Chinese character for a Korean character of the same pronunciation and choosing the corresponding Chinese character to that Korean character results in a spelling that translates to "something that can be killed by fire".

statement.id: Salah satu pembacaan namanya berarti sesuatu yang mustahil dibunuh.
statement.en: One reading of its name denotes something impossible to kill.

claims.quote: The Bulgasari is often portrayed as heroic in mythology because it causes destruction to punish evil in society, although negative folktales about it also exist.

statement.id: Sebagian kisah menampilkan kehancuran yang dilakukannya sebagai hukuman atas kejahatan.
statement.en: Some tales portray its destruction as punishment of evil.

claims.quote: According to legend, the Bulgasari is a bloodthirsty beast that grows in size as it eats metal. Myth states that it was created by a Buddhist monk who was fleeing persecution because Buddhism was illegal in Goryeo-era Korea. He created a small figure out of rice grains, which he fed needles, and it began to grow.

statement.id: Sebuah versi menyebut figur dari beras yang tumbuh setelah diberi jarum.
statement.en: One version describes a rice figure growing after being fed needles.

claims.quote: ‘불가살(不可殺)이’는 한자의 의미처럼, 아무리 죽이려고 해도 죽일 수 없는 존재를 의미한다.

statement.id: Ensiklopedia Budaya Korea menjelaskan bahwa 불가살이 berarti sosok yang tidak dapat dibunuh betapa pun orang berusaha membunuhnya.
statement.en: The Encyclopedia of Korean Culture explains that 불가살이 means, as its Chinese characters indicate, a being that cannot be killed no matter how one tries.

claims.quote: 어떻게 해도 죽일 수 없지만 불로는 죽일 수 있다고 해서 ‘화가살(火可殺)’이라고도 한다. 이는 오행(五行) 사상에 근거한 것으로, 오행에 따르면 불은 쇠와 상극이며 쇠를 이긴다.

statement.id: Karena tidak dapat dibunuh dengan cara apa pun tetapi dapat dibunuh dengan api, makhluk ini juga disebut 화가살 (火可殺); hal ini didasarkan pada pemikiran Lima Unsur, yang menyatakan api berlawanan dengan logam dan mengalahkannya.
statement.en: Because it cannot be killed by any means yet can be killed by fire, it is also called 화가살 (火可殺); this rests on Five Phases thought, according to which fire opposes metal and overcomes it.

claims.quote: 우리나라에 전해지는 ‘불가살이’와 중국의 ‘맥’은 쇠를 먹는다는 공통점이 있지만, 별개로 발전한 것으로 파악된다.

statement.id: Bulgasari di Korea dan 맥 (貘) di Tiongkok sama-sama memakan logam, tetapi dipahami berkembang secara terpisah.
statement.en: The Korean bulgasari and the Chinese 맥 (貘) share the feature of eating metal but are understood to have developed separately.

claims.quote: 어떠한 방법으로도 죽일 수 없어서 ‘불가살’이라고 불렸다. ... 소금과 주문, 회초리와 불 등이 동원되는데, 결국 ‘불가살이’는 불에 태워져 없어진다는 내용이다.

statement.id: Karena tidak dapat dibunuh dengan cara apa pun, makhluk ini disebut 불가살; untuk melenyapkannya dikerahkan garam, mantra, cambuk, dan api, dan akhirnya ia dibakar hingga lenyap.
statement.en: Because it could not be killed by any means it was called 불가살; salt, incantations, switches and fire were used to remove it, and in the end it is burned away.

claims.quote: 중은 벽장에 숨어 밥을 먹으며 밥풀로 괴상한 짐승을 만들었다. ... 쇠붙이를 닥치는 대로 먹어치워서 몸집이 점점 거대해졌고

statement.id: Dalam kisah ini, seorang biksu yang bersembunyi di lemari dinding membuat binatang aneh dari butir nasi; binatang itu memakan logam apa saja sehingga tubuhnya terus membesar.
statement.en: In this tale a monk hiding in a wall cupboard makes a strange beast out of grains of rice; the beast eats any metal it finds and its body grows ever larger.

claims.quote: 나라에서 괴물을 죽이려고 활과 칼을 써봐도 소용이 없자 불을 질러 없애려고 했다. 그러나 괴물은 죽지 않고 불덩이가 된 몸으로 돌아다녀 곳곳이 불바다가 되었다.

statement.id: Ketika busur dan pedang yang dipakai negara untuk membunuh makhluk itu tidak berguna, mereka mencoba membakarnya; tetapi ia tidak mati dan berkeliling dengan tubuh yang menjadi bola api sehingga banyak tempat menjadi lautan api.
statement.en: When the bows and swords the state used to kill the creature proved useless, they tried to burn it away; but it did not die and roamed about with its body turned into a ball of fire, so that places everywhere became seas of flame.

claims.quote: 『대동운부군옥(大東韻府群玉)』에 따르면 불가사리는 상상의 짐승으로 곰같이 생겼으며 악몽과 요사한 기운을 물리친다고 했다고 했다. 불가사리는 설화에서는 환상 속 괴물로 형상화 되지만, 민속에서는 재앙과 화재를 예방해 주는 존재로 여겨 병풍이나 굴뚝에 그려넣기도 한다.

statement.id: Menurut 『대동운부군옥』, bulgasari adalah binatang khayalan yang berwujud seperti beruang dan menangkal mimpi buruk serta energi jahat; dalam adat rakyat ia dianggap pencegah bencana dan kebakaran sehingga digambar pada paravan atau cerobong.
statement.en: According to the 『대동운부군옥』, the bulgasari is an imaginary beast shaped like a bear that wards off nightmares and evil energy; in folk custom it is regarded as preventing disaster and fire and is drawn on folding screens or chimneys.

claims.quote: 소멸되는 방법은 중이 부적을 불가사리에 붙이는 경우, 중이 지팡이를 휘두르자 그 동안 먹었던 쇠붙이를 모두 쏟아내고 사라지는 경우 ... 불가사리 꼬리에 불을 붙여 까맣게 태우는 경우, 무당의 참언(讖言)으로 고려가 멸망하면서 극성을 부르던 불가사리도 자동 소멸되는 경우 등이 있다.

statement.id: Versi-versi kisah berbeda tentang cara ia lenyap: biksu menempelkan jimat, biksu mengayunkan tongkat sehingga ia memuntahkan semua logam yang dimakannya dan menghilang, ekornya dibakar hingga hangus, dan seterusnya.
statement.en: Versions of the tale differ on how it vanishes: a monk sticks a talisman on it, a monk swings a staff so that it spews out all the metal it ate and disappears, its tail is set on fire and burned black, and so on.

short_description.id: Caboclo de Agua adalah makhluk mitologi timur laut Brasil yang tinggal di dasar Sungai São Francisco dan menakut-nakuti nelayan [caboclo-de-agua-c01].
short_description.en: The Caboclo de Agua is a mythological being of northeastern Brazil that lives at the bottom of the São Francisco River and frightens fishermen [caboclo-de-agua-c01].

long_description.id: Caboclo de Agua konon tinggal dalam gua emas di dasar Sungai São Francisco dan menakut-nakuti nelayan serta pelaut [caboclo-de-agua-c01]. Ia digambarkan sebagai raksasa berotot berkulit perunggu dengan satu mata besar [caboclo-de-agua-c02], berjantung tak tembus peluru [caboclo-de-agua-c03], dan dapat menyamar sebagai kuda [caboclo-de-agua-c04].
long_description.en: The Caboclo de Agua is said to live in a golden grotto at the bottom of the São Francisco River, frightening fishermen and boatmen [caboclo-de-agua-c01]. It is described as a muscular giant with bronze skin and a single huge eye [caboclo-de-agua-c02], with a bullet-proof heart [caboclo-de-agua-c03], able to appear as a horse [caboclo-de-agua-c04].

long_description.id: Ia mengosongkan jaring nelayan yang tidak disukainya dan memenuhi jaring yang disukainya [caboclo-de-agua-c05], serta sering membalikkan perahu [caboclo-de-agua-c06]. Nelayan memasang figur "carrancas" di haluan [caboclo-de-agua-c07] dan melukis bintang di dasar perahu untuk mengusirnya [caboclo-de-agua-c08].
long_description.en: It empties the nets of fishermen it dislikes and fills those of men it likes [caboclo-de-agua-c05], and often capsizes boats [caboclo-de-agua-c06]. Fishermen mount "carrancas" figures on their bows [caboclo-de-agua-c07] and paint a star on the boat bottom to ward it off [caboclo-de-agua-c08].

long_description.id: Dalam kamus folklornya, Cascudo menyebut Caboclo-d'Água sebagai makhluk fantastis di Sungai São Francisco yang berkuasa atas air dan ikan [caboclo-de-agua-c09]. Ia berpihak pada sahabat-sahabatnya tetapi memburu nelayan yang tidak disukainya dengan membalikkan kano [caboclo-de-agua-c10]. Nama lainnya Bicho-d'água, Rolão, Romão, dan Romãozinho [caboclo-de-agua-c11].
long_description.en: In his folklore dictionary, Cascudo describes the Caboclo-d'Água as a fantastic creature of the São Francisco River with dominion over the waters and the fish [caboclo-de-agua-c09]. It favours its friends but pursues the fishermen it dislikes, overturning canoes [caboclo-de-agua-c10]. Its other names include Bicho-d'água, Rolão, Romão and Romãozinho [caboclo-de-agua-c11].

long_description.id: Cascudo mengutip dua gambaran yang berbeda: tubuh monster berproporsi raksasa luar biasa [caboclo-de-agua-c12], dan tipe yang paling sering dilaporkan, yaitu pendek, tebal, berotot, berwarna tembaga, gesit, dan pemarah [caboclo-de-agua-c13]. Para pengayuh perahu di São Francisco mempersembahkan tembakau kepadanya [caboclo-de-agua-c14], dan penyeberang yang menancapkan pisau di dasar kano konon tidak diserangnya [caboclo-de-agua-c15].
long_description.en: Cascudo quotes two different descriptions: a monstrous body with the proportions of an enormous giant [caboclo-de-agua-c12], and the type most often reported, short, thick, muscular, copper-coloured, quick and ill-tempered [caboclo-de-agua-c13]. The boatmen of the São Francisco offer it tobacco [caboclo-de-agua-c14], and a traveller who sticks a knife in the bottom of his canoe is said not to be attacked [caboclo-de-agua-c15].

cultural_context.id: Cascudo mencatat bahwa para pengayuh perahu di São Francisco mempersembahkan tembakau kepada Caboclo-d'água.
cultural_context.en: Cascudo records that the boatmen of the São Francisco offer tobacco to the Caboclo-d'água.

short_description.id: Cavalo do pensamento adalah kuda mitos dalam legenda Portugal.
short_description.en: The cavalo do pensamento is a mythical horse of Portuguese legend.

long_description.id: Cavalo do pensamento, "kuda pikiran", adalah makhluk mitos dalam legenda Portugal. Keterangan lain tentang wujud dan kisahnya belum dapat dikutip dari sumber.
long_description.en: The cavalo do pensamento, "horse of thought", is a mythical being of Portuguese legend. No further sourced detail about its form or tales is available yet.

long_description.id: Seorang pengumpul cerita rakyat mencatat sebuah kisah di mana seorang pemuda diminta memilih antara kuda angin dan kuda pikiran. Ia memilih kuda pikiran, seekor kuda yang menyemburkan api dari mata dan mulutnya; begitu ia menungganginya ia melesat sedemikian cepat sehingga tak tahu ke mana ia pergi, dan dalam sekejap sudah berada di depan pintu rumahnya. Setelah ia mengucapkan kata-kata yang dipesankan, kuda itu meledak dengan dentuman dan lenyap seperti sesuatu yang jahat.
long_description.en: A collector of folk tales recorded a tale in which a youth is asked to choose between the horse of the wind and the horse of thought. He chooses the horse of thought, a horse that spits fire from its eyes and mouth; once he mounts it he is carried so fast that he does not know where he is going, and in the blink of an eye he is at his front door. After he speaks the words he had been told, the horse bursts with a bang and vanishes like an evil thing.

long_description.id: Dalam tulisannya yang lain, "A Mourama", penulis yang sama menceritakan bahwa lelaki dari Donim dibawa ke mourama dan, untuk kembali ke bumi, harus datang dengan kuda pikiran yang ia pilih daripada kuda angin. Ia juga memasukkan "cavalo do pensamento" ke dalam daftar 25 tempat di concelho yang penting bagi para mouro.
long_description.en: In another text, "A Mourama", the same author relates that the man of Donim was taken to the mourama and, to return to earth, had to come on the horse of thought, which he preferred to the horse of the wind. He also includes "cavalo do pensamento" in his list of 25 places in the concelho that are important for the mouros.

short_description.id: Chashkel adalah raksasa pemakan manusia dalam mitologi Selknam yang ditakuti karena kekuatannya, dan dikalahkan oleh Kwányip ketika menyelamatkan keponakannya.
short_description.en: Chashkel is a man-eating giant in Selknam mythology, feared for his power, who was defeated by Kwányip while the latter saved his nephews.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Selknam, Chashkel (juga ditulis Cháskilts, Čáskels, atau Cháskels) adalah raksasa antropofag, yaitu pemakan manusia. Ia ditakuti orang-orang sezamannya karena kekuatannya yang sangat besar dan merupakan lawan utama Kwányip.
long_description.en: In Selknam mythology, Chashkel (also written Cháskilts, Čáskels or Cháskels) was an anthropophagous giant, that is, a man-eater. He was feared by his contemporaries because of his enormous power and was Kwányip's arch-rival.

long_description.id: Chashkel tinggal di tepi sungai Mac Lelan (atau McCLellan), yang bermuara di Bahía Inútil di provinsi Tierra del Fuego, Chile. Konon di sana kini masih ditemukan banyak tulang berserakan milik orang-orang yang dimakan raksasa itu. Ia memiliki anjing-anjing yang dilatih khusus untuk memburu dan membunuh manusia; anjing itu memakan mangsanya atau membawanya ke gubuk sang raksasa.
long_description.en: Chashkel lived on the banks of the Mac Lelan (or McCLellan) river, which flows into Bahía Inútil in Tierra del Fuego province, Chile. It is said that many scattered bones of the people the giant devoured can still be found there. He had dogs specially trained to hunt and kill people; the dogs devoured their prey or brought it to the giant's hut.

long_description.id: Menurut mitos, Chashkel menculik saudara-saudara Sasán, keponakan Kwányip, dan menahan mereka sebagai budak di gubuknya, memaksa mereka membuang dan membersihkan isi perut mayat manusia. Kwányip datang menyelamatkan mereka; para saudara Sasán kabur ke tempat persembunyian, lalu Kwányip memasang jebakan, menjebak Chashkel di rawa lumpur dan membekukannya, kemudian mematahkan tulang punggungnya. Saudara-saudara Sasán lalu keluar dan menembak mata sang raksasa dengan ketapel; dari mata yang hancur itu lahirlah lalat.
long_description.en: According to the myth, Chashkel kidnapped the Sasán brothers, Kwányip's nephews, and kept them as slaves in his hut, forcing them to gut and clean the entrails of human corpses. Kwányip came to rescue them; the Sasán brothers fled to a hiding place, and Kwányip set a trap, catching Chashkel in a mire and freezing him, then breaking his spine. The Sasán brothers then came out and shot the giant's eyes with slings; flies were born from the destroyed eyes.

note.id: Keponakan Kwányip yang diculik dan dijadikan budak oleh Chashkel, lalu menembak matanya dengan ketapel.
note.en: Kwányip's nephews, kidnapped and enslaved by Chashkel, who later shot his eyes with slings.

learning_questions.id: Bagaimana pertarungan antara Kwányip dan Chashkel mencerminkan kemenangan keteraturan moral atas bahaya alam liar?
learning_questions.en: How does the duel between Kwányip and Chashkel reflect moral order subduing wild wilderness perils?

sources.title: Antepasados míticos (minisitio Rito, chamanismo y música Selknam)
sources.publisher: Memoria Chilena, Biblioteca Nacional de Chile

claims.quote: En la mitología selknam, Chashkel, Cháskilts o Čáskels era un gigante antropófago.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Selknam, Chashkel adalah raksasa pemakan manusia.
statement.en: In Selknam mythology, Chashkel was an anthropophagous giant.

claims.quote: Adversario por excelencia de Kwányip, fue derrotado por este al salvar a sus sobrinos, los hermanos Sasán.

statement.id: Menjadi musuh bebuyutan pahlawan Kwányip dan dikalahkan saat menyelamatkan keponakannya.
statement.en: The arch-rival of Kwányip, he was defeated while saving the hero's nephews.

claims.quote: Chashkel vivía a orillas del río Mac Lelan

statement.id: Chashkel berdiam di sepanjang tepi sungai Mac Lelan di Tierra del Fuego.
statement.en: Chashkel inhabited the banks along the Mac Lelan river.

claims.quote: Era temido por sus contemporáneos debido a su enorme poder.

statement.id: Ia ditakuti orang-orang sezamannya karena kekuatannya yang sangat besar.
statement.en: He was feared by his contemporaries because of his enormous power.

claims.quote: Chashkel vivía a orillas del río Mac Lelan (o McCLellan), que desemboca en la bahía Inútil, provincia de Tierra del Fuego (chile), Región de Magallanes y de la Antártica Chilena, en la zona de Villa Cameron, capital de la comuna de Timaukel.

statement.id: Chashkel tinggal di tepi sungai Mac Lelan (atau McCLellan), yang bermuara di Bahía Inútil, provinsi Tierra del Fuego (Chile), Región de Magallanes dan Antártica Chilena, di kawasan Villa Cameron, ibu kota komune Timaukel.
statement.en: Chashkel lived on the banks of the Mac Lelan (or McCLellan) river, which flows into Bahía Inútil in Tierra del Fuego province (Chile), Magallanes and Chilean Antarctica Region, in the area of Villa Cameron, capital of the Timaukel commune.

claims.quote: Se dice que actualmente en aquel lugar es posible encontrar muchos huesos dispersos, de las personas que el gigante devoraba.

statement.id: Konon di tempat itu kini masih dapat ditemukan banyak tulang berserakan milik orang-orang yang dimakan sang raksasa.
statement.en: It is said that many scattered bones of the people the giant devoured can still be found at that place today.

claims.quote: Chashkel tenía varios perros a los cuales adiestraba especialmente para perseguir y matar personas. Estos perros devoraban a sus presas, o bien las llevaban a la choza del gigante.

statement.id: Chashkel memiliki beberapa anjing yang ia latih khusus untuk memburu dan membunuh manusia; anjing-anjing itu memakan mangsanya atau membawanya ke gubuk sang raksasa.
statement.en: Chashkel had several dogs he specially trained to hunt and kill people; the dogs devoured their prey or brought it to the giant's hut.

claims.quote: Según cuenta el mito, Chashkel secuestró a los hermanos Sasán, sobrinos de Kwányip, y los mantuvo como esclavos en su choza, donde les obligaba a destripar y limpiar las entrañas de los cadáveres humanos que llevaba.
claims.locator: Mitología – Combate contra Kwányip y muerte

statement.id: Menurut mitos, Chashkel menculik saudara-saudara Sasán, keponakan Kwányip, dan menahan mereka sebagai budak di gubuknya, memaksa mereka membuang dan membersihkan isi perut mayat manusia yang ia bawa.
statement.en: According to the myth, Chashkel kidnapped the Sasán brothers, Kwányip's nephews, and kept them as slaves in his hut, where he forced them to gut and clean the entrails of the human corpses he brought.

claims.quote: Kwányip le tendió una trampa, atrapándolo en un lodazal y posteriormente congelándolo. Chashkel quedó fatigado al escapar de la trampa y luego Kwányip aprovechó la oportunidad para fracturar su columna.
claims.locator: Mitología – Combate contra Kwányip y muerte

statement.id: Kwányip memasang jebakan, menjebak Chashkel di rawa lumpur lalu membekukannya; setelah Chashkel kelelahan lolos dari jebakan, Kwányip memanfaatkan kesempatan itu untuk mematahkan tulang punggungnya.
statement.en: Kwányip set a trap, catching Chashkel in a mire and then freezing him; once Chashkel was exhausted from escaping the trap, Kwányip took the chance to break his spine.

claims.quote: Los hermanos Sasán salieron de su escondite y, cada uno con una honda, dispararon a los ojos del gigante, de los cuales, una vez destruidos, nacieron moscas.
claims.locator: Mitología – Combate contra Kwányip y muerte

statement.id: Saudara-saudara Sasán keluar dari persembunyian dan, masing-masing dengan ketapel, menembak mata sang raksasa; setelah mata itu hancur, lahirlah lalat-lalat darinya.
statement.en: The Sasán brothers came out of hiding and, each with a sling, shot at the giant's eyes; once destroyed, flies were born from them.

claims.quote: Kwanyip, otro chamán muy poderoso que distribuyó el día y la noche, mató al gigante Cháskels y trajo la muerte al mundo

statement.id: Memoria Chilena menyebut Kwanyip, dukun yang sangat kuat yang membagi siang dan malam, membunuh raksasa Cháskels dan membawa kematian ke dunia.
statement.en: Memoria Chilena states that Kwanyip, another very powerful shaman who distributed day and night, killed the giant Cháskels and brought death to the world.

short_description.id: Chullachaki adalah makhluk hutan Amazon di Peru dan Brasil yang digambarkan pendek, berkaki tidak sama, dan dapat menyamar sebagai orang tercinta untuk menyesatkan orang ke dalam rimba. Sebagian sumber juga menyebutnya pelindung hutan.
short_description.en: The Chullachaki is a forest creature of the Peruvian and Brazilian Amazon, described as short with mismatched feet, who can disguise himself as a loved one to lead people deep into the jungle. Some sources also call him a protector of the forest.

long_description.id: Chullachaki adalah makhluk hutan mitos dari hutan Amazon Peru dan Brasil. Ia umumnya digambarkan pendek dan buruk rupa, dengan satu kaki lebih pendek dan satu kaki lebih besar, menghadap ke belakang, atau berbentuk kuku hewan. Dalam versi Iquitos, salah satu kakinya berbentuk gada dan ia berusaha menyembunyikannya.
long_description.en: The Chullachaki is a forest creature from the myths of the Peruvian and Brazilian Amazon. He is usually pictured as a short, ugly figure with legs of unequal length and a foot that is oversized, turned backward, or shaped like a hoof. In the Iquitos version one of his feet is club-shaped and he tries to hide it.

long_description.id: Menurut cerita, ia membujuk korbannya mengikutinya jauh ke dalam hutan dengan menyerupai anggota keluarga, orang tercinta yang lama tak terlihat, atau hewan buruan. Kepada anak-anak, ia sering tampil sebagai anak lain atau teman bermain. Kaki yang tidak sama menjadi satu-satunya penanda yang membedakannya.
long_description.en: According to the stories, he persuades his victims to follow him deep into the jungle by taking the form of a family member, a loved one long unseen, or a prey animal. To children he often appears as another child or a playmate. His mismatched feet are the only thing that sets him apart.

long_description.id: Sebagian orang menyebut ia muncul sebagai lelaki sangat pendek berpakaian compang-camping yang mengajak berkelahi; yang menolak tantangannya dikutuk tidak bisa berburu dan bernasib sial. Di sisi lain, sebuah artikel jurnal menggambarkannya sebagai pelindung hutan dan hewannya yang tidak jahat dan hanya mencelakai orang yang mengganggu alam. Seorang biolog menyatakan komunitas Amazon percaya ia adalah ibu hutan yang patut dihormati dan, sampai batas tertentu, ditakuti.
long_description.en: Some say he appears as a very short man in rags who invites a fight; those who decline are cursed with the inability to hunt and with foul luck. A journal article, on the other hand, portrays him as a protector of the forest and its animals who is not evil and harms only those who disturb nature. A biologist states that Amazonian communities believe he is the mother of the forest, to be respected and, to a degree, feared.

cultural_context.id: Seorang biolog menyatakan bahwa selama bertahun-tahun komunitas Amazon menyampaikan pesan pelestarian hutan melalui keberadaan makhluk ini.
cultural_context.en: A biologist states that for many years Amazonian communities have conveyed forest conservation messages through the existence of this creature.

description.id: Menyamar sebagai kerabat, orang tercinta, hewan buruan, atau anak lain bagi seorang anak.
description.en: Disguises himself as relatives, loved ones, prey animals, or as another child to a child.

description.id: Kakinya yang tidak sama membongkar penyamarannya; menurut legenda Iquitos, jika terbongkar ia kabur ke hutan.
description.en: His mismatched feet betray his disguise; in the Iquitos legend, if discovered he flees into the jungle.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa makhluk penyamar di hutan sering punya kaki yang aneh?
learning_questions.en: Why do forest disguisers often have odd feet?

statement.en: The Chullachaki is a mythical forest creature of the Peruvian and Brazilian Amazon.

claims.quote: He is generally described as short and ugly, with one leg shorter than the other and one foot either larger than the other, pointed backward or in the form of a hoof.

statement.en: According to this journal article, the Chullachaqui is a mythological being of the forest, a short duende (goblin-like being) with animal feet, and a protector of the forest.

claims.quote: En ambos existe la figura de un ser místico protector de la selva y sus animales, esto ser, según la creencia popular puede sufrir metamorfosis y asumir la forma física de una persona próxima a quien él desea engañar.

statement.id: Artikel jurnal itu membandingkan mitos curupira dan chullachaqui: keduanya makhluk mistis pelindung hutan dan hewannya yang menurut kepercayaan populer dapat berubah wujud menjadi orang dekat yang hendak ditipunya.
statement.en: The journal article compares the curupira and chullachaqui myths: both are mystical protectors of the forest and its animals which, by popular belief, can transform into a person close to whomever they wish to deceive.

claims.quote: Pero ellos no son malos, solo causan daños a quien intenta molestar la naturaleza.

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.
The accepted research entry is embedded unchanged; the image may only depict what its claims document.
Creatures an earlier batch left out keep that reason as catatan_sebelumnya; the generator may decline them with status tidak-digambar.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
